items.title: Ensure explicit zero-data-retention (ZDR) across LLM serving
items.body:
## Goal

Make the public LLM serving path explicitly **zero-data-retention (ZDR) by configuration**, rather than relying on defaults that may change across vLLM / KServe / Envoy upgrades.

Current public request path is approximately:

`Cloudflare edge -> cloudflared -> llm-public-gw (Envoy Gateway) -> llm-ai-gw (Envoy AI Gateway) -> InferencePool / EPP -> vLLM`

Relevant files include:

- `kserve/llmisvc-*.yaml`
- `kserve/llmisvc-runtime-configs-s2z.yaml`
- `kserve/envoy-gateway.yaml`
- `kserve/envoy-ai-gateway.yaml`
- `apps/llm-public-gateway.yaml`
- `apps/llm-ai-gateway.yaml`
- `apps/llm-routes.yaml`
- `apps/cloudflared.yaml`
- `infra/prometheus.yaml`
- `apps/llm-grafana-dashboards/llm-serving-dashboard.yaml`

## Working definition of ZDR

Use a **customer-content ZDR** definition, anchored to OpenAI's published behavior:

> prompts and model responses are not retained after a request is processed, and customer content is excluded from retained abuse-monitoring/application-state storage.

OpenAI also distinguishes **customer content** from system/usage metadata that does not contain customer content. That distinction is useful for our Prometheus policy: aggregate operational telemetry can remain while prompt/completion content cannot.

References:

- https://openai.com/index/our-commitment-to-zero-data-retention/
- https://platform.openai.com/docs/models/default-usage-policies-by-endpoint

For this cluster, define **customer content** broadly as:

- prompt/message text
- completion/output text
- input/output token IDs
- image/audio/file contents
- tool arguments/results supplied by a user
- raw request/response bodies
- API keys / Authorization values
- user-provided headers
- any directly identifying per-request value derived from those fields

Allowed retained telemetry may include aggregate/system metadata such as:

- model/pool name
- replica/readiness state
- aggregate request counts
- status/error class
- queue depth
- token-count counters/histograms
- request/response size histograms
- latency/TTFT/TPOT histograms
- GPU/KV-cache utilization
- infrastructure metrics

Those values must **not** carry prompt text, completion text, token IDs, API keys, client identifiers, request IDs, trace IDs, or arbitrary request headers as labels/exemplars.

## Current Prometheus assessment

**Current Prometheus usage is compatible with the above ZDR definition.** `infra/prometheus.yaml` intentionally retains metrics for 15 days, but the LLM metrics being scraped are operational/aggregate telemetry rather than customer content.

Examples currently in use:

- vLLM: running/waiting requests, prompt/generation token totals, latency histograms, success counts, cache utilization
- EPP: ready pods, average queue size, KV-cache utilization, saturation, scheduler/token-count distributions
- Envoy: cluster/upstream request counters used for scale-from-zero
- HAMi / node-exporter / cAdvisor: infrastructure utilization

vLLM's Prometheus metrics are aggregate gauges/counters/histograms and normally carry `model_name` rather than request content:

- https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/design/metrics/

llm-d / Inference Extension metrics similarly expose pool/model names, queue depths, token-count/request-size distributions, and scheduler latency rather than payloads:

- https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d-benchmark/blob/main/docs/metrics_collection.md

**Keep the 15d Prometheus retention.** ZDR does not need to mean "no telemetry"; it means no retained customer content. However, add an explicit guardrail/test that rejects unsafe labels/exemplars if future versions introduce them.

## Required changes

### 1. vLLM: explicitly disable request and output logging

Apply to **every public KServe/vLLM model**, not only Qwen38.

Where supported by the deployed vLLM version, explicitly set:

```yaml
- "--no-enable-log-requests"
- "--disable-uvicorn-access-log"
```

Also explicitly ensure output logging is off where that flag exists:

```yaml
- "--no-enable-log-outputs"
```

Do not rely on current defaults. vLLM documents `--enable-log-requests` as capable of logging request IDs/parameters at INFO and prompt text/token IDs at DEBUG; output logging can emit generated text.

References:

- https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/cli/serve/
- https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/api/vllm/entrypoints/openai/cli_args/

Also require:

- no `--otlp-traces-endpoint`
- no `--collect-detailed-traces`
- `VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL` must not be DEBUG/TRACE in production
- no custom middleware/image wrapper that dumps bodies/headers

### 2. vLLM: explicitly disable cross-request prefix/KV reuse

For the strongest interpretation of "nothing derived from a prompt survives completion", explicitly set:

```yaml
- "--no-enable-prefix-caching"
```

Current vLLM versions default prefix caching on and intentionally retain processed-request KV-cache blocks for reuse by later matching prefixes. Even though this is volatile GPU memory rather than a log/database, it is post-request retention of prompt-derived state and creates a multi-tenant timing/privacy surface.

References:

- https://docs.vllm.ai/en/stable/design/prefix_caching/
- https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/cli/serve/

Do not treat `cache_salt` as equivalent to ZDR: salting isolates reuse but still retains prompt-derived KV state.

Note: ordinary active-request KV cache is necessary transient processing. This requirement is about retaining/reusing completed-request prefixes, not forensic zeroization of freed GPU RAM.

### 3. KServe runtime preset: ZDR-safe defaults

Update `kserve/llmisvc-runtime-configs-s2z.yaml` so the generic vLLM template is ZDR-safe by default.

The current version-detection logic chooses either blanket `--disable-uvicorn-access-log` or, for newer vLLM, only:

```text
--disable-access-log-for-endpoints /health,/metrics,/ping
```

For ZDR, do **not** leave inference endpoint access logging enabled. Prefer blanket:

```text
--disable-uvicorn-access-log
```

and explicitly add request/output logging disable flags when supported by the running version.

Any service that replaces the preset's command/args inline must repeat the ZDR flags or inherit them through a common mechanism.

### 4. Envoy Gateway: disable proxy access logs on both LLM gateways

Set access logging off explicitly on:

- `apps/llm-public-gateway.yaml` -> `llm-public-gw-proxy`
- `apps/llm-ai-gateway.yaml` -> `llm-ai-gw-proxy`

Expected shape for the `EnvoyProxy` API/version in use:

```yaml
spec:
  telemetry:
    accessLog:
      disable: true
```

Keep Prometheus proxy metrics enabled; they are aggregate counters/gauges and are needed by KEDA scale-from-zero.

### 5. Envoy AI Gateway / tracing: explicitly forbid payload traces

We currently do not intentionally configure OTLP tracing. Make that an explicit invariant.

Do not enable GenAI/OpenInference detailed tracing on the public LLM route unless it is proven to omit request/response content. In particular, no trace backend may receive:

- prompt/messages
- completion text
- tool content
- request/response bodies
- Authorization / API-key material
- `X-Client-Id`

If tracing is added later, default to metadata-only spans and add a regression test before deployment.

### 6. Prometheus: retain useful metrics, prohibit content-bearing labels/exemplars

Prometheus can retain the existing 15d operational telemetry.

Add an acceptance check against the live `/metrics` endpoints and Prometheus label set. Fail the ZDR test if any LLM-serving series contains labels/exemplars such as:

- prompt/completion/message/content/token IDs
- `request_id`
- `trace_id` / `span_id`
- API key / Authorization
- `X-Client-Id` / client identity
- arbitrary user headers
- raw path/query values if they can contain user data

Static route/model/pool/pod names are fine.

Also ensure the dashboards never introduce per-client/per-request labels as a convenience feature.

### 7. cloudflared / Cloudflare boundary

`apps/cloudflared.yaml` uses `--loglevel info`; keep it out of debug/trace modes.

Because TLS terminates at Cloudflare's edge, Git cannot fully prove end-to-end ZDR. Document a manual account-side verification for `llm.birks.dev`:

- no request/response body logging
- no Worker/custom code persisting payloads
- no Logpush/Logpull field or destination that captures customer content or Authorization values
- WAF/security tooling does not persist request bodies containing model content
- only metadata/analytics that contain no customer content are allowed under this ZDR definition

If Cloudflare cannot make the customer-content-retention guarantee we want, document the limitation explicitly rather than calling the entire path ZDR without qualification.

## Verification / acceptance test

### A. Effective vLLM configuration

For every public model pod, verify the running process/CLI supports and receives the ZDR flags:

```bash
python3 -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server --help | \
  grep -Ei 'log.requests|log.outputs|uvicorn.*access|otlp|trace|prefix.cach'
```

Expected effective policy:

- request logging OFF
- output logging OFF
- Uvicorn access logging OFF
- prefix caching OFF
- OTLP/detailed tracing absent
- DEBUG/TRACE logging absent

### B. Canary-content test

Send a unique payload, e.g.:

```text
ZDR_CANARY_<random-uuid>
```

Then search all components that handled the request:

- vLLM pod logs
- EPP logs
- Envoy Gateway proxy logs
- Envoy AI Gateway controller/proxy logs
- cloudflared logs
- any Loki/log collector
- any Tempo/Jaeger/OTel backend

The canary must appear **nowhere** after the response is complete.

### C. Prometheus canary test

After sending the same canary, verify it is absent from all exposed metrics and retained Prometheus labels:

```bash
curl -s http://<vllm>/metrics | grep -F 'ZDR_CANARY_' && exit 1
curl -s http://<epp>:9090/metrics | grep -F 'ZDR_CANARY_' && exit 1
curl -s http://<envoy>:19001/stats/prometheus | grep -F 'ZDR_CANARY_' && exit 1
```

Also inspect label names/values for suspicious high-cardinality request identity:

```text
request_id
trace_id
span_id
client_id
x_client_id
authorization
prompt
completion
message
content
```

Token **counts** and latency/size histograms are expected and allowed; token **IDs/content** are not.

### D. Persistence check

Repeat the canary search after Prometheus/log retention has had time to ingest the request. This catches payload leakage introduced by exporters/collectors rather than the serving process itself.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All active public `LLMInferenceService` vLLM processes explicitly disable request logging.
- [ ] All active public vLLM processes explicitly disable output logging where supported.
- [ ] All active public vLLM processes disable Uvicorn access logs.
- [ ] All active public vLLM processes explicitly disable prefix caching / completed-request KV reuse.
- [ ] No vLLM OTLP/detailed tracing configuration is present.
- [ ] Both public and AI Envoy gateway proxies explicitly disable access logs.
- [ ] Envoy/AI Gateway tracing cannot export prompt/completion/body/header content.
- [ ] Prometheus retains only aggregate/system telemetry; no customer-content labels or exemplars exist.
- [ ] Existing 15d Prometheus retention remains acceptable under the documented customer-content ZDR definition.
- [ ] Unique canary text is absent from every component log, trace backend, `/metrics` output, and Prometheus-retained label value.
- [ ] Cloudflare account-side logging/analytics settings are manually verified and documented.
- [ ] The repo contains a short ZDR policy/comment explaining what is and is not retained so future upgrades preserve the invariant.

## Non-goal / terminology

This does **not** mean "no observability" or "no metadata exists." Aggregate system/usage telemetry that contains no customer content is compatible with the working ZDR definition.

If we later decide to promise the stronger statement **"no request-derived metadata is retained at all"**, the current Prometheus token-count/latency/request-volume metrics would need to be reduced substantially. That is intentionally a different and stricter policy.

items.title: [RFC] Mooncake Conductor as an external KV-cache index provider for vllm-router
items.body:
## Summary This RFC proposes letting vllm-router use [Mooncake Conductor][conductor] as a KV-cache index backend for the `kv_aware` policy, next to the router's built-in event-driven indexer (`src/kv_index/`). Conductor is a standalone global prefix-cache indexer. It consumes KV events from vLLM, SGLang and the Mooncake Store master over ZMQ, keeps a tiered (device / host / shared-pool / disk) prefix table, and answers "how many prefix tokens of this request does each instance already hold, at which tier". It does not route: endpoints, health, load and the final decision stay in the router. The proposal keeps the router's current behaviour as the default and adds: 1. A `ConductorMatchProvider` that implements the existing `TieredMatchProvider` port, so `kv_aware`'s load accounting, scorer and picker are reused. The cost model needs one change: crediting a chain of continuation tiers instead of a single one. 2. A `--kv-index-backend {local,conductor,hybrid}` switch. `hybrid` keeps the in-process index for engine-local tiers and takes shared-pool (Mooncake Store) residency from Conductor. 3. Router-driven registration: the router already discovers each worker's KV event sources and forwards them to Conductor (`conductor` mode replaces the local subscribers; `hybrid` keeps both). [conductor]: https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/tree/main/mooncake-conductor ## Motivation The router's `kv_index` works well for a single router replica watching vLLM workers' own caches. Three deployment patterns push past it: - **Shared KV pool.** With Mooncake Store as an L2/L3 pool, blocks live in the pool rather than in any worker. The router models this (`ResidencyOwner::CacheOwner`, `StorageTier::External`, documented as "shared pool (Mooncake)"), but nothing feeds it correctly today: - vLLM's `MooncakeStoreConnector` emits `BlockStored(medium="cpu")` with no `ownership` when it puts a block, so the router records it as the writing worker's own `HostPinned` block. Other workers that could load it from the pool get no credit. - Eviction happens in the Store master, and the connector emits no `BlockRemoved` for it, so those entries go stale. - The master does publish puts and evictions (Mooncake RFC #1527 schema), but `kv_index/wire.rs` does not decode that schema. Conductor already ingests it. - **Multiple router replicas.** Each replica opens one SUB socket per `(worker, dp_rank)` and holds a full copy of the index, so connections and memory grow as replicas × workers, and a freshly started replica only sees blocks stored after it subscribed (replay covers the publisher's bounded buffer, not the full cache). A shared indexer lets replicas stay stateless with respect to cache residency. - **Heterogeneous engines.** Conductor already normalizes vLLM and SGLang events and their different hash recipes behind one query API. The goal is not to replace `kv_index`. It stays the zero-dependency default; Conductor is an opt-in backend for deployments that need a shared pool view or a shared index. ## Background ### vllm-router `kv_index` (as of `08d4038`) - `KvIndexSupervisor` asks each worker for its server info (`instance_id`, `block_size`; gRPC `GetServerInfo` or HTTP `/get_server_info`) and its KV event sources (per-rank `endpoint`, `replay_endpoint`, `topic`; gRPC `GetKvEventSources` or HTTP `/kv_event_sources`), rewrites wildcard bind addresses to the worker host, then runs a ZMQ SUB + DEALER-replay subscriber per `(worker, dp_rank)`. - `KvBlockIndexer` is a radix tree keyed by a router-local hash (`local_block_hashes`: per-block SHA-256 of tokens + LoRA, unchained; chain position comes from the tree path). Engine block hashes are used only as anchors for parent resolution and `BlockRemoved`. - `KvAwarePolicy` hashes the request's token ids, calls `TieredMatchProvider::find_tiered_matches(&MatchQuery)` and gets `Vec`. `credited_tokens` applies vLLM's two-segment reuse rule with per-tier transfer credits (device 1.0, host 0.8, external 0.6, disk 0.3); cost is `ptoken × (active + 1)`, picked by `TemperaturePicker`. - Placement credit needs token ids, which today exist only on the all-gRPC `/v1/chat/completions` path. `kv_aware` is rejected in PD mode. ### Mooncake Conductor - Ingest: ZMQ SUB `[topic, seq, payload]` plus DEALER replay against the publisher's ROUTER; gap detection with bounded buffering; on unrecoverable loss the source is marked stale and everything it contributed is retracted. Decoders for vLLM, SGLang and Mooncake Store (`PublisherKind`). - Index: `PrefixCacheTable`, one context per `{tenant_id, model, lora_name, block_size}`, keyed by a 64-bit projection of the engine's own chained block hash. Tiers, in reuse priority order: `device` (engine GPU/NPU), `cpu_local` (engine host memory), `cpu_share` (Mooncake Store memory replicas), `disk` (engine-local or Mooncake disk replicas). - What is indexed per publisher: vLLM events for medium `gpu`, `cpu_pinned`; SGLang `gpu`, `cpu_pinned`, `disk`; the Mooncake Store master feeds `cpu_share` and `disk`, deriving block identity from the Store object key (the master emits no hashes). Shared-tier hits count for every instance registered in the same context. - Hashing: Conductor recomputes the engine's chain from token ids on query. Each registration declares a `hash_profile` (`vllm_v1` + `sha256_cbor`/`sha256`, `sglang` + `sha256_raw`), verified against golden vectors generated from vLLM. `lora_name` and `cache_salt` are part of the chain, so salted requests can be matched. All services in one context must share one profile. - API: msgpack HTTP on `:13333` (`POST /query`, `/register`, `/unregister`, `GET /services`, `/global_view`) and coro_rpc on `:13334`, with C++, Python and Rust clients. The Rust crate `mooncake_conductor` is a bindgen wrapper over the C ABI that statically links Mooncake's C++ client core. Measured RPC query latency is under 10 ms for a 1M-token prompt. - `POST /query` takes `{model, block_size, token_ids, tenant_id (Optional), lora_name(Optional), cache_salt(Optional), instance_id(Optional)}` and returns per instance `{longest_matched, dp: {rank: device_tokens}, rank_matches: {rank: {device, cpu_local, cpu_share, disk}}, device, cpu_local, cpu_share, disk}`. Tier counts are cumulative along one contiguous prefix, `device <= cpu_local <= cpu_share <= disk`: each is the prefix reachable using that tier and every tier before it, and `longest_matched == disk`. - Registrations are in memory. Re-registering an identical config is a no-op; a different config for an existing `instance_id|tenant_id|dp_rank` key, or an endpoint already used by another service, is rejected. ### Comparison | | router `kv_index` | Mooncake Conductor | |---|---|---| | Deployment | in-process, per router replica | separate service, shared | | Engines | vLLM | vLLM, SGLang | | Shared pool events | modelled; master stream not decoded | Mooncake Store master | | Lookup key | router-local token hash | engine chained hash (recomputed) | | `cache_salt` | no credit | supported | | Result shape | block segments per `(target, tier)` | cumulative tokens per `(instance, rank, tier)` | | kvcache offload (`medium=CPU`) | indexed as `HostPinned` | indexed as `cpu_share` or `cpu_local` | | Query latency | in-memory, sync | one round-trip; RPC < 10 ms at 1M tokens | | Restart state | rebuilt from live events | rebuilt from live events | ## Design Principle: **Conductor reports cache facts; the router decides.** Conductor never sees load, health or policy parameters, and a Conductor failure must degrade to today's behaviour, never fail a request. ```mermaid flowchart LR req([Request]) --> prepare subgraph router["vllm-router"] prepare["frontend.prepare
(tokenize)"] -->|token_ids| policy["KvAwarePolicy
cost model + picker"] policy --> port{{"TieredMatchProvider"}} port -->|local| localp["KvBlockIndexer"] port -->|conductor| condp["ConductorMatchProvider"] port -->|hybrid| comp["CompositeMatchProvider"] comp --> localp comp --> condp sup["KvIndexSupervisor
(worker discovery)"] end workers["vLLM workers"] conductor[("Mooncake Conductor")] master["Mooncake Store master"] workers -. "KV events (ZMQ)" .-> localp workers -. "KV events (ZMQ)" .-> conductor master -. "KV events (ZMQ)" .-> conductor condp -->|"query (RPC / HTTP)"| conductor sup -->|"register / unregister / reconcile"| conductor sup -->|"GetServerInfo / GetKvEventSources"| workers policy ==>|dispatch| workers ``` Solid arrows are calls on the request or control path; dotted arrows are KV event streams. `local` mode uses only `KvBlockIndexer` and its subscribers, `conductor` only `ConductorMatchProvider`, `hybrid` both through `CompositeMatchProvider`. ### 1. Extend `MatchQuery` with request context `MatchQuery` currently carries only router-local hashes, which Conductor cannot use: it keys on the engine's chained hash and recomputes it from token ids. Add the inputs the policy already has (`select_worker_with_receipt` receives `token_ids`, `lora_name`, `cache_salt`): ```rust pub struct MatchQuery<'a> { pub group_idx: u32, pub local_hashes: Vec>, // used by KvBlockIndexer pub tiers_of_interest: Vec, pub request: Option>, // new; used by external providers } pub struct MatchRequest<'a> { pub model_id: &'a str, pub block_size: u32, pub token_ids: &'a [u32], pub lora_name: Option<&'a str>, pub cache_salt: Option<&'a str>, } ``` `KvBlockIndexer` ignores `request`; local hashing stays where it is. The `placement_enabled` short-circuit for salted requests moves into the local provider so an external provider can still credit them. ### 2. `ConductorMatchProvider` Implements `TieredMatchProvider` by calling `POST /query` or `RPC query` and translating the answer. For each instance and rank in `rank_matches`, the cumulative boundaries `d <= l <= s <= k` (device, cpu_local, cpu_share, disk; tokens, divided by `block_size` and floored) become one segment per tier, each starting where the higher-priority tier stopped: | Conductor field | router `StorageTier` | segment (blocks) | |---|---|---| | `device` | `Device` | `[0, d)` | | `cpu_local` | `HostPinned` | `[d, l)` | | `cpu_share` | `External` | `[l, s)` | | `disk` | `Disk` | `[s, k)` | Empty segments are omitted. The target is `RoutableTarget{instance_id, dp_rank}` from the response key and the `rank_matches` key. The provider drops ranks the router does not know or that are unhealthy, and drops a response that violates the documented invariants (`d <= l <= s <= k`, `k` not beyond the query length, `dp[r] == rank_matches[r].device`). A dropped response means zero credit, not an error. **Cost-model change.** Today `credited_tokens` takes the device prefix plus the single best non-device segment that covers the device boundary, credited at that one tier's rate. Conductor's chain is several adjacent segments (`[d,l)`, `[l,s)`, `[s,k)`), and only the first non-empty one touches the device boundary, so under the current rule everything after it (typically the pool and disk) would be lost. This RFC changes the continuation rule: walk forward from the device boundary, credit each block at the highest transfer credit among the target's non-device segments covering it, and stop at the first uncovered block. With Conductor's disjoint segments this credits `[d,l)` at host rate, `[l,s)` at external rate and `[s,k)` at disk rate. With a single continuation segment (today's local index) the walk credits the same blocks at the same rate as before; with several overlapping local segments it can only credit more, never less. `local` scoring changes only in that last case. `instance_id` must be the same string on both sides. The router already treats the engine-reported `instance_id` from `GetServerInfo` as stable target identity, and registers it with Conductor (section 4), so no mapping table is needed. Shared-pool hits: Conductor credits `cpu_share` and shared `disk` to every instance registered in the context, which matches the router's `External` model (any worker attached to the pool can load the block). The router's health filter still applies, so only reachable workers receive the credit. ### 3. Query path and latency budget `find_tiered_matches` is synchronous and runs inline in worker selection. A network call there needs a hard bound: - Add an async `prefetch_matches(&MatchQuery) -> Vec` to the provider trait with a default that calls the sync method. The router awaits it before entering the selection retry loop, under `--conductor-query-timeout-ms` (default 10, which covers the measured RPC latency for 1M-token prompts). On timeout the request is scored with no placement credit, exactly as an HTTP-worker request is today. - One query per request and `CacheKey`, not per worker: Conductor returns all instances in one response (the policy already dedups by `CacheKey`). - Transport sits behind a small client trait with two implementations: - **RPC (recommended for production)**: the `mooncake_conductor` crate against `:13334`, behind a cargo feature `conductor-rpc`. It is the path with the measured latency. The crate's API is blocking and serializes calls per handle, so the router runs it on `spawn_blocking` with a small pool of handles. It needs a Mooncake build tree at compile time, which is why it is opt-in rather than a default dependency. - **HTTP/msgpack (default build)**: `POST /query` on `:13333` with the router's existing `reqwest` and `rmp-serde`; tokens go as a packed little-endian int32 `bin`. Pure Rust, no extra build dependency; latency to be benchmarked against RPC before recommending it for long prompts. - A simple circuit breaker (N consecutive failures → skip Conductor for T seconds) keeps a dead Conductor from adding the timeout to every request. ### 4. Registration and lifecycle Conductor needs to know each event source and its hash profile. The router already discovers the sources, so in `conductor`/`hybrid` mode `KvIndexSupervisor::on_worker_added` posts them to Conductor instead of (or in addition to) starting local subscribers: ``` POST /register { endpoint, replay_endpoint, // GetKvEventSources, host-resolved type: "vLLM", modelname, lora_name: "", instance_id, dp_rank, block_size, // GetServerInfo / source rank tenant_id: "default", cache_group: 0, hash_profile: { strategy: "vllm_v1", algorithm: "sha256_cbor", python_hash_seed: "", // omitted when unset index_projection: "low64_be" } } ``` - vLLM's `KVEventsConfig.endpoint` is a bind address (default `tcp://*:5557`). The router already rewrites it to the worker's host for its own subscribers and must send the resolved address, since Conductor rejects an endpoint already used by another service. - `/unregister` on worker removal and periodic reconciliation against `GET /services` (re-register anything missing, which also covers a Conductor restart). Identical re-registration is a no-op on Conductor, so several router replicas registering the same worker is safe; unregister with several replicas is an open question. - Mooncake Store master sources (`type: "Mooncake"`) are not workers and are not discovered by the router. They come from `--conductor-shared-source` or Conductor's own static config, must use the same hash profile as the engines writing the keys, and can only be registered after at least one engine of that context. The master has no replay endpoint, so a sequence gap marks the stream stale until it is registered again; reconciliation re-registers it. #### Hash profile discovery `hash_profile` must reproduce the engine's NONE_HASH root and block hash exactly. From the vLLM source (`vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py`, `resolve_none_hash_seed`): | `--prefix-caching-hash-algo` | `PYTHONHASHSEED` | vLLM version | seed text vLLM hashes | |---|---|---|---| | `sha256` (default), `sha256_cbor` | set | any | its value | | `sha256`, `sha256_cbor` | unset | ≥ 0.29.0 (#51875) | `"vllm-none-hash"` | | `sha256`, `sha256_cbor` | unset | < 0.29.0 | none: NONE_HASH is 32 random bytes | Conductor follows the same rule, so it reproduces vLLM's root in both supported cases: - **`PYTHONHASHSEED` set:** the registration carries the exact value in `hash_profile.python_hash_seed`, and Conductor hashes it as the seed text, as it does today. CPython itself only starts with `"random"` or a decimal in `0..4294967295`, which is exactly what Conductor validates. - **`PYTHONHASHSEED` unset:** the registration omits `python_hash_seed` (or sends nil), and Conductor applies vLLM #51875: the seed text is `"vllm-none-hash"` for `sha256` / `sha256_cbor`. Today Conductor requires the field for `vllm_v1`, so this is a Mooncake change (see Required changes). "Unset" must stay distinguishable from an explicit value on the wire; it is never encoded as an empty string. - **Unset on vLLM < 0.29.0:** the root is random per process and no indexer can reproduce it. The router checks `ServerInfo.engine_version` and does not register such workers with Conductor, logging that `PYTHONHASHSEED` must be set; they still route normally, with no placement credit from Conductor. Conductor cannot read a worker's environment, so the router has to tell it whether the seed is set and to what. vLLM's gRPC `ServerInfo` and `KvEventSource` carry neither the hash algorithm nor the seed; the HTTP `/server_info` dump includes `cache_config.prefix_caching_hash_algo` only in dev mode, and never the seed. This RFC proposes two `ServerInfo` fields: - `prefix_caching_hash_algo` - `python_hash_seed`: the raw `PYTHONHASHSEED` value, absent when unset. Only for `sha256` / `sha256_cbor`, whose seed vLLM does not treat as secret. The raw value is passed through, not vLLM's resolved seed, so the "unset" rule lives in one place (Conductor) and the router stays a pass-through. Until the fields land, the router takes them from `--conductor-hash-profile`. A mismatch yields zero hits, never wrong hits. Deployments where an operator or sidecar already manages Conductor registrations can set `--conductor-register=false`; the router then only queries. ### 5. Compatibility with the router's `kv_index` | mode | local subscribers | Conductor tiers used | use case | |---|---|---|---| | `local` (default) | yes | none | today's behaviour, no new dependency | | `conductor` | no | all | many router replicas, SGLang workers | | `hybrid` | yes | `cpu_share`, `disk` | vLLM workers + Mooncake Store pool | vLLM emits `medium=cpu` from two different sources, and they must not be treated alike: | source | what the block is | `BlockRemoved` on eviction | distinguishing field today | |---|---|---|---| | native CPU offload (`OffloadingConnector`) | engine-local host memory | yes | `locality`, `ownership` set by the offload tier | | `MooncakeStoreConnector` | a put into the shared Mooncake pool | no | none | The second kind is already reported, correctly, by the Store master stream as `cpu_share` with evictions. Indexing it again as `cpu_local` would credit the writing worker as if it held the block locally, and the entry would never be removed after a pool eviction. `hybrid` uses a `CompositeMatchProvider`. `Device`, `HostPinned` and `Disk` segments come from `KvBlockIndexer`; from Conductor's answer it keeps only the `[l, s)` (`External`) and `[s, k)` (`Disk`) segments. Both providers report absolute block positions in the same prompt, so their segments line up; the chained continuation walk (section 2) takes, at each position, the highest-credit segment of that target covering it, so overlap needs no dedup rule. Engines are still registered with Conductor in this mode, because a Mooncake master stream only attaches to a context that has an engine. If Conductor times out, `hybrid` degrades to `local`. Until the connector sets `ownership`, the local index records its puts as the writer's `HostPinned`. In `hybrid` the same block then appears as local `HostPinned` (credit 0.8) and Conductor `External` (0.6) for that worker; the per-block max picks 0.8, a small bias toward the writer, and the local entry can outlive a pool eviction. Other workers get only the `External` credit, which is correct. The local and Conductor indexes hash differently (router-local unchained SHA-256 vs. the engine's chained hash). That is by design: each provider derives its own key from the same `MatchRequest`, so neither has to emulate the other. `src/kv_hash.rs` (vLLM `sha256_cbor`, golden-tested, currently unused) is not needed for this RFC, but would let a future provider query by hash instead of by tokens. ### 6. Configuration ``` --kv-index-backend {local,conductor,hybrid} default: local --conductor-url http://conductor:13333 (HTTP transport) --conductor-rpc-addr conductor:13334 (RPC, needs feature conductor-rpc) --conductor-query-timeout-ms 10 --conductor-register / --no-conductor-register default: register --conductor-hash-profile vllm_v1:sha256_cbor:0:low64_be (seed "unset" = vLLM default) --conductor-tenant-id default --conductor-shared-source tcp://store-master:PORT (repeatable, optional) ``` All are rejected unless `--policy kv_aware`. Equivalent fields go in `KvAwareConfig` in `config/types.rs`. ### 7. Observability Counters and histograms: `conductor_query_latency_seconds`, `conductor_query_errors_total{reason=timeout|http|decode|invariant}`, `conductor_breaker_open`, `conductor_registered_sources`, and `kv_aware_credited_tokens{tier}` so operators can see what the pool tier contributes. ## Scope and limitations - Same coverage as `kv_aware` today: only requests with token ids (all-gRPC chat path) get placement credit. Conductor does not change that; extending tokenization to HTTP workers is a separate effort. - PD mode stays out of scope for the first phase. Prefill selection is the natural next step (it is what Mooncake's own cache-aware proxy example does) once `kv_aware` is allowed as `--prefill-policy`. - `cache_group` other than 0 (hybrid-attention models with several KV groups) is not supported by Conductor yet; such models stay on `local`. ## Required changes vllm-router: 1. `MatchQuery` gains `request: Option`; move the salted-request skip into the local provider. 2. Chained continuation rule in `credited_tokens` (section 2), with tests showing `local` results are unchanged for single-segment matches. 3. Async `prefetch_matches` on the provider port and a timeout-bounded call before selection. 4. Conductor client trait with HTTP/msgpack (default) and RPC (`conductor-rpc` feature) implementations; `ConductorMatchProvider` (response translation, invariant checks, circuit breaker) and `CompositeMatchProvider`. 5. `KvIndexSupervisor`: register / unregister / reconcile against Conductor, using the already host-resolved event endpoints. 6. CLI and `KvAwareConfig` options, validation, metrics, docs in `docs/load_balancing/README.md`. 7. Tests: translation table and invariant rejection against recorded Conductor responses; timeout and breaker behaviour against a stub server; an e2e test with a real Conductor and a synthetic vLLM publisher. Mooncake: 1. Make `python_hash_seed` optional for `vllm_v1`. When it is absent or nil, follow vLLM #51875 and hash `"vllm-none-hash"` as the seed for `sha256` / `sha256_cbor`; when present, keep today's validation and use it verbatim. Add golden vectors for the unset case generated with vLLM ≥ 0.29.0. 2. Index vLLM `STORAGE` events into `disk`, skipping events whose `ownership` marks them as shared-pool puts (those come from the Store master as `cpu_share`). 3. Keep the `/query` and `/register` msgpack schemas stable and versioned; the router depends on them. 4. Upstream the router-integration guide and cache-aware proxy example. ## Alternatives considered - **RPC only, or HTTP only.** RPC has the measured latency but links Mooncake's C++ core into the router build; HTTP keeps the default build pure Rust. Supporting both behind one client trait lets the default build stay dependency-free while production builds opt into RPC. - **Separate `conductor` policy.** Mooncake's proxy example routes to max `longest_matched`. Reusing `kv_aware` instead gets load-aware scoring, tier credits, temperature and slot accounting for free.

items.title: [RFC]: Semantic KV Cache Reuse Interface
items.body:
### Motivation.

vLLM's exact prefix cache is the right primitive when requests share the same token prefix. Many long-context workloads have a nearby but different shape: the expensive reusable content is present, but the request starts with a different instruction, chat wrapper, retrieval order, or paraphrased lead-in. Exact prefix caching correctly misses in those cases. This potentially leaves a lot of potential optimization on the table.

This proposal is about exposing the engine-side controls needed for that class of reuse without putting a semantic search algorithm in vLLM. External systems can discover donors; vLLM should continue to own scheduling, paged KV allocation, block lifetime, failure recovery, and exact prefix-cache semantics.

- semantic lookup is an optional external policy decision,
- reporting external tokens to vLLM is a materialization promise,
- exact prefix-cache writes must remain exact,
- any approximate or request-only reuse needs explicit cache-commit semantics before it can be enabled safely with prefix caching.

### Proposed Change.

# Semantic KV Cache Connector Interface for vLLM


## Summary

vLLM already has most of the control points needed for semantic KV cache reuse. `KVConnectorBase_V1` separates scheduler-side external match discovery from worker-side KV materialization, the scheduler already has an explicit `num_external_computed_tokens` path, and the worker/model-runner path already lets connectors load KV into vLLM-owned paged KV slots before attention reads them.

This proposal defines a conservative semantic-KV connector strategy on top of that existing surface:

1. implement semantic donor discovery in an out-of-tree connector first,
2. use vLLM's existing external-token allocation path for materialized reuse,
3. keep vLLM's exact prefix cache semantics unchanged,
4. add only small generic upstream hooks after the connector proves out,
5. use SemBlend as an optional open-source example provider, not as a required vLLM dependency.

The first target is prefix-anchored, contiguous, block-aligned reuse: `| exact local prefix | external prefix | tokens to compute |`. With vLLM's current API, materialized external KV should be exact-equivalent to the target token/hash namespace or run in discovery-only mode. True non-identical semantic KV materialization needs one additional generic control: vLLM must be able to avoid committing approximate external KV as exact prefix-cache state. More general N:M, fragmented, or non-prefix semantic reuse is valuable, but it should not be the first upstream contract because it requires deeper changes in the scheduler, model runner, slot mapping, batching, and attention lifecycle.



## Preliminary SemBlend and SGLang Findings

Early work has been underway within SGLang to provide the interface for semantic/fuzzy kv cache reuse. This includes the first, open source semantic kv cache provider SemBlend (https://github.com/WorldFlowAI/semblend). This works shows that semantic donor discovery can find reuse opportunities exact prefix matching misses, especially in cross-instruction long-context prompts.

Early SGLang/SemBlend experiments reported warm-path TTFT wins that are very promising. We have observed up to 32x speedup at 16K. This is with **no** degradation in quality. In fact it is not uncommon for the PPL to improve. Benchmarks are still early and we (WorldFlow AI) are working on a labeled dataset tailor built for semantic kv cache reuse measurements.

The start of this within vLLM should be conservative: keep semantic discovery out of core, start with prefix-anchored contiguous reuse, and add a generic cache-commit policy before non-identical semantic KV can be materialized with prefix caching enabled.

## Non-goals for v1

- Do not merge a semantic search algorithm into vLLM core.
- Do not introduce a mandatory dependency on SemBlend -> https://github.com/worldflowai/semblend, embeddings, ANN libraries, or a remote service.
- Do not route semantic reuse through LMCache as a requirement.
- Do not change the meaning of vLLM's `BlockHash`, `BlockPool`, or exact prefix cache.
- Do not insert semantic donor KV into the exact prefix-cache hash table unless the token sequence and block hash are truly exact.
- Do not standardize arbitrary fragmented or multi-donor materialization in the first interface.
- Do not claim a semantic match is reused unless the connector can actually materialize the corresponding KV blocks into vLLM-owned slots.
- Do not materialize non-identical semantic KV through vLLM's exact external token path while exact prefix-cache writes remain enabled for that request or deployment.
- Do not require model-weight access in the first semantic connector patch.
- Do not support prompt embeddings, multimodal prompts, encoder-decoder models, LoRA-mixed batches, speculative edge cases, or Mamba/hybrid layouts until the connector has explicit compatibility gates for them.
