items.body:
# vLLM Router 2026 Roadmap Issues > Planning date: September 8, 2026 > Code baseline: vLLM Router `main@1d10e71` (identical to upstream `main` at the time of review) > Objective: define an actionable roadmap for the remainder of 2026 around vLLM-native integration, lightweight high-performance routing, exact KV awareness, and agent-aware scheduling. > Scope: CPU fast path, exact KV routing, agent-aware scheduling, E/P/D, Router HA, native API compatibility, SLO-based autoscaling, and in-flight request migration. ## Overview | # | Roadmap issue | Current foundation | Priority | 2026 target | External value | |---:|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | Integrate and Optimize the CPU-side Inference Fast Path #348 | ◐ Rust tokenizer, streaming utilities, and benchmarks exist, but they do not yet form an end-to-end request fast path | P0 | Tokenizer cache, request-scoped reuse, and JSON/streaming hot-path optimization | Demonstrate the performance advantage of a lightweight Rust router | | 2 | Event-driven Exact KV-aware Routing #294 | ○ Exact KV awareness is missing; the current cache-aware policy uses an approximate request-history tree | P0 | KV Events, an exact index, unified cost, and safe fallback | Flagship capability for the year | | 3 | Extend Session Affinity to Agent/Program-aware Scheduling #393 | ◐ Session-ID-based consistent hashing exists | P1 | Program metadata, a workflow profiler, a program-aware policy, and a KV TTL prototype | Differentiate for agentic workloads | | 4 | Extend P/D Routing to E/P/D #296
(Rust gRPC: #505) | ◐ P/D, DP-rank routing, and KV connectors exist; the Encode stage does not | P1 | Encode pool and three-stage routing MVP | Extend multimodal scheduling | | 5 | Complete Multi-Router HA and State Recovery | ◐ Health checks, retries, readiness, and process-level graceful shutdown exist; multi-Router state HA does not | P0 foundation / P1 complete | Drain and recovery foundations; active-active as a stretch goal | Make stateful routing production-ready | | 6 | Native API Compatibility for vLLM-Served Endpoints #440 | ◐ Transparent-proxy fallback forwards unknown endpoints, but without policy fidelity, retries, or metrics | P1 | First-class `/v1/messages` (Anthropic Messages), an API-compatibility contract, and a hardened fallback | Anthropic-SDK / Claude Code clients and non-OpenAI vLLM endpoints get full-fidelity routing | | 7 | SLO-Based Autoscaling | ◐ K8s service discovery, per-request TTFT/ITL metrics, and P/D rate calibration exist; no SLO aggregation, scaling recommendations, or autoscaling integration | P2 | Freshness-aware SLO signal pipeline, reactive scaling recommendations, and HPA/KEDA integration | Keep vLLM deployments within TTFT/ITL SLOs while autoscaling on demand | | 8 | In-flight Request Migration and Generation Continuity | ◐ Request retry / worker failover exist, but a failed decode restarts prefill from scratch; no token-state carryover | P2 / exploratory | Migration-vs-retry cost decision, a request-migration contract on top of engine snapshot/restore, usage re-baselining | Mid-stream worker fault does not discard completed generation | ## Roadmap principles - Do not turn vLLM Router into a broad, all-in-one gateway; its core remains vLLM inference routing. - Prioritize CPU optimizations that directly benefit tokenization, routing, and the streaming fast path. - Make exact KV state trustworthy before optimizing policy gains. - Agent hints must be optional, and ordinary OpenAI-compatible requests must remain compatible. - Deliver minimal closed loops for EPD and HA first rather than expanding the initial issues into full platform projects. - Base every performance claim on reproducible experiments using the same hardware, model, and trace. --- ## Issue 1: [Roadmap][P0] Integrate and Optimize the CPU-side Inference Fast Path > Details are tracked in #348. ### Background As GPU inference becomes faster, CPU work such as tokenization, JSON encoding/decoding, and stream processing can become the bottleneck. SMG moves tokenization and detokenization into a Rust gateway and uses an L0 exact-match tokenizer cache, an L1 prefix-aware tokenizer cache, and a gRPC tokens-in/tokens-out path to reduce Python/GIL and serialization overhead. vLLM Router already includes a Rust tokenizer, chat-template support, streaming decoding utilities, and benchmark infrastructure. However, the tokenizer module is not yet part of a complete CPU pipeline across the main request path, and there is no L0/L1 token-result cache. The worker data plane is currently HTTP; the gRPC/Tonic dependency in Cargo is primarily used for OpenTelemetry and does not constitute a worker gRPC fast path. The goal of this issue is to integrate and optimize the existing modules into a measurable CPU fast path. It is not to reimplement the Rust tokenizer or to build a complete tool, MCP, or provider gateway. ### Scope - Establish stable baselines for Router CPU usage, latency, throughput, and memory. - Integrate the existing Rust tokenizer, chat template, and streaming decoder into the request paths that need them. - Add a bounded L0 exact-match tokenizer cache. - Evaluate and implement an L1 prefix token cache aligned to special-token boundaries. - Tokenize and apply the chat template once per request, then reuse the result across the KV index, routing policy, and P/D flow. - Reduce JSON copies, repeated parsing, and intermediate string allocations in the request path. - Optimize incremental streaming decode and stop-sequence detection. - Evaluate an optional pre-tokenized/gRPC backend fast path. - Add metrics for cache hits, CPU time, allocations, and Router-added latency. ### Deliverables - [ ] CPU fast-path benchmark suite. - [ ] Request-path integration for the existing tokenizer and streaming modules. - [ ] Bounded L0/L1 tokenizer cache. - [ ] Request-scoped tokenization-result reuse. - [ ] JSON and streaming hot-path optimizations. - [ ] Design document or experimental implementation for an optional tokens-in/gRPC path. - [ ] Before-and-after performance report. ### Acceptance criteria - Token IDs and chat-template results match the target vLLM version. - Every cache has a capacity bound, TTL/eviction policy, and memory metrics; unbounded growth is not allowed. - Publish CPU, memory, P50/P99 Router-added latency, and throughput results. - Preserve existing HTTP behavior when the new fast path is disabled. - Do not count the OpenTelemetry gRPC exporter as worker gRPC support. ### Non-goals - Complete MCP tool orchestration. - Provider API translation. - Reimplementing every Hugging Face multimodal processor inside the Router. --- ## Issue 2: [Roadmap][P0] Add Event-driven Exact KV-aware Routing ### Background The current cache-aware policy maintains an approximate character-level tree from Router request history. It cannot determine which KV blocks are currently resident on a Worker or DP rank. Dynamo Router combines KV lifecycle events, a prefix index, and active load when selecting a Worker. ### Scope - Subscribe to vLLM KV `Stored`, `Removed`, and `Cleared` events. - Build an exact KV index keyed by model, Worker, DP rank, and block key. - Query request prefixes at token/block granularity and calculate actually reusable blocks. - Combine uncached prefill, active decode, active requests, and KV transfer cost in a unified cost model. - Automatically fall back to approximate cache-aware routing or P2C when KV Events are unavailable or the index is not trustworthy. - Emit a structured route receipt and decision metrics. - Validate block size, tokenizer compatibility, Worker epoch, and event freshness. ### Deliverables - [ ] vLLM KV Event subscriber. - [ ] Token/block KV placement index. - [ ] Unified KV-plus-load cost policy. - [ ] Exact/approximate/load-aware fallback. - [ ] Route receipt and Prometheus metrics. - [ ] Comparative benchmark covering RR, P2C, approximate cache-aware, and exact KV-aware routing. ### Acceptance criteria - `Stored`, `Removed`, and `AllBlocksCleared` events update the index correctly. - DP-rank-level KV placement matches actual Worker state. - Requests continue through a fallback policy when events are unavailable. - Report KV hit rate, TTFT P99, goodput/GPU, incorrect-routing rate, and Router overhead. - Do not claim absolute superiority using competitor data collected in a different environment. ### Non-goals - A multi-data-center global index is not required in the first phase. - Full multi-tier KV-offload orchestration is not required in the first phase. --- ## Issue 3: [Roadmap][P1] Extend Session Affinity to Agent/Program-aware Scheduling @warriorsniu ### Background Agent workflows contain multiple LLM calls, tool calls, and waiting periods. Per-request scheduling loses program-level context, which can cause session KV eviction, migration of one agent across Workers, and repeated prefill after a tool returns. The current consistent-hash policy can read headers such as `x-session-id`, `x-user-id`, and `x-tenant-id` and attempts to map the same key to the same Worker. This provides sticky sessions, but it does not understand programs, steps, tool waits, KV TTL, or expected output length. ThunderAgent introduces an LLM Program abstraction and a program-aware scheduler. Continuum uses a KV TTL based on recomputation/reload cost and eviction-induced queueing cost to selectively retain KV across tool calls. Pythia adds the profiling half: agentic frameworks pass only three identity fields (workflow type, workflow instance, agent role) via `extra_body`, and a gateway-side profiler asynchronously mines the annotated traces into a workflow model — a regex-projected control-flow graph (fan-outs, bounded loops, retry edges), per-agent output-length percentiles, and prompt-composition templates. Its production traces show why this pays off: >40% of agentic requests see near-zero prefix cache hits across agent boundaries and tool waits, heterogeneous requests mixed without output-length awareness cause preemption-inducing hot spots, and workflow fan-outs cascade >50% bursts across downstream models faster than reactive scaling can follow. Pythia reports up to 2.9× JCT reduction and 1.96× throughput from these models, implemented on SGLang. ### Scope - Define optional program/session/step metadata. - Preserve existing `x-session-id` consistent-hash behavior as the baseline when program metadata is absent. - Support program ID, step ID, agent role, priority, deadline, and expected output length. - Accept lightweight workflow identity metadata (`workflow_type_id`, `workflow_id`, `agent_id`) in the request body and forward it transparently to Workers. - Add a background workflow profiler that mines annotated traces into a control-flow model plus per-agent output-length profiles, off the request critical path, modeling the dominant percentile of executions rather than every edge case. - Use per-agent predicted output lengths in Worker selection (predicted-capacity scoring instead of raw request counts) and weight cache-aware routing by predicted future reuse from the control-flow model. - Select Workers using both KV affinity and live load at program scope. - Add program-level fairness so long-running agent workflows cannot monopolize a Worker. - Design a KV TTL/retention hint for tool-wait periods. - Evaluate eviction or offload at TTL expiry and prefetch before a tool returns. - Fall back to ordinary KV-aware routing when hints are absent or unsupported by the engine. - Evaluate job completion time using real or public agent traces. ### Deliverables - [ ] Agent scheduling metadata contract. - [ ] Workflow profiler prototype (control-flow model + per-agent output-length profiles). - [ ] Predicted-output-length-aware Worker selection. - [ ] Program/session-aware policy evolved from the existing session-affinity policy. - [ ] KV TTL/retention policy prototype. - [ ] Optional prefetch/offload hint design. - [ ] Agent trace replay and benchmark. ### Acceptance criteria - Ordinary requests do not need to supply agent metadata. - Profiling-derived predictions degrade gracefully to existing policies when metadata is absent, stale, or wrong. - Scheduling decisions for one program are explainable and replayable. - Compare ordinary KV-aware routing, sticky sessions, and program-aware routing. - Report agent job completion time, KV reuse, Worker migrations, and fairness. - Router-to-engine KV control must receive explicit accept/reject feedback from the engine; the Router must not assume a hint was executed. ### Non-goals - The Router does not execute tools. - The Router does not manage complete tool runtimes, disks, or network ports. - The profiler does not retain raw prompt/response content beyond what length- and identity-level profiling requires. - Performance numbers reported by the research papers are not project results. --- ## Issue 4: [Roadmap][P1] Extend P/D Routing to E/P/D ### Background A multimodal request can be decomposed into Encode, Prefill, and Decode stages. SGLang's EPD Router work introduces Encode Workers, a three-stage pipeline, and independent Worker policies. The referenced CI run covers its EPD routing pipeline work. ### Scope - Add an Encode Worker type, Encode pool, and service discovery. - Support a minimal Encode → Prefill → Decode orchestration flow. - Support independent policies for Encode, Prefill, and Decode. - Carry encoder output and KV-transfer metadata between stages. - Remain compatible with vLLM EC Connector/EPD interfaces rather than defining a separate private protocol. - Skip Encode for text-only requests and continue using the existing P/D path. - Add health, load, and latency metrics for all three stages. ### Deliverables - [ ] Encode Worker type and discovery. - [ ] E/P/D pipeline MVP. - [ ] Per-stage policy configuration. - [ ] Text-only P/D fallback. - [ ] End-to-end test with one multimodal model. ### Acceptance criteria - Encode, Prefill, and Decode can be deployed and scaled independently. - Text-only requests do not enter the Encode stage. - A failure in any stage produces an explicit error; execution must not continue with incomplete intermediate state. - Streaming response and client-cancellation behavior are correct. ### Non-goals - A general-purpose Omni stage graph is not part of the first phase. - Complex topology-aware EPD is not part of the first phase. --- ## Issue 5: [Roadmap][P0/P1] Complete Multi-Router HA and State Recovery ### Background Exact KV state, sessions, and active load make the Router stateful. The current Router already has Worker health checks, retries, circuit breakers, liveness/readiness endpoints, and Axum graceful shutdown on `SIGTERM` or `Ctrl+C`. It does not have an explicit `DRAINING` state, readiness-based traffic removal, multi-Router state recovery, or cross-replica HA. SMG uses SWIM and CRDTs to synchronize Worker, policy, rate-limit, and cache-aware state. llm-d supports leader election, warm standby, and constrained active-active operation. This issue completes multi-Router HA on top of the existing single-process reliability mechanisms rather than reimplementing health checks and retries. ### Scope - Extend the existing liveness/readiness endpoints and process-level graceful shutdown with an explicit `DRAINING` state, readiness-based traffic removal, and rolling-upgrade behavior. - Add replay for KV Event gaps and a snapshot/rebuild path for cold starts. - Provide a basic active-passive/warm-standby mode. - Evaluate active-active operation in which exact KV indexes converge independently and only the minimum required state is synchronized. - Define explicit `EXACT`, `DEGRADED`, and `FALLBACK` states during recovery. - Add fault-injection, RTO, and state-convergence metrics. ### Deliverables - [ ] Graceful drain and readiness gate built on the existing shutdown/readiness implementation. @LOGO127 - [ ] KV-index replay/snapshot foundation. - [ ] Warm-standby deployment example. - [ ] Multi-Router recovery tests. - [ ] Active-active design document as a stretch goal. ### Acceptance criteria - In a multi-Router deployment, restarting or rolling one Router does not make the service unavailable. - A new Router does not perform exact KV routing until its index is trustworthy. - Event gaps are detected, and failed recovery triggers safe fallback. - Complete Router-kill, Worker-kill, event-loss, and 24-hour steady-state tests. ### Non-goals - Strong-consistency Raft is not a mandatory dependency in the first phase. - The first phase does not synchronize every local counter or transient request state. --- ## Issue 6: [Roadmap][P1] Native API Compatibility for vLLM-Served Endpoints ### Background vLLM's serving surface has grown beyond the OpenAI APIs: it now natively serves the Anthropic Messages API at `/v1/messages` (registered alongside the OpenAI routes), which lets Anthropic-SDK clients and tools such as Claude Code point `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` at a vLLM deployment. vLLM Router currently gives first-class treatment — typed parsing, routing-text extraction, per-model policies, retries, circuit-breaker accounting, load tracking, per-route metrics, concurrency limiting, and WASM middleware — to only five route families: `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/completions`, `/v1/responses`, `/v1/embeddings`, and `/v1/rerank`. Every other endpoint falls through to the transparent-proxy fallback, which is a lossy byte-pipe: no retries, no circuit-breaker accounting, no per-route metrics, no concurrency limit or WASM middleware, Bearer-only authentication (Anthropic-style `x-api-key` is rejected when API-key validation is enabled), stripped protocol headers (e.g. `anthropic-version`), and worker selection on the raw serialized JSON body — degrading cache-aware affinity, consistent-hash stickiness, and session affinity. This issue defines an API-compatibility contract: any endpoint vLLM serves natively must be routable by the Router with full fidelity. It is about native-endpoint parity, not protocol translation between API dialects. ### Scope - Define an API-compatibility matrix: vLLM-served endpoint × routing fidelity level (first-class / transparent / unsupported), published and kept in sync with vLLM. - Add `/v1/messages` as a first-class route (non-streaming and streaming). - Extract routing text from the Anthropic request shape (top-level `system`, `messages[].content` content blocks) so cache-aware, session-affinity, and consistent-hash policies operate on semantic text rather than serialized JSON. - Accept Anthropic-style authentication (`x-api-key` + `anthropic-version`) alongside `Authorization: Bearer`, and forward protocol headers to workers. - Handle Anthropic SSE semantics (`message_start`, `content_block_*`, `message_delta`, `message_stop`, `ping`) for stream-completion detection, TTFT measurement, and graceful mid-stream errors. - Parse Anthropic usage (`input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `cache_creation_input_tokens`, `cache_read_input_tokens`) into request tracking and Prometheus metrics. - Harden the transparent fallback — or define explicit promotion criteria — so endpoints not yet first-class still get retries, circuit-breaker accounting, per-model policies, load tracking, header forwarding, and metrics. - Optionally serve `/v1/messages/count_tokens` router-side using the existing tokenizer module. - Add conformance tests that replay each supported API against mock and real vLLM workers. ### Deliverables - [ ] API-compatibility matrix document. - [ ] First-class `/v1/messages` routing (non-streaming and streaming) with routing-text extraction. - [ ] `x-api-key` authentication and `anthropic-version` forwarding. - [ ] Anthropic usage ingestion into metrics. - [ ] Transparent-fallback hardening or a documented promotion path. - [ ] Conformance test suite for supported endpoints. - [ ] (Stretch) Router-side `/v1/messages/count_tokens`. ### Acceptance criteria - The Anthropic SDK and Claude Code work unchanged against the Router via `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`. - Cache-aware, session-affinity, and consistent-hash policies produce the same worker decisions for `/v1/messages` as for equivalent chat requests. - Streamed responses complete with correct finish semantics; TTFT and usage metrics are recorded. - No endpoint listed in the compatibility matrix silently degrades to the lossy fallback. - Existing OpenAI-compatible behavior is unchanged when the new routes are disabled. ### Non-goals - Cross-provider protocol translation (e.g. OpenAI ↔ Anthropic request/response conversion) — consistent with Issue 1's non-goals. - Becoming a multi-provider gateway; the Router routes vLLM-native endpoints only. --- ## Issue 7: [Roadmap][P2] SLO-Based Autoscaling ### Background The Router has Kubernetes service discovery, mock CPU benchmarks, criterion benches, and P/D rate calibration — but no SLO signal pipeline, no autoscaling integration, and no replay harness that reproduces both request load and KV-event streams (the existing mock bench explicitly does not model affinity evolution). Prometheus metrics expose per-request TTFT/ITL and throughput, but there is no freshness-aware per-model SLO aggregation and no scaling-recommendation path, so scaling today is manual pool management and policy comparisons cannot be validated offline. ### Scope - SLO signal pipeline: per-model/per-route TTFT, ITL, goodput, queueing, and KV hit-rate series with explicit freshness/liveness flags (stale or missing signals must be distinguishable from healthy), exported in a form consumable by HPA/KEDA external metrics. - Reactive scaling recommendations first (scale-out on SLO burn, scale-in on sustained idle with a floor), documented integration with HPA/KEDA; no in-tree cluster controller in the first phase. - Trace replay harness: record (opt-in) and replay anonymized request traces that drive both the request path and a synthetic KV-event stream, so cache-aware, `kv_aware`, and session-affinity policies face realistic affinity evolution. - Reuse Issue 1's tokenizer/benchmarks and the existing P/D calibration to predict worker capacity; publish policy-comparison runs (RR, P2C, session-affinity, cache-aware, `kv_aware`) on identical replays. - Privacy: record lengths, hashes, and identities only — same constraint as the Issue 3 profiler; no raw prompt/response content. ### Deliverables - [ ] Freshness-aware SLO metrics export + HPA/KEDA integration example. - [ ] Scaling recommendation logic (reactive) with idle scale-in and capacity floor. - [ ] Replay harness reproducing load + KV-event streams (opt-in recording, anonymized). - [ ] Capacity calibration guide per worker SKU/model from existing calibration data. - [ ] Published policy-comparison replay results. ### Acceptance criteria - Signals correctly report staleness/absence; the scaling path never acts on silently stale data. - Replay reproduces affinity-sensitive behavior: a replayed session/prefix mix yields measurably different KV hit rates across policies (validated against a live small cluster once). - Recording is off by default and leaks no prompt content (verified by inspection/tests). - The first phase delivers recommendations + integration docs, not a bespoke scheduler. ### Non-goals - A general-purpose cluster autoscaler or Kubernetes controller inside the Router. - Predictive/ML-based scaling in the first phase. - Multi-cluster capacity optimization. --- ## Issue 8: [Roadmap][P2/exploratory] In-flight Request Migration and Generation Continuity ### Background Today the Router's answer to a worker fault is retry/failover, which restarts prefill from scratch — completed generation tokens are lost, and usage counters restart from the original prompt. Research systems have established both halves of the problem. Llumnix (OSDI '24) migrates in-flight requests across instances by pipelining append-only KV-cache copying with token generation, achieving near-zero, constant downtime. DéjàVu (ICML '24) provides a KV-cache streaming library with checkpoint-and-migrate protocols for fault-tolerant generative serving, and GhostServe (MLSys '26) protects the streaming KV cache with erasure-coded shadow checkpoints in host memory for fast reconstruction after device failure — motivated by long-running agentic requests. LUMEN (2026) treats recovery as a coordinated, load-aware decision across checkpoint placement, interrupted-request distribution, and serving-capacity restoration during model reload — i.e., a router/coordinator-level problem, not just an engine mechanism. On the cost side, Mooncake (FAST '25) makes KV transfer a first-class cost in a KVCache-centric global scheduler, and CacheGen (SIGCOMM '24) makes context fetch bandwidth-adaptive, recomputing on the fly when bandwidth is scarce — the same fetch-vs-recompute trade-off that a migration-vs-retry decision must evaluate. This issue is exploratory because it depends on engine-side snapshot/restore and KV-transfer primitives that vLLM exposes only partially today; the Router's job is the decision and the contract, not the engine mechanism. ### Scope - Define a migration-vs-retry decision framework: recompute cost (uncached prefix × prefill rate from calibration) vs migration cost (KV transfer + state handoff), reusing the Issue 2 unified cost model. - Define a request-migration contract: eligible models/backends, pause point, minimal request + KV migration metadata, and an explicit terminal error when migration is unsupported or the snapshot is incomplete (consistent with Issue 4's "no execution on incomplete intermediate state"). - Integrate behind a flag with vLLM engine snapshot/restore or KV-transfer APIs as they become available; do not build a private engine protocol. - Re-baseline usage accounting on resume (migrated tokens count once; prompt/completion attribution preserved). - Observe and report: migration attempts, success rate, tokens saved vs retry, TTTR (time-to-resume). - Fault-injection tests: kill a worker mid-stream under each policy. ### Deliverables - [ ] Migration-vs-retry cost decision document + prototype policy hook. - [ ] Request-migration contract (metadata, eligibility, failure semantics). - [ ] PoC with a vLLM snapshot/restore-capable backend, default off. - [ ] Usage re-baselining rules and tests. - [ ] Fault-injection benchmark comparing retry vs migration (TTTR, tokens recomputed, correctness). ### Acceptance criteria - A worker killed mid-generation yields either a correctly resumed response with consistent token accounting, or an explicit error — never silent corruption or duplicated/dropped content. - Migration is attempted only when the cost model predicts a win; decisions are logged and replayable. - Disabled by default; zero behavior change when off. ### Non-goals - Lossless migration for all models, parallel strategies, or topologies in the first phase. - Migration across incompatible engine versions or adapter sets. - Transparent client-invisible guarantees stronger than at-least-once semantics. - Performance numbers reported by the research papers are not project results. --- ## Dependencies ```text Issue 1: CPU Fast Path Integration ─┐ ├─> Issue 3: Agent-aware Scheduling Issue 2: Exact KV Routing ──────────┤ │ └─> Issue 5: Router HA │ └─> Issue 4: E/P/D reuses token/block and load foundations Issue 6: API Compatibility is independent; router-side count_tokens (stretch) reuses the Issue 1 tokenizer. Issue 7: SLO-Based Autoscaling reuses Issue 1 benchmarks, Issue 2 metrics, and P/D calibration; independent of Issues 3–6. Issue 8: Request Migration is exploratory; it reuses the Issue 2 cost model and depends on engine-side snapshot/restore and KV-transfer primitives. ``` ## References ### CPU-side inference fast path - [SMG: The Case for Disaggregating CPU from GPU in LLM Serving](https://pytorch.org/blog/lightseek-smg/) ### Exact KV-aware routing - [NVIDIA Dynamo Router Overview](https://docs.nvidia.com/dynamo/dev/knowledge-base/modular-components/router/overview) ### Agent/program-aware scheduling - [ThunderAgent: A Simple, Fast and Program-Aware Agentic Inference System](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.13692) - [Continuum: Multi-Turn LLM Agent Scheduling with KV Cache TTL](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.02230) - [Pythia: Exploiting Workflow Predictability for Efficient Agent-Native LLM Serving](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.25899) ### E/P/D routing - [SGLang EPD Router CI Run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/21357413504) - [SGLang EPD Router umbrella PR #15683](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/15683) - [vLLM EPD Tracker #52409](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/52409) ### Router high availability - [SMG High Availability](https://smg-project.github.io/smg/concepts/architecture/high-availability/) - [llm-d Router HA Modes](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d-router/blob/main/config/charts/README.md) ### API compatibility - [vLLM Anthropic Messages API serving handler](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/stable/api/vllm/entrypoints/anthropic) - [vLLM feature request: Anthropic `/v1/messages` support](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/21313) - [vLLM Rust-frontend RFC: Anthropic Messages API](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/47753) - # Phase26 — Support Hub & Conversation Management

**Implementation-ready specification. All D1–D40 decisions and amendments are ratified; the founder confirmed the testing approach.**

Support Hub is one cohesive Asym surface with shared native CRM context and correctly authorized owner actions. This specification preserves the complete email/intake/work lifecycle, private collaboration, drafts and reading preferences, contextual guidance, safe file reading and recoverable Unwanted/future-mail holding journeys.

**Start with the user-story book**, then follow its stable US26/REQ26/AC26 identifiers into the detailed requirement volumes. The glossary fixes domain language; OpenSpec carries observable behavior, design and the unchecked implementation/qualification checklist. The source trace records every captured section's authority and disposition.

The full package contains **217 independently verifiable user stories, 2,210 detailed requirement definitions, 717 main OpenSpec scenarios, and all additional exact proof/operating-control suites**. It covers **all 40 ratified decisions**, including D27-C, D29-X01 and every accepted correction. Numerical limits, state/audience/source rules, failure recovery and release gates remain binding.

**Email Studio/P17** owns governed reusable content, canonical authoring and whole-message preparation. **P6** owns actual communication, provider evidence and recovery. **Support** owns human work, source-specific intent and private drafting; canonical intake owns receiving and held-mail decisions. CRM and giving/care domains retain their own truth, permissions and mutations. These seams are specified throughout the requirements, not left as integration assumptions.

**Confirmed proof approach:** real authenticated Support/API and canonical intake/job boundaries on disposable local Supabase; focused actual database permission/concurrency/migration proof; and full Playwright journeys on that same backend. Existing frameworks are reused and real-provider qualification stays separate.

No feature implementation or implementation-ticket graph is included. Specification/documentary validation has passed; product runtime, provider, accessibility, intended-user and release evidence remains required before activation. Local formal/OpenSpec mirrors are validated; this publication is the complete issue-tracker specification and does not claim a source PR.
