items.title: private-beta tracking: tortoise P0/P1 waves, owner decisions, epic status, and WIP
items.body:
<!-- beta-tracking -->
# The tortoise path — **four stages, in this order** (owner, 2026-11-09)

**Owner ruling, verbatim:** *"1. get to private beta (so all the issues needed for that, also ensuring they're labelled p0 or p1 so the auto dispatch prioritises them) 2. any issues and work needed for the venture studio design partner (they record meetings and feed it to an extractor that needs to work for meeting transcripts…) 3. complete any remaining issues that will improve longmem eval directly … so that means also making sure they're marked in the tracking issue as the next wave(s) following private-beta ones 4. run benchmarks for longmemeeval and also for reasoning (the gbrain ones we already setup)"*

**And the ordering constraint that governs stage 4:** *"the issues we filed that affect longmem eval need to be finished before the benchmark, as otherwise we're benchmarking over something that we know is broken and know how it's broken and just needs a fix from us."*

**So: wave 3 gates wave 4.** The benchmark is a *measurement of a known-good state*, not a way to discover the state.

---

## ⛔ STAGE 1 — PRIVATE BETA: the set, stated so it can be counted

The beta is the P0/P1 set. **Re-measured 2026-11-13 by label: P0 6 · P1 23 = 29 open** (this line previously read *P0 10 · P1 17 = 27*; the P0 half was 4 CLOSED issues and the P1 half was short). Each is either *beta work*, *a decision waiting on the owner*, or *mis-filed into the wrong wave* — the table says which.

### P0 — 6 open
| issue | what it actually is | wave |
|---|---|---|
| `#5087` | **epic** Extractor v4, the selective write path (S0→S6) — 19/27 children closed | 1 (children) |
| `#5095` | **lane** L3 extractor pipeline body — 3 of its 4 issues closed, the fourth's PR landed | 1 → **verify + close** |
| `#7879` | **epic** the Postgres record — 23/36 children closed | 1 (children) |
| `#7949` | **epic** v4 CAPSTONE, the end-to-end proof (E1–E6) — 3/12 children closed | 1 |
| `#10977` | tracking: making the hosted graph usable — "the three things nobody owns" | 1 |
| `#11609` | **the live surface is 72 tools / 150 methods against an approved 27 / 40** | 1 |
| `#12047` | **P0 NEW — entity resolution does not exist and the queue reports a false clean.** `list_dedup_candidates(candidate_type='entity')` returns `[]` from a hard-coded stub, so "are there duplicate entities?" answers **none** when the truth is **cannot answer**; `#783` was closed COMPLETED on an acceptance criterion naming `entity_resolver.py`, a file that has never existed in git. Measured damage: one person under five Subject names, one role under three, documents filed as roles, `holdsRole` has zero edges in both hosted graphs, and `default`'s 872 Subjects are 870× kind `other` (453 of them `issue:<repo>#<n>`). **Blocks the graph re-file** — that work multiplies entities on every item | 1 |
| `#12477` | **P0 NEW — the hosted API times out on every request while its health check reports 2/2 passing.** Measured 2026-11-13: `GET /v1/health` / 1-row `GET /v1/points` / `POST /v1/objects` all time out (30-45 s), MCP returns `-32009 wait budget exceeded`, an in-process write hung past 300 s — while the control plane answers instantly and `flyctl` reports `2/2 checks passing` on a `shared-cpu-2x:4096MB` box that restarted at 17:53Z, with vector/FTS queries blowing a 500 ms budget at 1.5-3.9 s. **Blocks the private-beta dogfood** — the clean-graph migration cannot start until a write completes | 1 |

> **📌 Board edit 2026-11-11** — added `#11089` (P1, the `#5090` capstone) and `#4333` (P2, deliberately out of the beta set) to this table, and refreshed the `#5090` row. **The counts in this section are a MEASUREMENT STAMP, not a live figure** — they were measured by another lane on 2026-11-11 and several rows have since closed; re-measure before quoting them.

### P1 — 23 open, split by what they are *for*
| issue | subject | wave |
|---|---|---|
| `#5333` | design(extractor): the destructive half of G5 — may any pass remove/archive an existing fact? **DECIDED, needs the capstone** | 1 |
| `#10360` | extractor: no mechanical enforcement of the verbatim state-value guarantee | 1 |
| `#11002` | extractor: the eight steps actually — bounded re-narrate, S4 gap-filling misplaced. ⚠️ **Its blocker is now cleared:** the ADD-capable stage landed (`#11534` → `#11554`), which is exactly the successor S4's removal requires. The owner question was **withdrawn** 2026-11-07 — the repo's own ordering obligation decides it (build the successor, prove the merge property, then delete `run_s4`) | 1 |
| ✅ **`#11237` — LANDED 2026-11-10 (`#11548`)** | extractor: the relations channel's **write path**. It also **closed the wiring gap** I reported on 2026-11-07: `tortoise/relation_write.py` now calls `plan_hierarchy_edges` (`:53`, `:589`, `:631`) and writes the pack-declared structural hierarchy edges, so a capture **can** produce them. `#11001`'s "no production call site" finding is **false on today's main** and was corrected there and here | 1 |
| ✅ **`#11083` — CLOSED 2026-11-10** | packs: per-pack relation census + the ruled vocabulary. **Landed via `#11543`** (census artifact + `tools/pack_relation_census.py` on `main`) and the pm relations resolved (`blocks`+`dependsOn`+`direction: "<-"`, `partOfSprint`+`hasPart`, `assignedTo`+`managedBy`, `onBoard` kept as `declarationOnly` with the view reason). `funds` stayed a **label**; `produces` became a **meaning** (`<-`, IMPL) because a direction has to be recorded. ⚠️ **One residual, owed and NOT done:** `E6` is still not registered in `docs/evidence/7949-capstone/PRE-REGISTRATION.md` — the sixth acceptance row has no bar yet | 1 |
| `#11534` | extractor: the ADD-capable stage must reach PARTIAL gaps | 1 |
| `#11673` | **register `E6`** — the sixth capstone row the owner created on 2026-11-05 has no bar in `PRE-REGISTRATION.md`. ⚠️ Not a doc edit: `REQUIRED_CRITERIA` in `tools/capstone_preregistration_check.py` must gain `E6` in the same change, and the registration commit must be strictly older than any scored log. Bar proposed: **unbound-and-unexplained declared relations = 0**, denominator 42 (36 relations + 6 hierarchy paths), with the `written` column *reported beside* — not the bar, because `A1` already measures the written graph | 1 | ✅ **implemented in PR #11688** (head `41550c65a9`, MERGEABLE): `E6` is required for the **record** (`REQUIRED_CRITERIA`), recognised by the scorer (`RECOGNISED_CRITERIA`), and **not** part of the close — `V9`/`--require-green` stays `E1..E5`, per the `A1`–`A5` precedent (*"a registration may not turn a row into a gate before anyone has measured it"*). ⚠️ **The head's checks are mostly `cancelled`** (a push landed while CI was running, which cancels the queue position) — it needs a **fresh run** before the rail will accept it |
| `#11695` | **nothing can emit an `E6` verdict**, so no **scored run can produce a complete record** (`E6` is required by `REQUIRED_CRITERIA`). ⚠️ **Not** a closing blocker: the close is five rows. The fix is a producer reading the existing `docs/evidence/11083/pack-relation-census.json` — it must **not** re-open the closing set | 1 |
| `#11000` | packs: **`subclassOf` never widens — the expansion loop drops the parent** | 1 (**a pack that cannot widen connects nothing**) |
| `#4051` | quota: the commit lane's only org-limit gate was the session cap | 1 (revenue guard) |
| `#10175` | ops(capture): the hosted capture cap is HELD deliberately — never override | 1 (standing rule, not work) |
| `#8486` | **Run LongMemEval-S** (never executed; no comparable number exists) | **4 — this IS the benchmark** |
| `#2513` | multi-session retrieval evidence surface — the dominant QA loss (53 % of misses) | **3** |
| `#8488` | context-enriched embeddings **+ BM25 lexical** — the two signals we lack | **3** |
| `#10538` | time-aware query expansion — the fix for the 53 %-of-misses part | **3** |
| `#2281` | ask/answer surface reads ingest-time-distilled knowledge (ontology-organised) with raw-turn fallback | **3** |
| `#9097` | measure(ask): seal and publish the Q3 exit measurement | **4 (it is a measurement)** |
| `#11460` | re-register the ask exit pre-registration to the owner-ruled DeepSeek judge | **4 (prerequisite of #9097)** |
| **`#4333`** | **storage-architecture owner** — node volume + true per-node cost. **`P2-moderate`, so it is deliberately OUTSIDE the beta set** (the set is P0/P1) and is listed here only so nobody re-files it as a `#5090` child: it is the *owner* of the storage question, not a child of the vector layer | **3 (not beta)** |
| `#11395` | tracking(5090): the S3 vector-removal / surface-approval call has no successor issue | **3** |
| `#10656` | **credential provenance (REOPENED 2026-11-11** — it had been closed COMPLETED by a PR that never touched it; all three claims re-measured true at `origin/main` `372f926cd9`: `:1506` writes `<cwd>/.tortoise`, `:2133` ranks it above the global store, `:1662-3` is a non-atomic `write_text`+`chmod`) — plaintext key in a working tree, at a precedence that shadows the user-global store. **Both halves are lane decisions, not owner ones** (contradiction test 2026-11-11: no recorded decision requires the cwd location — it arrived with `61f32e1ce4` and `#1708` moved `signup`/`recover` to the global store without ever ruling on `init`). (a) atomic write + FIFO guard **dispatched**; (c) write to the user-global store with `<cwd>/.tortoise` kept read-compatible **decided and queued behind (a)** — same function, so one lane at a time | 1 |
| `#11912` | **`doctor` cannot see half the product** — 8 local checks, **zero** credential or hosted ones, so a revoked key reads `8 pass, 0 fail` (measured on this box). #10655 built `config show` (the offline reporter); this is the first-run surface that should REACH it. **Dispatched** | 1 |
| `#12060` | **P1 NEW — per-kind guards: redirect mis-filed writes with an AX contract, not a refusal.** Every core kind gets a deterministic, token-free guard: accept / **redirect** / refuse — a guard may never refuse a case whose right home is known. Shipped with a fixed AX message shape (what changed, why, the exact override, how to undo) plus a `kind_redirect` field so agents branch on data not English, an `intent="as_declared"` override that records that it fired, and redirect counters. **Cross-pack resolved:** targets are core / own namespace / `depends_on` only; `pack validate` refuses a bad reference (fail at install, not at write); at write time a missing target makes the guard **abstain** — never reject, because a write must not depend on which packs are installed. Packs declare guards **optionally**; `_template` carries a worked example. **Prevents the re-file from re-creating the 453 issue-as-Subject + 870 `other` nodes** | 1 |

### ✅ DEFINITION — UNCHANGED, AND NOT MINE TO MOVE (owner, 2026-11-09)
> **"the cut line depends on what's needed not a fixed number — focus on advancing towards the private-beta while I handle what 'done' is and my definition hasn't changed."**

**So: beta ships when the open `P0-blocker` + `P1-severe` issues are merged and closed. There is no A/B/C, no relabelling, no frozen set.** The options previously written here are withdrawn — they were me asking the owner to solve a *queue-dynamics* problem that is the fleet's job to solve by closing issues.

**What that makes true immediately:**
- **The six P1s filed yesterday are BETA WORK, not a post-beta wave.** `#11641 #11642 #11646 #11653 #11654 #11656` join Stage 1 and get dispatched like any other beta item.
- **The P1 count rising is not an argument to narrow the definition — it is a dispatch backlog.** Report it as such: *N new beta items, N dispatched, N unassigned.*
- **Nothing is relabelled.** Recent additions to the set stay `P1-severe`; `#11382` is proposed for `P1-severe` and `#8713` already carries `P2-moderate`.

### Where the set stands (measured 2026-11-10)
```
P0-blocker 10 · P1-severe 22 · closed yesterday 27, of which 2 were P0/P1 (#11534, #9664)
NEW P1s yesterday (all beta work): #11641 #11642 #11646 #11653 #11654 #11656
```

### Where the set stands (measured 2026-11-11, after the #10655 onboarding lane)

```
P0-blocker 6 · P1-severe 22 (MEASURED; 2 of the 22 are this lane's: #10656 reopened, #11912 filed)
NEW P1s (beta work, both dispatched): #10656 #11912
NEW P2s (NOT beta-gating, labelled P2-moderate, rows below): #10657 (DECIDED 2026-11-11, dispatched) · #10741 (dispatched with #10656)
OWNER DECISIONS OWED BY THIS LANE: 0 (both items previously parked on the owner were decided on 2026-11-11 with the contradiction test recorded on each issue)
```

**The #10655 lane, closed out (verified 2026-11-11, not just merged):** `#10655` is CLOSED and its artifact is
on `origin/main` — `tortoise config show [--json]` present, `tests/test_cli_config_show.py` = **205 passed**,
census + config suites 55 passed, documented in `docs/quickstart-cloud.md`. Two follow-up PRs improved it after
merge (`#10857` collapsed-DSN redaction). The lane also filed `#10656` (above) and `#10657` (decided), and
commented the measured evidence on `#9548` (the record DSN is unarmed — the real `record-reconcile` blocker)
and `#10582` (the hosted API was **up** on re-probe: 12/12 x 200 in 0.2-1.6 s; the "never returns HTTP" reading
was a cold-start stall, i.e. a measurement artifact).

### P2 — tracked here, NOT beta-gating (the beta set is P0 + P1 only, per the ruling above)

⚠️ `P2-moderate` has **205 open** repo-wide (measured 2026-11-11) — this table lists ONLY the two that belong to
the #10655 onboarding/credential-provenance lane. It is not a P2 backlog.

| issue | what it is | state |
|---|---|---|
| `#10657` | a graph-scoped key cannot learn which graph it is bound to — no key-authed self-description surface (`GET /v1/team` refuses it by design, C5 #2114) | **DECIDED 2026-11-11** (RFC 7662 / AWS `GetCallerIdentity` / GitHub `GET /user` convergence; C5 explicitly NOT relaxed) → route + inventory + `config show --verify` **dispatched** |
| `#10741` | `init --api-key` blocks forever on a FIFO at `<cwd>/.tortoise` (reads `exists()`, writes block) | same function as `#10656` → **dispatched in that lane** (non-regular-file guard) |


---|---|---|---|
| `#8488` | **BM25 lexical: LIVE** · context-enriched embeddings: **implemented, `TORTOISE_CONTEXT_ENRICH` fail-safe OFF** | arm or decline · cost measurement · per-category report | 1 decision + 1 measurement |
| `#10538` | **fully implemented** in `tortoise/time_aware.py` | the dense-anchor branch is **`time_aware: False`** · prove it via `#9097`'s re-run | 1 arming + 1 measurement |
| `#2281` | built | both open children are **measurements** | **0 build** |
| `#2513` | unit 1 = `#10538`; re-injection landed | 2 open children still real (`#11382` PRESENT-unpinned, `#8713` falsified); `#10819` **verified FIXED and closed** | ~2 bugs |
| `#5090` | **CLOSED 2026-11-12 — 12/12 children closed**; `#11086` and `#11641` both CLOSED, `#11642` landed via `#11660` | `#4333` storage-architecture owner only (P2, separate track) — **capstone `#11089` CLOSED 2026-11-12** | **1 open in beta (`#11089`) + 1 outside it (`#4333`)** |

**Stage 3 is days, not weeks — because the fixes are already written and switched off.** So (A) costs little and keeps the beta definition intact. **Still the owner's word to confirm, and nothing has been relabelled.**

### ⛔ AND THE NUMBER THAT MATTERS MORE THAN ANY OF THE ABOVE: **P1 grew 17 → 22 today**
```
P0 open: 10 (unchanged)   P1 open: **17 → 22**   issues closed today: 27 — of which only **2 were P0/P1**
6 NEW P1s filed today (#11641 #11642 #11646 #11653 #11654 #11656), all found by lanes doing real work
```
**"All P0/P1" is a moving target: the fleet is filing real Severe findings faster than it lands fixes.** That — not the size of any single wave — is the strongest reason to state an explicit **cut line** for the beta: a sha, a date, or a named issue set frozen at that moment. Otherwise the beta definition cannot be completed, only approached.

---

## STAGE 2 — ⏸ AFTER PRIVATE BETA, NOT IN IT: the venture-studio design partner

> **⛔ DO NOT LABEL `#2696` P0 OR P1 UNTIL THE PRIVATE-BETA SET IS COMPLETE, AND DO NOT DISPATCH IT.**
> The order is: **finish the private-beta set first.** A `P0`/`P1` label on this would make the automated harness pick it up and pull it into the beta wave — which is the opposite of the ruling. **It stays `P2-moderate`.** The ruling is: *"P2 for now, prioritise to P0 for the design partner after we complete the requirements for the private-beta"* (owner, 2026-11-09).
> **This section exists so the work is not lost, not so it is started.**

**The issue exists: `#2696` (currently `P2-moderate`) — "epic: meeting-ingestion pipeline for venture-builder customers — meeting-attunement".**
Its subject is exactly the partner's need: a meeting *is* a session, but its structure is different (speakers, agenda, decisions, action items, cross-meeting continuity) from an agent session's (tool calls, file edits, errors fixed).

**The question you raised — one universal extractor, or modular variants?** The evidence we have says **modularise the seam, keep one extractor**:
- The extractor is already staged S0→S6 (`#5087`) with a per-stage contract, and `#11484` derives the structural write vocabulary **per graph** from core + packs. That is already a per-domain configuration seam.
- A "meeting variant" that is a *prompt-and-vocabulary* variant costs little; a forked pipeline costs a second capstone and a second set of guarantees (verbatim retention `#10360`, value survival `#10989`).
- **So: one extractor, one proof, two profiles.** Stage 2's real work is (a) a meeting profile — speaker turns, decisions, action items — as a pack/vocabulary, and (b) the ingestion path from a transcript source to the extractor's door.

**This stage also carries `#2696` from P2 → the label that makes auto-dispatch pick it up *after* the beta set.** That relabel is part of the same decision as (A)/(B)/(C) above.

**⚠️ Prerequisite for iterating the profile at all — `#11661` (`P2-moderate`, deliberately NOT a beta item).** We record *which source version* produced a fact and never *which extractor* did, so after a profile change there is no way to tell which already-ingested meetings need re-extraction: every tuning round either re-extracts the whole corpus or silently serves output from a prompt that no longer exists, and neither failure is visible in the graph. Filed with its design — `extractorId` (a deliberately-bumped profile identity) + `extractorDigest` (a hash of the compiled prompt/vocabulary, for explainability), carried on the `extractedFrom` link exactly as `sourceVersion` already is, plus a third `unknown` state so pre-existing nodes are neither blessed as fresh nor re-extracted wholesale. **Do not pull it into the private-beta wave** — it is not a launch requirement. **Promote it to `P1` at the moment meeting-profile iteration starts**, because that is when its absence stops being a nuisance and becomes a correctness risk (`D13` draft → run → look → refine is the working method, so iteration starts immediately after stage 2 begins).

**The decision itself is recorded on `#2696` (comment `6752567775`) and `#11081` (`6752174448`, corrected by `6752335134`):** one extractor, no fork, meetings as connector #4 conforming to the registry-free mapper contract; the profile is a **shape** mapping (speaker turn · section · action item · decision · status update · blocker · open question), not a source-branded prompt set; no depth/cheap mode; no per-source field-cost registry.

## STAGE 3 — THE LONG-MEMORY FIXES THE BENCHMARK WOULD OTHERWISE MEASURE AS BROKEN

**The organising rule for this stage, and it is the whole point of it:** *an issue whose build landed is not done — it is at the "decide, or experiment and decide from the results" step.* **Building a retrieval improvement, leaving it switched off, and abandoning it is the worst outcome, and it is the current state of two of these.** Every row below therefore names its **decision home** and its **next action**, not just its subject.

| issue | state measured on `main` (2026-11-09) | next action | decision home |
|---|---|---|---|
| `#8488` (P1, **`owner-decision`**) | **lexical/BM25: LIVE** (on by default) · **context-enriched embeddings: implemented, `TORTOISE_CONTEXT_ENRICH` fail-safe OFF** | experiment (on/off on a fixed corpus, cost per chunk) → decide → per-category report | issue `#8488` + **lane `DECISION #8488`** (workspace `29C008AA`). ⭐ **Research appendix: `#8488` comment `6755095497`** (competitors, the quote-vs-paraphrase reconciliation, what we already ship) — **read before re-researching** |
| `#10538` (P1, **`owner-decision`** added 2026-11-09) | **fully implemented** in `tortoise/time_aware.py`; the dense-anchor branch is **`time_aware: bool = False`** | run `#9097`'s Q3 measurement over the expanded pipeline (`recall_all@5`, multi-session must move off **0.45**) → decide | issue `#10538` + the **same** lane as `#8488` (both flags decided together — deciding them apart yields a benchmark that measures neither) |
| `#2281` (P1) | built; both open children are **measurements** (`#9097`, `#11460`) | measurement only | issue `#2281` |
| `#2513` (P1, epic-scope) | scope unit 1 = `#10538`; re-injection `#10540` landed | **verify its three open children (below), then re-scope what is left** | issue `#2513` |
| `#5090` (P1, epic) | **CLOSED 2026-11-12** — 12/12 children closed; DoD **3 MET / 1 PARTIAL** (row 4's `PARTIAL` is an INSTRUMENT limit — the probe prints `implemented: UNMEASURED`) | **capstone `#11089` CLOSED**; `#4333` is P2 and a separate storage-architecture question (P2) |
| `#11395` | tracking issue, no code | folds into `#5090` | `#5090` |
| `#11682` → **`#11739`** (**P1**) | **`#11682` CLOSED — two halves landed.** Lexical: `#11706` put `quote` in the Point FULLTEXT field set (`sparse.POINT_INDEX_TEXT_FIELDS`), with the two-field index migrated. Quote-half of the embedding text: `#11805` → `0bdb08dbdb` (`tortoise/embed_compose.py`, gated OFF by `TORTOISE_COMPOSED_EMBED_TEXT`; attested by the existing hash so **#4194 holds as written**; replay restores rather than recomposes — verified against a real journal). **`#11739` OPEN — the NAMES half.** Built and tested but **deliberately NOT wired**: `create_point` writes **no `about*` edge** (they are minted later by `backfill_about_entities` and the capture's entity link), so a created point has **zero resolved neighbours** and composing names from string props would attest a relation the graph does not have. | remaining: the **recompose seam** that runs once the edges exist · the **delete-time redaction sweep** · **the ship-gate** (`0.89` per-subject raw-vs-composed discrimination **+** rank-distribution/displacement **+** `cross_lens` false-proposal). ⚠️ The gate is **not** in the landed tests (`grep -c '0\.89|NEAR_DUPLICATE|displac'` → 0), and the **`quote` population rate is still unmeasured** | `#11739` + `#11682` |
| `#2518` (**P2**) | **built, switched OFF** — `entity_key_expansion: bool = False`. Fact-augmented index keys; one of the three fixes arXiv 2410.10813 measures (+9.4% recall@k, +5.4% accuracy) | **built-and-off is precisely the state this stage exists to catch** — decide, or experiment and decide | issue `#2518` |
| `#2516` (**P2**) | per-category `evidence_recall@5` + official `recall_all@5` gates — **the reporting surface** | **arguably FIRST in this stage** — without it the run cannot express a per-category result at all (`recall_all@5` is identically 0 for questions needing >5 evidence pieces) | issue `#2516` |
| `#2683` (**P2**) | evidence-assembly Slice A — dedup + cap + order of the retrieval package (the reader window) | QA accuracy — wave 3 | issue `#2683` |
| `#2684` (**P2**) | evidence-assembly Slice B — verbatim value-spans on value-bearing points | **verbatim/raw class** — the class the fidelity literature says is decisive — wave 3 | issue `#2684` |
| `#8775` (**P2**) | `_RE_RECENCY`'s bare `latest` guard rejects a genuine interval question | **temporal-reasoning** class — wave 3 | issue `#8775` |

⚠️ **GAP CLOSED (2026-11-09).** `#8486`'s own gate ruling names **eight** issues as *"every open P0/P1/P2 we know affects this eval"*. Six were on this board; **`#2518`, `#2516`, `#2683`, `#2684`, `#8775` were missing entirely** and are added above, together with `#11682` (filed this session as `#8488` scope 1's delivery vehicle). `#11070` is the eighth and is **CLOSED**, so it needs no row. **The benchmark's precondition is now stated in one place** — it was previously enforced only by a comment on `#8486` and contradicted by silence here. See `#8488` comment `6754710803` for the evidence.


**⛔ PRIORITY — these six stay `P2` on purpose, and this is the rule (owner, 2026-11-09 / 2026-11-10).** *"P1 would mean making it a requirement before we launch the private beta."* **None of these are beta requirements.** They are Stage 3 — **after** the private-beta set is merged and closed, **before** the benchmark runs. Their wave is carried by this row, not by a priority label.

**They may be re-prioritised to `P1` once the private-beta set is complete**, if the owner then decides they are needed. Until that point a `P1` label on any of them would make the automated harness pull it into the beta wave — which is exactly what Stage 2's `⛔ DO NOT LABEL` rule exists to prevent for `#2696`. **Leave them `P2`; re-prioritise after beta, not before.**

⚠️ **CONSEQUENCE TO RESOLVE — `#11682` is currently `P1-severe`.** By this board's own definition (*"beta ships when the open `P0-blocker` + `P1-severe` issues are merged and closed"*) that makes it **beta work**, which contradicts the owner's stated intent for this work. **Flagged for the owner's call: leave `P1` and treat the composer as a beta requirement, or drop it to `P2` and let this Stage 3 row sequence it.** Not changed by this edit — relabelling is the owner's.

### `#2513`'s three open children — **unlabelled, and NOT previously tracked here. That was a gap in this board.**
| issue | subject | current labels | **proposed** |
|---|---|---|---|
| `#11382` | the seed key is stripped and the graph group key is racy on the session-re-injection path | **none** (a merged PR `#11365` references it — so the fix may have landed) | **`P1-severe`**, Stage 3 |
| `#10819` | the census window is not narrowed on the R6 rerank DEGRADE arms | **none** (merged `#11212` references it) | **`P2-moderate`**, Stage 3 |
| `#8713` | the C4 re-injection arm's pre-registered surface census is **falsified** | `complexity:standard`, `team:epistemic-team` — **no P** | **`P2-moderate`**, Stage 3 |

⚠️ **All three have zero comments and merged PRs that reference them — the "fix landed, issue never closed" pattern.** Their first step is therefore **verification, not coding**: a lane confirms whether the merged work addressed each, then closes or re-scopes it. **The proposed labels above await the owner's approval; nothing has been applied.**

**These are the ones we already know are broken and know how they are broken.** Running LongMemEval before them measures our own known defects.

## STAGE 4 — THE BENCHMARKS
| what | issue | state |
|---|---|---|
| LongMemEval-S (end-to-end QA) | `#8486` | **never executed** — no comparable number exists |
| the ask exit measurement | `#9097` (+ `#11460` re-registration) | pre-registration owed |
| **reasoning (gbrain)** | `#1402` epic agent-reasoning eval battery · `#2080` epic gbrain learnings · `#2107` capstone | partially set up |
| battery wiring | `#2800`, `#11056` | in progress |

**Rule for this stage: a benchmark result is only published with (a) the sha, (b) the corpus hash, and (c) the profile/config it ran under.** A number without those three is not a measurement.

---

## Working rules (learned the hard way; all measured)

- **One lane per item; the terminal milestone is LANDED + CLOSED**, not "a PR opened".
- **Closure requires proven criteria** — a closing keyword only when the last criterion is proven beside the measurement.
- **A review lane records at the FINAL head.** Push first, then review, then record, then **read back** `~/.pi/agent/reviews/…json` and assert `head_sha` matches. A record bound to a stale sha is indistinguishable from no record — three died that way on 2026-11-09.
- **`mergeable` AND `mergeStateStatus` are both caches.** `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main <head>` is the only authority; acting on a phantom `DIRTY` moves heads and destroys reviews.
- **Never edit a PR body after a review is recorded** — it wipes the attestation.
- **Never push to a PR whose CI is queued or running** — it cancels that run.
- **Pre-flight before dispatch**: `collision_preflight.py <N>` + `who-is-on.sh <N>`.
- **Keep advanced work.** Adopt and drive existing work to completion; re-do only where it is genuinely off, and file a follow-up rather than starting over silently.

## Instruments (do not re-derive)
`~/.pi/agent/state/P01-PRMAP.md` · `~/.pi/agent/state/WORKSTATUS.md` · `uv run python tools/surface-target-check.py` · `tools/surface_manifest.py check` · the `tracking-table` comment this issue carries (posted every beat).

items.title: MCP tools: подключение, исполнение и долгие вызовы без активной модели

milestone.title: M4 — API, tools и приложения
milestone.description: Самостоятельный authenticated API, совместимый inference subset, tool continuation, MCP и SDK. Интеграции с внешним контроллером и приложением Задачера без передачи provider keys и без второго orchestration engine.

items.body:
<!-- ariel-plan:v1:mcp-tools -->

## Цель и граница

Предоставить Ariel универсальную возможность подключать разрешённые MCP-серверы, обнаруживать инструменты, выполнять вызовы и возвращать результаты. Это применимо к файлам, вычислениям, API и генерации изображений/постеров (#109/#110), без встроенной редакционной логики или адаптеров соцсетей.

Уточнение 2026-10-16: **MCP — исполнительная возможность воркера, а не исключительно возможность приложения-потребителя.** Вызов может прийти от модели через #53 либо напрямую от авторизованного клиента. Для исполнения уже заданного MCP tool не требуется запуск LLM.

Разрешённый внешний инструмент может иметь любые явно допущенные эффекты, включая HTTP-запись. Это не делает знание площадки, расписание публикаций или контентную кампанию частью Ariel. Известен исполнитель, конкретный target и технические ограничения; бизнес-решение остаётся у вызывающей стороны.

## Подключение и каталог

- Раздельные профили локального stdio server и удалённого Streamable HTTP. Версии протокола, auth, методы и transport capabilities проверяются, не предполагаются по названию SDK.
- Configured, discovered, approved и running — разные состояния. Запуск сервера/установка зависимостей не следуют автоматически из импорта конфигурации; approved command/endpoint, окружение и provenance фиксируются.
- Разрешения на server и отдельные tools выдаются через #17. Discovery, tool annotations и prompts сервера сами по себе не grants. Схемы фиксируются на attempt; endpoint/catalog/schema drift не расширяет доступ после reconnect, reload или смены cwd.
- Credentials и контексты разделены по клиенту, principal, профилю и generation; публичный UI/модель не получают секреты. Файловые roots не подменяют реальную изоляцию #13, включая дочерние процессы локального MCP.
- Один каталог и execution owner по #53: native tools и MCP могут доставлять одну capability, но не регистрируют и не исполняют её дважды. Application-owned tool не запускается локально без явного назначения исполнителя. Runtime-internal MCP без необходимого pre-action контроля объявляется limited/unsupported для строгого профиля.
- MCP resources/prompts квалифицируются отдельно. Прочитанный prompt/resource — недоверенные данные, не разрешение выполнить команды или вызвать модель.

## Вызов и результаты

`McpInvocationBinding` связывает client/job/attempt, originating tool_call_id при наличии, server/profile identity, protocol/transport revision, exact tool/schema/args digest, credential/policy generation, deadline/budget и operation ID. JSON-RPC request ID не заменяет durable operation identity.

Сначала сохранить intent → проверить текущие grants → выполнить → сохранить outcome/artifacts → доставить результат. Не создавать второй JobStore, scheduler или agent loop.

Возвращать bounded text/structured results, изображения/аудио и разрешённые resource refs через #33. Проверять объявленную output schema и отличать tool error от protocol/transport error. Большие binary данные сохраняются как artifacts, не копируются целиком в модель/поток событий. Получение remote URL или file URI не разрешает автоматически его скачать либо прочитать локальный путь; нужны отдельные проверки доступа, размеров и origin.

## Долгие инструменты без обращения к planner

- Интеграция с #103: Ariel самостоятельно ждёт локальный процесс, обычный длительный call либо поддержанное сервером async/task выполнение; прогресс направляется клиенту, не модели. При прямом API-вызове модель вообще не участвует.
- Закрепить поколение MCP. Для MCP 2026-07-28 отдельно квалифицировать расширение `io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks`; task/result/input-required обрабатываются согласно согласованному контракту. Не смешивать его с экспериментальными Tasks 2025-11-25 или придумывать методы из другой версии. Существующие комментарии о совместимости поколений и MRTR сохраняют силу.
- Task handle/status/result сохраняются вместе с principal/profile binding; poll interval, TTL, отмена и result retrieval учитываются по реальным capabilities. У обычного вызова без task/resume нельзя обещать восстановление после разрыва — нужен честный unknown outcome и запрещён blind replay внешнего эффекта.
- В требуемом режиме ожидания запрещены скрытые вызовы планирующей модели, в том числе MCP sampling. Не рекламировать неподдерживаемую sampling capability; server request возвращает поддержанный отказ/needs_input, либо требуется отдельно одобренная смена режима. Elicitation направляется в существующий #43/#17, не означает автоматический допуск.
- Auth refresh, reconnect, progress и polling сами по себе не инициируют inference. Внешний MCP tool может использовать собственную модель/платный API: это отдельный исполнитель и учёт, не обещание отсутствия всех provider costs.
- Cancel/revoke блокирует новые действия; локальный disconnect не равен remote cancel. При lost ACK/restart сверять исходный outcome, не создавать новый call вслепую. Повторная доставка результата не повторяет tool; недоступный planner оставляет result_ready.

## Критерии готовности

- [ ] Read-only MCP fixture работает через один qualified runtime и прямой API без модели.
- [ ] Fake generate_image/render_poster возвращает файл/structured result; #109/#110 используют тот же каталог, permissions, Job/Attempt и artifacts.
- [ ] Долгий fake MCP call/task с управляемыми часами: ноль model requests во время ожидания, прогресс доступен клиенту, результат доставлен в исходный tool_call_id.
- [ ] Скрытый sampling, denied tool/endpoint, schema drift, неправильный principal и попытка прочитать чужой artifact отклоняются.
- [ ] Lost ACK/reconnect/restart, task expiry, late callback и cancel race не создают повторный внешний эффект; unsupported resume виден явно.
- [ ] Злоумышленный resource URI, oversized binary и tool error не становятся успешным результатом или неразрешённым чтением.
- [ ] Native/MCP регистрация не удваивает один инструмент; закрытие одной сессии не разрушает чужой разрешённый transport.

## Связи и порядок

- Roadmap: #1. Milestone: **M4 — API, tools и приложения**.
- **Blocked by:** #53, #11 — существующие зависимости сохраняются.
- Связи: #8, #12, #13, #16, #17, #18, #22, #23, #30, #33, #34, #43, #85, #91, #93, #94, #102, #103, #104, #109, #110.
- Контракт и fake stdio/HTTP fixtures можно готовить параллельно. Tasks и дополнительные версии квалифицируются отдельно; обычный безопасный MCP путь не ждёт поддержки всех расширений.
- Нативные GitHub blockers этой правкой не меняются; публичная приёмка не зависит от закрытых исходников.

## Первоисточники

Проверено 2026-10-16, только документация, без live-подключений:
- https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/tools
- https://tasks.extensions.modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/tasks

Предыдущие комментарии о lifecycle, едином каталоге, изоляции, startup policy и совместимости поколений сохраняются. MCP-серверы, генераторы и аккаунты этой правкой не подключаются.

items.title: Design: agent sandboxes on spore.host (spawn sandbox, MCP sandbox tools, Managed Agents worker, hypha)

milestone.title: Post-1.0
milestone.description: Features deferred until after the hardening phase (spore-host/spore-host#644).

items.body:
Design proposal: how spore.host could offer **agent sandboxes** (the category Docker Sandboxes, E2B, Daytona, Modal, Lambda MicroVMs and others sell), and do better for its own audience: GPUs, large memory, data in the user's own AWS account, and hard TTL and cost guarantees. The full research brief is in the first comment. It covers a landscape of about 20 products with sources, a capability map against spawn, design options A–D, phases and experiments. Each claim is tagged [P] primary docs, [3P] third party, [code], EST (estimate) or UNVERIFIED. ## TL;DR 1. **What the market sells.** Nearly every "agent sandbox" is the same thing: a Firecracker microVM, a gVisor container, or a full VM, behind a create/exec/files/snapshot/destroy API. - They start in well under a second to a few seconds, because they restore from snapshots or use warm pools. - They bill per second. - They cap lifetime: 45 min to 24 h on most, 8 h on AWS's two offerings. - They run on the vendor's cloud. - Almost none offer GPUs. Modal and Daytona do. Northflank also claims GPU support [3P]. 2. **The ground shifted in 2026, in two ways.** - **AWS Lambda MicroVMs** went GA on 2026-06-22 [P]. They are Firecracker sandboxes that run **in the customer's own AWS account**, with suspend/resume. Limits: 8 h hard cap, ARM64 only, 16 vCPU / 32 GB at most, and no GPU mentioned. - **EC2 nested virtualization** on C8i/M8i/R8i and some 7th-gen Intel types (announced 2026-02) [P]. Firecracker now runs on ordinary, cheap EC2 instances instead of `.metal`. - Together these remove "your own AWS account" as a unique differentiator for small CPU sandboxes. AWS now sells exactly that. 3. **Claude Managed Agents has a self-hosted sandbox mode** (beta) [P]. A worker inside your infrastructure polls a work queue over outbound HTTPS and runs the agent's tool calls locally. It is already listed with 11 platform guides: Lambda MicroVMs, E2B, Daytona, Modal, Cloudflare, Fly, GKE, Vercel, and others. - The model is almost exactly `spawn pool`: workers in your account pull work from a queue. - This is the cheapest high-leverage integration available to spore.host. 4. **spore.host already has most of a "heavy sandbox"** [code]: - ephemeral EC2 with TTL, cost limit and idle stop, enforced in-instance by a signed `spored`, plus an out-of-band reaper; - truffle sizing, including GPUs, Spot and capacity blocks; - keyless SSM connect; - TaskSpec container runs with `--gpus all`; - SQS worker pools; - S3, EFS and FSx data in the user's account; - an MCP server that can already launch billable tasks behind a mandatory TTL. What it lacks is a **programmatic interactive surface**: exec, file put/get, snapshot/fork, an egress policy, and fast start. Today a sandbox is either a batch task or an SSH session. 5. **Recommendation.** Don't start by building a Firecracker fleet. Build `spawn sandbox`, an agent-facing create/exec/cp/snapshot/destroy surface over EC2 spores (Option A), and expose it through spore-host-mcp (Option C). Ship a **Claude Managed Agents self-hosted worker recipe** on top (Option D1). - Position it as **the sandbox tier incumbents don't serve**: GPUs, big memory, long lifetimes, data in your account, and hard cost/TTL guarantees. - Treat the sub-second tier as a **pluggable backend**: - evaluate Lambda MicroVMs first (buy); - build a nested-virt Firecracker broker (Option B, working name **`hypha`**) only if measurements show it pays off. - Run the de-risking experiments in Part 4 before committing to B. ### 4.2 Phases | Phase | Deliverable | Size | |---|---|---| | **P0: de-risk and decide** (1–2 wks) | Run experiments E1–E3 below. Decide the open questions in 4.4. | S | | **P1: MVP, `spawn sandbox` (Option A1)** | 1. `create / exec / cp / status / extend / destroy`, with exec via SSM and cp via an S3 relay.
2. Egress `none|s3|open` (per-sandbox SG + VPC endpoints).
3. Mandatory TTL **and** cost limit.
4. Reaper-armed precondition.
5. `pkg/sandbox` Go API and Python SDK methods.
6. MCP tools (Option C). | M | | **P1.5: Managed Agents recipe (D1)** | Poller spore plus a per-session sandbox script. Documented and validated on a GPU sandbox reading S3 data. Offer it to Anthropic's platform-guide list. | S | | **P2: v1, fast-enough and forkable** | 1. Pre-baked sandbox AMI (Docker + NVIDIA toolkit + exec agent).
2. Warm/stopped pool claim.
3. `snapshot` / `fork` via AMI.
4. `allow:` egress through the per-account proxy spore.
5. Credential placeholder injection.
6. `--backend lambda-microvm` (Option B′) with reaper coverage for MicroVMs, images and snapshots. | M–L | | **P3: optional, `hypha` (Option B)** | Only if E2 and E3 show:
• Lambda MicroVMs is inadequate (x86, >8 h, FSx mounts, egress, fork, cost at density); **and**
• nested-virt Firecracker hits target latency and density. | L | ### 4.3 First concrete milestone > **`spawn sandbox` A1 + MCP**: > 1. An agent in Claude Code calls `sandbox_create {gpu:1, ttl:"2h", cost_limit:5, egress:"s3", data:["s3://…:ro"]}`. > 2. It runs `nvidia-smi` and a Python script over the mounted dataset via `sandbox_exec`. > 3. It pulls a result file with `sandbox_read_file`, then calls `sandbox_destroy`. > > **Pass criteria:** > - the agent never held AWS keys beyond the local MCP chain; > - the sandbox had no inbound ports and no internet egress; > - the reaper was armed; > - an independent post-run sweep finds zero leaked instances, volumes, SGs, ENIs or instance profiles, and no S3 objects outside the results prefix. ### 4.4 Open questions for the owner 1. **Tenancy.** Sandboxes stay strictly single-account and BYO? Recommendation: yes. A hosted multi-tenant sandbox service would break "data never leaves your account". Any hosted helper must respect the existing cross-account trust constraints: no trusts toward management or internal accounts. 2. **Reaper as a precondition.** Should `sandbox create` hard-require an armed reaper in the target account, or warn plus `--accept-no-backstop`? 3. **MCP spending policy.** The boundary already moved with `spawn_task_run`. Is autonomous sandbox creation acceptable with a mandatory TTL and cost limit plus per-day caps in config? Should GPU sandboxes require an explicit config opt-in? 4. **Egress default.** `none`, `s3`, or `open`? Recommendation: `s3` for data science, with `open` requiring a flag. 5. **Lambda MicroVMs as a backend.** Acceptable to depend on it (ARM64-only, 5 regions, 8 h)? It needs reaper extensions for non-EC2 artifacts. 6. **Managed Agents beta.** Is it acceptable to build a recipe on a beta API (`managed-agents-2026-04-01`)? It is low-cost, because it's a doc plus a script, not core code. 7. **Naming.** Is `hypha` OK for the microVM tier, with `sclerotium` for snapshots and `conidia` for forks? Or should everything live under `spawn sandbox`? 8. **Scope of "fork".** Is a disk-only fork (AMI) enough for v1, or is memory-state fork a requirement? Memory-state fork effectively forces Option B. ## Status - **E1** (EC2 time-to-first-exec) is being run now. Its results will be posted here. - **E2–E4** are specified in the brief, not yet run.

items.title: managed-agent: in a Harness pool, a fire on a Session the draining Harness has released can answer 404 and retire the automation for good

labels.name: status/ready-for-human
labels.description: Specified but requires human judgment to implement; not suitable for an autonomous agent

items.body:
### What happened?

This applies to a Harness pool in which the firing control-plane node sees no reachable, accepting member. A draining Harness can release a Session while the pool still selects that Harness for it. During that window, an automation fire for the Session can reach the draining Harness. By then the Harness has dropped the Session from memory, so it answers `404 hosted_session_not_found`.

The scanner treats that code as "the definition or its Session is gone for good" and retires the definition's mirror. After that:

- no new occurrence is derived for it;
- `GET` reports it retired;
- a revise is refused.

Recreating the automation is the only way back, even though the Session's own record of the definition is still live.

**Reproduced in two parts** at `main` `bfa7a2f52e`. The 404 comes from a scratch IT built on the `HostedHarnessPoolMySqlIT` fixture, with real Harness processes, Spring and MySQL 8.4. The retirement comes from a scratch `AutomationScannerTest` case with a faked 404. The real-process run defines no automation and does not run the scanner.

The IT creates a Session on `pool-a`, so the control plane holds an attachment for it. It then drains `pool-a` through `HarnessPoolConnector.drainInstance`, which marks the member quiescing in the pool at once. (With the shipped Kubernetes manifest, the drain comes from the Pod's preStop, and each control-plane node's pool sees it only at its next refresh, which runs every 5 s; see below.) After the drain starts, it calls `HarnessPoolConnector.runAutomationOperation`, the call the scanner's fire makes, every 50 ms. Every request used the `scheduleId` `verify-schedule`, which is deliberately not an `asch_` id, so no call could commit anything. Before the drain, the request answered `400 invalid_automation_operation`, because the route checks the Session and the client id before the body. The later calls reused the same cached attachment, so their 404 means the Session was gone, not a client-id mismatch.

- **One-member pool.** Times are from the start of the drain:
  - 0–~70 ms: `409 hosted_harness_quiescing`, while the placement went from ACTIVE to QUIESCING.
  - From ~128 ms: the placement was RELEASED and the Harness DRAINED, and the call answered `404 hosted_session_not_found` 69 times over about 3.75 s.
  - Then one `MutationOutcomeUnknownException`, most likely the background refresh closing the member's client mid-call. After that the call answered `503 harness_pool_unavailable`.
- **Two-member pool (control).** The Session moved to `pool-b` (placement ACTIVE on `pool-b`, epoch 2), and no 404 appeared.
- **Scanner unit case.** The fire is answered `404 hosted_session_not_found`:
  - the occurrence settles skipped with `definition_retired`;
  - the mirror becomes `retired`, and later ticks derive nothing;
  - `GET` reports `state: retired, enabled: false`;
  - a revise answers `409 automation_retired`.

**The chain in the code:**

1. **Release.** The draining Harness quiesces and then releases ownership. The control plane sets the placement to RELEASED (`ManagedSessionStore`) and leaves its epoch unchanged. After that commit, the Harness drops the Session from its in-memory map (`sessions.delete`).
2. **Selection.** In `HarnessPoolConnector.select`, a placement that is not ACTIVE takes the acquire branch. When there is no reachable accepting candidate and the old owner is still reachable, `select` does not throw. It returns the old owner, and this fall-through does not check the placement state. The only comment in `select` about keeping calls on the old owner ("Keep completion RPCs on the live owner while its SQL fence refuses a handoff") is on the refused-takeover branch, which requires an ACTIVE placement on a quiescing owner.
3. **Membership.** After a refresh with a current discovery snapshot, the old owner stays in `members` only while an open Session placed on it is unreleased (`hasUnreleasedOwnership`). `select` falls back to it only while it is marked reachable. So for a released Session, the window lasts until the pool drops the member, the Harness stops answering, an accepting member appears, or some node takes the Session over and its epoch moves.
4. **Cached attachment.** In `QwenHostedHarnessConnector`, the attachment cache key is (tenant, Session, placement epoch). A release that the Harness starts does not change the epoch, and nothing on that path clears the entry. On the automation path, the entry stays until the pool drops the member and closes its leaf connector. So `runAutomationOperation` reuses the cached attachment and posts to the draining Harness.
5. **Harness answer.** The automation route answers `404 hosted_session_not_found`. The drain gate in front of it applies only to a Session the Harness still has.
6. **Scanner.** `AutomationScanner.fire` and the reconcile path treat `hosted_session_not_found` like `automation_not_found` and `automation_retired`: the occurrence settles skipped and `store.retire` runs. A manual run fires through the same `AutomationScanner.fire`, so it retires the mirror too.
7. **No recovery.**
   - `projectSchedule` updates a mirror row only for a higher record revision.
   - `findArmed` reads only live rows.
   - `update` and `run` refuse a row that is not live (`requireLive`).
   - A claim already taken before the retire can still be re-driven. That is the only fire left.

**When it can happen.** The run drained through the control plane (`HarnessPoolConnector.drainInstance`), which marks the member quiescing at once. A preStop drain reaches each control-plane node's pool only at that node's next refresh. Until then the node still counts the draining member as accepting: a call for a released Session can place it back on that member at a new epoch, where the load is refused with `409 hosted_harness_quiescing`. From the code, the 404 needs all of these:

- **The pool still has the draining member after the member releases the Session.** A refresh drops a non-accepting member only when no open Session placed on it is still unreleased (`hasUnreleasedOwnership`), for example one still running a turn; until such a refresh the member stays. In the run nothing else was placed on `pool-a`, so the member stayed until the next refresh, about 3.75 s after the release. On a node whose Kubernetes discovery snapshot is not current (after any watch or list error, until the next successful list), a refresh skips this removal altogether.
- **The firing node's pool has no reachable member it counts as accepting.**
- **The fire comes from a control-plane node whose cached attachment for the Session is still at the epoch the Session was released with.** A node without that cached attachment has to load the Session first, and the draining Harness refuses the load with `409 hosted_harness_quiescing`.

The shipped manifest aims to keep a second Pod accepting while one drains: it runs two replicas, a `RollingUpdate` with `maxSurge: 1` and `maxUnavailable: 0`, a PDB with `minAvailable: 1`, and an optional HPA whose scale-down is disabled. The firing node's pool can still see no accepting member. From the code:

- on a node whose discovery snapshot is not current, a refresh empties the pool's accepting list (and skips member removal);
- during a rollout whose new Pods advertise a different Hosted Harness feature list or protocol versions, the pool refuses them, because it accepts only the contract it negotiated first.

In a single-member pool, every drain meets the second condition.

### What did you expect to happen?

The automation keeps its definition, and the fire waits (with a 503 or a deferral) until the Session is placed again. Possible fixes, one or more of:

- On the acquire path, `select` should never hand a RELEASED placement to the leaf connector. With no accepting candidate, it answers `503 harness_pool_unavailable` instead of falling back to the old owner. Clearing the attachment cache on the release path would not be enough, because a Harness-initiated release reaches only the control-plane node that served it.
- The scanner does not retire on `hosted_session_not_found` without confirming that the Session is closed.

### Client information

Server side: the Managed Agent server at `main` `bfa7a2f52e`, with a Harness pool.

### Login information

N/A

### Anything else we need to know?

- A public create or revise in the window takes the same path. It answers `404 hosted_session_not_found`, because `translate` maps a Harness 404 to 404.
- The spurious retire also orphans the old definition. A public retire of the retired mirror only replays locally and relays nothing, so the Session's record of the old definition stays live. It still counts toward the Harness's limit of 32 live definitions per Session, while the control plane's own count (live mirrors only) leaves it out. Once the automation is recreated on the same Session, it holds two of those slots on the Harness while the control plane counts one.
- Related: #15666, other pool refusals on the public routes.
- I can share the scratch IT and the unit case if they are useful.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

### 发生了什么？

前提是执行 fire 的控制面节点在 Harness 池里看不到可达且在接收的成员。这时，排空中的 Harness 释放某个 Session 后，池可能仍为它选中这个 Harness。在这段窗口里，该 Session 的自动化 fire 可能发到这个排空中的 Harness。此时 Harness 已把这个 Session 从内存中移除，所以答 `404 hosted_session_not_found`。

扫描器把这个码当作"定义或其 Session 已永久不在"，把定义的镜像退役掉。此后：
- 不会再为它派生 occurrence；
- `GET` 显示它已退役；
- 修订被拒绝。

只能重建这个自动化，尽管该 Session 自己记录的定义仍是 live 的。

**分两部分复现**，基线是 `main` `bfa7a2f52e`。404 来自一个基于 `HostedHarnessPoolMySqlIT` fixture 写的临时 IT，使用真实的 Harness 进程、Spring 和 MySQL 8.4。退役来自一个临时 `AutomationScannerTest` 用例，其中的 404 是伪造的。真实进程的那次运行没有定义自动化，也没有运行扫描器。

IT 先在 `pool-a` 上创建一个 Session，控制面因此持有它的 attachment。然后通过 `HarnessPoolConnector.drainInstance` 排空 `pool-a`，这个调用会让池立刻把该成员标为静默。（按随附的 Kubernetes 清单，排空来自 Pod 的 preStop，各控制面节点的池要到下一次刷新才看到它，刷新每 5 秒一次；见下文。）排空开始后，IT 每 50 毫秒调用一次 `HarnessPoolConnector.runAutomationOperation`，这正是扫描器 fire 用的调用。每个请求的 `scheduleId` 都是 `verify-schedule`，刻意不是 `asch_` id，因此任何调用都不会提交内容。排空前，请求答 `400 invalid_automation_operation`，因为路由先检查 Session 和 client id，再校验请求体。之后的调用复用同一条缓存的 attachment，所以它们的 404 说明 Session 已经不在，而不是 client id 不匹配。

- **单成员池**（时间从开始排空算起）：
  - 0 到约 70 毫秒：`409 hosted_harness_quiescing`，此时 placement 从 ACTIVE 变为 QUIESCING。
  - 约 128 毫秒起：placement 已是 RELEASED，Harness 已 DRAINED，调用在约 3.75 秒内 69 次答 `404 hosted_session_not_found`。
  - 随后出现一次 `MutationOutcomeUnknownException`，很可能是后台刷新在调用中途关闭了该成员的客户端。之后调用答 `503 harness_pool_unavailable`。
- **双成员池（对照）**：Session 迁到了 `pool-b`（placement 在 `pool-b` 上为 ACTIVE，epoch 2），没有出现 404。
- **扫描器单测**（fire 答 `404 hosted_session_not_found`）：
  - occurrence 记为 skipped，原因为 `definition_retired`；
  - 镜像变为 `retired`，之后的 tick 不再派生；
  - `GET` 显示 `state: retired, enabled: false`；
  - 修订答 `409 automation_retired`。

**代码中的因果链：**
1. **释放**：排空中的 Harness 先静默，再释放属主。控制面把 placement 置为 RELEASED（`ManagedSessionStore`），epoch 不变。这次提交之后，Harness 把 Session 从内存里的 map 中移除（`sessions.delete`）。
2. **选择**：在 `HarnessPoolConnector.select` 里，非 ACTIVE 的 placement 走获取分支。没有可达的接收中候选、而原属主仍可达时，`select` 不会抛出，而是返回原属主；这个回落不检查 placement 状态。`select` 里唯一讲留在原属主的注释（"Keep completion RPCs on the live owner while its SQL fence refuses a handoff"）在接管被拒的分支上，那个分支要求静默中属主上的 ACTIVE placement。
3. **成员资格**：每次（发现快照为最新的）刷新后，只有当原属主上还有未释放的开放 Session（`hasUnreleasedOwnership`）时，它才会留在 `members` 里；`select` 只在它被标为可达时才回落到它。所以对已释放的 Session 来说，窗口持续到池移除该成员、Harness 不再应答、有接收中的成员出现，或某个节点接管该 Session 使其 epoch 改变为止。
4. **缓存的 attachment**：`QwenHostedHarnessConnector` 的 attachment 缓存键是（tenant、Session、placement epoch）。由 Harness 发起的释放不改 epoch，这条路径上也没有任何地方清除这条缓存。在自动化路径上，缓存会一直保留，直到池移除该成员、关闭它的 leaf 连接器。所以 `runAutomationOperation` 会复用缓存的 attachment，把请求发到排空中的 Harness。
5. **Harness 的应答**：自动化路由答 `404 hosted_session_not_found`。路由前面的排空关卡只对 Harness 仍持有的 Session 生效。
6. **扫描器**：`AutomationScanner.fire` 和 reconcile 路径把 `hosted_session_not_found` 当作 `automation_not_found`、`automation_retired` 处理：occurrence 记为 skipped，并执行 `store.retire`。手动运行也经过同一个 `AutomationScanner.fire`，同样会退役镜像。
7. **无法恢复**：
   - `projectSchedule` 只在记录 revision 更高时才更新镜像行。
   - `findArmed` 只读 live 的行。
   - `update` 和 `run` 拒绝非 live 的行（`requireLive`）。
   - 退役之前已经认领的 claim 仍可能被重驱，这是唯一还会发生的 fire。

**何时会发生。** 实际运行是经控制面排空的（`HarnessPoolConnector.drainInstance`），这会让池立刻把该成员标为静默。preStop 发起的排空，要到各控制面节点的下一次刷新才会被各自的池看到。在那之前，该节点仍把排空中的成员算作在接收：针对已释放 Session 的调用可能以新的 epoch 把它放回这个成员，而加载会被以 `409 hosted_harness_quiescing` 拒绝。根据代码，出现这个 404 需要同时满足：
- **该成员释放这个 Session 之后，池里仍有它。** 只有当它上面已没有仍未释放的开放 Session（`hasUnreleasedOwnership`，例如一个仍在跑 turn 的 Session）时，刷新才会移除这个不在接收的成员；在这样一次刷新之前，成员一直留着。运行中 `pool-a` 上没有别的 placement，所以该成员留到了下一次刷新，即释放后约 3.75 秒。在 Kubernetes 发现快照不是最新的节点上（任何 watch 或 list 出错之后，直到下一次成功 list），刷新会完全跳过这一步移除。
- **执行 fire 的节点的池里没有它认为在接收的可达成员。**
- **fire 来自一个控制面节点，它为该 Session 缓存的 attachment 仍停留在 Session 被释放时的 epoch。** 没有这条缓存的节点必须先加载该 Session，而排空中的 Harness 会以 `409 hosted_harness_quiescing` 拒绝加载。

随附清单力求在一个成员排空时保持另一个 Pod 在接收：两副本、`maxSurge: 1` 与 `maxUnavailable: 0` 的 `RollingUpdate`、`minAvailable: 1` 的 PDB，以及可选、禁用缩容的 HPA。但执行 fire 的节点的池仍可能看不到在接收的成员。根据代码：
- 在发现快照不是最新的节点上，刷新会清空池的接收列表（并跳过成员移除）；
- 在新 Pod 声明的 Hosted Harness 特性列表或协议版本不同的滚动更新中，池会拒绝它们，因为它只接受最初协商的契约。

单成员池的每次排空都满足第二个条件。

### 期望的行为

自动化保留它的定义；fire 等待（答 503 或推迟），直到 Session 被重新放置。可能的修法（可任选其一或组合）：
- 在获取路径上，`select` 不应把 RELEASED 的 placement 交给 leaf 连接器：没有接收中的候选时，答 `503 harness_pool_unavailable`，而不是回落到原属主。只在释放路径上清除 attachment 缓存是不够的，因为由 Harness 发起的释放只会到达处理它的那个控制面节点。
- 扫描器在确认 Session 已关闭之前，不因 `hosted_session_not_found` 退役定义。

### 客户端信息

服务端：`main` `bfa7a2f52e` 的 Managed Agent 服务端，使用 Harness 池。

### 登录信息

不适用

### 补充信息

- 窗口内公共的创建或修订走同一条路径，会答 `404 hosted_session_not_found`，因为 `translate` 把 Harness 的 404 映射为 404。
- 误退役还会把旧定义变成孤儿：对已退役镜像做公共退役，只会在本地重放，不会中继任何操作，所以该 Session 记录的旧定义仍是 live。它仍计入 Harness 每个 Session 32 个 live 定义的上限，而控制面自己的计数（只数 live 镜像）已不含它，所以在同一 Session 上重建之后，这个自动化在 Harness 上占两个名额，而控制面只算一个。
- 相关：#15666（公共路由上的其他池拒绝）。
- 如有需要，我可以提供临时 IT 和单测用例。

</details>
