items.title: Milestone v5: BYOC team runtime (customer-operated, cloud-offloaded)

labels.name: milestone
labels.description: Tracks a major delivery milestone (e.g., Milestone v1, Milestone v2)

items.body:
**Predecessor:** #747 (Milestone v4)
**Successor:** #1066 (Milestone v6 — hosted control plane)

> **Re-positioned 2026-07-28.** The v5/v6 seam was re-cut from *solo-first vs teams-later* to **runtime vs control-plane**, matching the trust boundary. v5 is now the **BYOC team runtime** — everything that runs in the customer's VPC and touches content or credentials (rooms, node mesh, agent-plug/ACP, team/shared vault). The Aileron-hosted paid layer (identity/SSO, shared catalog service, billing, fleet audit, governance) is v6 (#1066). The original "fire one detached job while the laptop is offline" motivation still holds, but it is no longer the headline: the driver is **organizational, multiplayer capability** and **removing the per-user, cross-platform install/vault burden**. R1–R17 below are unchanged and still valid; R18–R27 and the new tracks/decisions capture the re-positioning.

## Goal

v5 takes the v4 containerized runtime and makes it a **customer-operated, team-shaped runtime** that runs in the customer's own environment (BYOC). It provisions agent containers across a pool of nodes, mounts shared team/project **room** context into each session, seals credentials at the ADR-0019 boundary, and lets any agent plug in through an open protocol. Aileron-the-company never holds customer credentials or content; the agent stays isolated from raw secrets via the v4 HTTPS data plane (ADR-0019).

**v5 is done when** a team can operate a BYOC runtime in their own cloud that: (a) provisions agent sessions on demand across one or more nodes, (b) mounts a shared room's context into a session and writes results back to it, (c) runs a pluggable agent (not only Aileron Claude) sealed at the credential boundary, and (d) offloads long-running jobs that survive the operator's laptop going offline — all with credentials never leaving the customer's environment and never reaching the agent in raw form.

This issue is the v5 roadmap checkpoint. It is **roadmap-level**: most tracks below need their own `/ce-brainstorm` + `/ce-plan` before they are orchestrate-ready. Readiness is flagged per track.

## Key decisions (settled)

- **BYOC topology.** Runtime is customer-operated; Aileron-the-company holds no customer credentials and no content. Agent isolated via the ADR-0019 data plane.
- **"Local" means "customer-operated," not "on each device."** The vault runs in the customer's cloud alongside compute and the sealing proxy, keeping the ADR-0019 model intact with no reinterpretation. (Resolved the "vault stays on the laptop" tension in favor of the cleanest sealing model.)
- **Runtime is a scheduler over a pool of nodes, not a single box.** A node can be org-VPC compute (default), a self-run cluster, or an individual's machine that joins the pool. The control plane holds the node registry + scheduling policy (metadata); it never becomes the compute.
- **Credential-aware scheduling.** A session that needs user U's sealed credentials runs only on nodes in U's trust domain (U's own machine or org-VPC nodes). Un-credentialed work may run anywhere in the pool. U's sealed creds never land on a peer's machine.
- **Rooms are the shared-context primitive** — they replace the per-user home directory. Room *content* (shared knowledge, history, artifacts) lives in the VPC and mounts into sessions; room *membership/discovery* is control-plane metadata (v6).
- **Multiplayer v1 is async shared context** (rooms as shared repos): everyone runs their own session against shared room state. Live co-presence (many humans steering one live session) is deferred.
- **Agents are pluggable via an open protocol (ACP direction).** The runtime treats the agent as a plug behind the existing `Agent` interface, generalized to an open protocol, so any agent — not just Claude/Codex — can run. Credential sealing happens at the network boundary, not inside the agent, so a third-party agent is sealed exactly the same way.
- **Detachable offload.** Fire-and-detach; laptop need not stay online. Reattach-to-running-job is deferred.
- **Persistent customer-operated vault** in the runtime environment (not ephemeral seed-and-destroy), with the ADR-0023 member-aware schema underpinning per-user *and* team/shared vaults.
- **Open-core, Apache-2.0** for the runtime + single-user control plane. The paid hosted control plane is v6.
- **Control plane stays out of the job data path.** Session I/O flows client ↔ VPC runtime directly; the control plane only issues commands, holds metadata, and hands out routing + short-lived access.

## Tracks

- [ ] **Runtime packaging (BYOC).** Relocate the v4 local stack (daemon + vault + sandbox) into a customer-deployable reference image + deploy recipe; substrate is the customer's choice. — *needs brainstorm/plan (substrate, packaging)*
  - [x] **Shareable frozen Flight Plans** — publish a frozen plan + composed image to OCI, install by reference, and launch across machines without re-freeze; the open-core runtime distribution primitive. — umbrella #1898 — *delivered: 5/5 merged (#1920/#1925/#1948/#1950/#1952); P2 cosmetic follow-up #1949 parked*
  - [ ] Includes the **read-only-filesystem sandbox topology** (agent home runs read-only) for hardening the runtime image. Once it lands, **#987** (Claude `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN` EnvBinding) becomes buildable and should ship with it.
- [ ] **Node pool + scheduler (mesh).** — **#2167**. The runtime schedules agent sessions across a pool of heterogeneous nodes (org-VPC compute, self-run clusters, individual machines that join). Includes node-join/enrollment, a **credential-aware scheduler** that pins credentialed sessions to the credential owner's trust domain, and node-liveness/awareness. — *needs brainstorm/plan (net-new)*
- [ ] **Rooms (shared context).** — **#2166**. A room is a durable, named shared-context store (team rooms, project rooms) that replaces the per-user home directory. The runtime mounts a room's context into a session and writes agent results back. Room content lives in the VPC; membership/discovery is v6. First cut is async (no live co-editing). — *needs brainstorm/plan (net-new)*
- [ ] **Agent-plug / ACP.** — **#2168**. Generalize the `Agent` interface to an open protocol so any agent plugs in; the runtime provides orchestration + room context and seals credentials at the boundary regardless of agent. — *needs brainstorm/plan (net-new); **open: which protocol** (Zed Agent Client Protocol vs an agent-to-agent spec such as A2A) — see Outstanding Questions.* Related: **#1462** (vendor-neutral provider/model/key primitive) feeds this seam.
- [ ] **Team / shared vault.** Extend the persistent customer-operated vault to per-user *and* team/shared credential bindings using the ADR-0023 member-aware wrapped-key schema. Runtime enforces per-user vs shared credential scope at the sealing boundary. — *needs plan (extends #827/#1065 vault work)*. Related: **#1664** (STS/SSO temporary credentials for `aws_sigv4`) lands here as headless cloud auth.
- [ ] **Remote job dispatch.** Local `aileron` (or the thin web client) fires offloaded jobs at a remote runtime; fire-and-detach; results + sanitized audit retrieval. — *needs brainstorm/plan (CLI↔runtime discovery + auth, incl. NAT / private VPC)*. Related: **#433** (scheduled/deferred dispatch primitive).
- [ ] **Headless cloud auth.** Claude LLM auth + connector credentials working headless in the cloud runtime (captured once, stored in the customer-VPC vault, used without per-job interactive login). — *needs research/plan*
- [ ] **Remote approval surface.** The v4 approval gate (ADR-0009) must reach a human when the runtime is remote and the session is detached — the localhost webapp/PTY TUI assumption breaks. Runtime enforces the gate; notification/routing is a v6 control-plane concern. — *needs brainstorm/plan (net-new; relates to #802 launch TUI)*
- [ ] **Persistent customer-operated vault.** Vault lives in the runtime environment; agent isolated via ADR-0019. Largely reuse of v4. — *partial reuse; needs plan for relocation*
- [ ] **Open-core licensing.** Apply Apache-2.0 to the runtime + single-user control plane; establish the clean code boundary for the proprietary v6 control plane. — *relatively concrete; closest to orchestrate-ready*

- [x] **Agent-as-Feature sandbox model.** Author each agent install as a devcontainer Feature (single source of truth) so customer tooling composes under any agent; CI bakes prebuilt per-agent images from the same Feature. — umbrella #1080 — *complete (2026-06-17): all 4 sub-issues merged (#1108/#1109/#1115/#1117); regression fix #1118; all review-residuals cleared. Umbrella closed 2026-06-20.* (This is the substrate the agent-plug/ACP track generalizes.)
- [x] **Publish + freshness-track per-agent images.** CI-bake per-agent sandbox images from the Features, publish to GHCR, auto-resolve at launch (zero local build), keep fresh on agent release cadence. — umbrella #965 — *complete (2026-06-18).*

## Foundations (existing v4 work this builds on)

- **#827** — state externalization + vault-centric, member-aware encryption schema. This is the seam that makes BYOC an *extension* of v4 rather than a rewrite: configurable state backends let the runtime persist vault / audit / sessions / **room content** in the customer's environment, and the member-aware schema underpins the team/shared vault track.
- **read-only-filesystem sandbox topology** — relevant to hardening the runtime image for BYOC packaging; tracked under the **Runtime packaging** track above. #987 depends on it.

## Out of scope (here)

- The hosted layer that Aileron operates — identity/SSO, room **membership/discovery**, the shared **catalog service**, billing/seats, fleet audit/governance — that is **v6 (#1066)**.
- **Live co-presence** (multiple humans steering one live session in real time) — deferred to a later layer; v5 multiplayer is async shared context.
- Aileron-hosted/multi-tenant runtime that touches customer credentials or content; restrictive licensing (BSL/SSPL/etc.); the archived SaaS product.
- Local cross-platform install polish (**#1452** signed DNF repo, **#583** macOS notarization) is *deprioritized* by this pivot — the motivation for moving to a customer-operated runtime is precisely escaping the per-OS install/vault burden. Not cancelled, but no longer on the critical path.

---


## Embedded requirements — BYOC team runtime + open-core control plane

## Summary

Aileron becomes a **team-shaped, customer-operated runtime**. The runtime (vault, agent compute, credential-sealing proxy, shared room context) runs in the customer's own cloud; it provisions agent sessions across a pool of nodes, mounts shared team/project room context into each session, runs any pluggable agent sealed at the credential boundary, and offloads long-running jobs that survive the laptop going offline. The runtime is open source (Apache-2.0) and fully functional for a single user. Aileron-the-company sells a hosted, proprietary **control plane** (v6) that adds the multi-user layer — identity/SSO, room membership, a shared catalog of flight plans and skills, billing, central governance, and fleet audit — sitting entirely outside the job data path, never touching credentials or content.

## Problem Frame

v4 (#747) delivers Aileron Claude running in a Docker sandbox, but only locally: the daemon, vault, and sandbox all run on one host, tightly coupled over localhost, and every user installs and operates that stack themselves across Linux/macOS/Windows. Two costs drive the change. First, the **per-user, cross-platform install and vault-management burden** is the dominant adoption friction — building and supporting the local stack on three OSes, and asking every user to set up their own vault, is where customers get stuck. Second, Aileron's value is increasingly **organizational**: a serious team wants *shared* capability — shared flight plans, shared skills, and shared context — not a per-laptop single-player tool. Making AI multiplayer means a shared environment where a team's context lives in something meant to be shared (like channels/rooms), not in one person's home directory.

Moving the runtime into the customer's cloud resolves both: the customer operates one runtime instead of N laptops, the vault lives beside compute (so credentials never leave the customer's environment and the ADR-0019 data plane keeps the agent isolated exactly as it does locally), and shared context/rooms/sessions become natural because everyone is operating against the same runtime. The original offload win (fire a long job, close the laptop) falls out for free once the runtime is remote and persistent.

That customer-operated, open-source choice creates a business problem: a customer could run everything for free in their own VPC. So Aileron-the-company's revenue has to come from a hosted layer that is genuinely hard to self-host and that a serious team actually needs — identity, a shared catalog, coordination, billing, and fleet governance — not from restricting the open core.

## Key Decisions

- **BYOC topology — the runtime is customer-operated.** The daemon + vault + sandbox + sealing proxy + room content run in the customer's environment. Aileron-the-company never holds customer credentials or content. The trust burden is "the agent can't read secrets," which v4's HTTPS data-plane proxy (ADR-0019) already solves.

- **"Local" = "customer-operated," not "per-device."** The vault runs in the customer's cloud beside compute and the proxy. This keeps the ADR-0019 sealing model intact with no reinterpretation, at the accepted cost that credentials leave the individual's device into infra the customer's org operates.

- **The runtime is a scheduler over a node pool.** Nodes are heterogeneous: org-VPC compute, self-run clusters, and individual machines that join. The single-runtime-in-one-VPC model is generalized to a pool. The control plane holds the node registry + policy (metadata); it never becomes the compute.

- **Credential-aware scheduling is mandatory once nodes federate.** A credentialed session runs only on nodes in the credential owner's trust domain; un-credentialed work runs anywhere. This is the mechanism that lets personal machines join the pool without a user's sealed credentials landing on a machine they don't control.

- **Rooms replace the home directory as the context primitive.** Room content lives in the VPC and mounts into sessions; room membership/discovery is control-plane metadata. v1 multiplayer is **async shared context** — everyone runs their own session against shared room state; **live co-presence is deferred**.

- **Agents are pluggable via an open protocol.** The `Agent` interface generalizes to an open protocol (ACP direction) so any agent plugs in. Because sealing happens at the network boundary (ADR-0019), agent-agnosticism does not dilute the credential-isolation moat — a third-party agent's credentialed calls are sealed identically.

- **The control plane is out of the job data path.** It never receives job inputs, outputs, credential material, or room content. Only identity/authorization, routing metadata, and sanitized audit cross to it. This preserves the credential- and content-isolation story even when the control plane is Aileron-hosted.

- **Open-core, Apache-2.0.** The runtime + single-user control plane are Apache-2.0 — a real OSI license with no field-of-use restriction. Monetization lives in a *separate proprietary product* (the hosted control plane), not in a restrictive license on the open core. Accepted tradeoff: anyone may fork or self-host; the moat is the hosted control plane + operational value + trademark.

- **The paid boundary is single-user → multi-user / organizational.** The OSS runtime is fully functional for an individual. Payment is triggered by needing the team layer (identity, catalog, coordination, seats, fleet governance), never by a license gate on the runtime.

- **Offloaded jobs are detachable.** A job survives the laptop going offline — which is *why* credentials must live in the customer's environment (a persistent, customer-operated vault) rather than ephemeral per-job seeding.

- **Railway hosts the control plane only.** It runs a service as a container and cannot natively nest Docker, so it is not the runtime substrate. The runtime ships as a reference image + deploy recipe; the customer picks the substrate.

## Actors

- A1. **Individual operator** — runs the OSS runtime + single-user control plane; fires sessions from a local CLI/thin client. Needs no hosted account.
- A2. **Team admin** — manages identity, room membership, permissions, sharing, and approval routing through the hosted control plane (v6).
- A3. **Team member** — fires sessions in shared rooms subject to permissions and approvals.
- A4. **The agent (pluggable)** — Aileron Claude/Codex or any ACP-compatible agent; runs in the sandbox, isolated from raw credentials.
- A5. **The customer-operated runtime** — scheduler + node pool + vault + sandbox + sealing proxy + room content in the customer's environment; executes sessions and emits sanitized audit.
- A6. **A node** — a unit of compute joined to the pool: org-VPC compute, a self-run cluster, or an individual machine.
- A7. **The hosted control plane (v6)** — Aileron-operated identity/membership/catalog/coordination/billing/governance layer; out of the job data path.

## Key Flows

- F1. **Offloaded session, single-user.**
  **Trigger:** operator fires a session locally.
  Client authenticates to the runtime → scheduler places the session on an eligible node → the agent runs in the sandbox, data plane injects credentials at the proxy boundary → laptop may detach → results and sanitized audit are retrievable from the runtime afterward.

- F2. **Team session in a shared room.**
  **Trigger:** a team member fires a session in room R.
  Control plane authenticates the member and checks room membership/permissions (metadata) → runtime schedules the session on a node in the member's trust domain → the room's shared context mounts into the container → the agent reads/writes room context, credentialed calls sealed at the proxy → results write back to room R and sanitized audit aggregates to the fleet view. The control plane never touches the session's content or credentials.

- F3. **Personal machine joins the pool.**
  **Trigger:** an individual joins their machine to the org's runtime as a node.
  The node registers with the control plane (metadata) → the scheduler may place *un-credentialed* work there, and *credentialed* work only when the machine is in the credential owner's trust domain → the node is aware of and reachable by the runtime scheduler.

## Requirements

**Topology and boundary**
- R1. The runtime (daemon + vault + sandbox) runs in the customer's environment, customer-operated; Aileron-the-company holds no customer credentials.
- R2. A local `aileron` command dispatches an offloaded agent job to a customer-operated runtime; the job runs remotely and the laptop need not stay online for its duration.
- R3. The control plane never receives job inputs, outputs, or credential material; only identity/authorization and sanitized audit cross to it.

**Runtime (offloaded execution)**
- R4. The runtime executes the v4 Aileron Claude sandbox model: the agent runs in a container, isolated from raw credentials via the HTTPS data-plane proxy (ADR-0019).
- R5. Credentials live in a persistent, customer-operated vault in the runtime environment; the agent never receives raw secrets.
- R6. Jobs are detachable — fire-and-detach, with results and sanitized audit retrievable after completion.
- R7. The runtime ships as a reference image + deploy recipe; the substrate is the customer's choice and Railway is not required for it.

**Control plane (open-core split)**
- R8. A single-user control plane is part of the OSS runtime and is fully functional for an individual.
- R9. The hosted control plane adds the multi-user layer: identity/SSO, teams, sharing, approval workflows, permissions (RBAC), central policy/connector governance, and fleet audit/observability.
- R10. The paid boundary is the single-user → multi-user transition; the runtime is never license-gated or feature-crippled for individuals.
- R11. The hosted control plane runs on Aileron-the-company infrastructure (Railway).

**Licensing and packaging**
- R12. The runtime and single-user control plane are licensed Apache-2.0 — OSI-approved, no field-of-use restriction, running-as-a-service permitted.
- R13. The multi-user control plane is a separate proprietary product, not a restrictive license layered on the open core.

**Local CLI**
- R14. The CLI authenticates the actor before dispatch — locally for the single-user path, via hosted control-plane SSO for the team path.
- R15. The CLI dispatches jobs directly to the runtime endpoint, never routing job content through the control plane (consistent with R3).

**Audit and governance**
- R16. The runtime emits sanitized audit (no secret material; job content only as policy permits) that the hosted control plane can aggregate for fleet observability.
- R17. The hosted control plane can distribute policy and connector-catalog governance to enrolled runtimes; enrollment is opt-in by the customer.

**Node pool + scheduler (re-positioned 2026-07-28)**
- R18. The runtime schedules agent sessions across a pool of one or more nodes; a node may be org-VPC compute, a self-run cluster, or an individual machine that joins the pool.
- R19. The scheduler is credential-aware: a session requiring a user's sealed credentials is placed only on nodes in that user's trust domain; un-credentialed work may run on any node. A user's sealed credentials never land on a node the user does not control.
- R20. A node can join and leave the pool; the runtime tracks node liveness and reachability. Node registration metadata lives in the control plane (v6); node compute and any credential injection stay in the VPC/on the node.

**Rooms (shared context)**
- R21. A room is a durable, named shared-context store (team room, project room) whose content lives in the customer's environment.
- R22. Launching a session in a room mounts that room's shared context into the agent container; agent results are written back to the room.
- R23. Room content never crosses to the control plane; only room identity and membership (metadata, owned by v6) do.
- R24. v1 rooms are async: multiple members run their own sessions against shared room state; concurrent live co-editing of one session is out of scope.

**Agent-plug / ACP**
- R25. The runtime treats the agent as pluggable behind an open protocol; agents beyond Aileron Claude/Codex can run without changes to the sealing model.
- R26. Credential sealing occurs at the network boundary (ADR-0019) independent of which agent runs, so a third-party pluggable agent's credentialed calls are sealed identically.

**Team / shared vault**
- R27. The vault supports both per-user and team/shared credential bindings via the ADR-0023 member-aware wrapped-key schema; the runtime enforces per-user vs shared credential scope at the sealing boundary.

## Acceptance Examples

- AE1. **Covers R2, R6.** A job is fired, the laptop is closed, and on reopening the results and audit for that job are retrievable from the runtime.
- AE2. **Covers R3, R15, R23.** During a team session in a room, the hosted control plane's records contain identity, routing metadata, and sanitized audit — but no job inputs, outputs, credential bytes, or room content.
- AE3. **Covers R9 (approval workflows).** A guarded action in a team job is held pending approval; an authorized approver releases or denies it; the decision is reflected in the audit.
- AE4. **Covers R8, R10.** An individual runs the OSS runtime end-to-end (fire session, execute, retrieve results) with no hosted account and no disabled core capability.
- AE5. **Covers R4, R5, R26.** Inside an executing session, the agent (Aileron Claude *or* a pluggable third-party agent) makes a credentialed third-party call, but raw credentials are absent from container env, files, and args.
- AE6. **Covers R19.** A credentialed session for user U is scheduled while an un-credentialed session and a peer's node are available; the credentialed session lands only on a node in U's trust domain, never on the peer's machine.
- AE7. **Covers R21, R22, R24.** Two members launch separate sessions in the same room; each mounts the shared context and writes results back; there is no live co-editing of a single session and both members' writes are visible in room state afterward.

## Scope Boundaries

**Deferred for later**
- **Live co-presence** — multiple humans steering one live agent session in real time. v1 multiplayer is async shared context only.
- Reattach to a *running* job (live log stream / interactive takeover) — first cut is fire-and-detach only.
- TEE / confidential-compute vault (only relevant if Aileron ever hosts the runtime; not needed in BYOC).
- Formal certification of multiple runtime substrates beyond the reference image + recipe.
- Local cross-platform install polish (#1452 DNF repo, #583 macOS notarization) — deprioritized by the pivot, not cancelled.

**Outside this product's identity**
- An Aileron-hosted or multi-tenant runtime where Aileron operates customer workloads and touches customer credentials or content.
- Restrictive "source-available" licensing (BSL, SSPL, Elastic, Commons Clause) or any license-gating of the runtime.
- The archived multi-tenant SaaS product (server/ui/docs + Postgres + OAuth sign-in); this is a different architecture.
- Putting the control plane in the job data path for any feature.

## Dependencies / Assumptions

- Builds on v4 (#747): the sandbox launch path, the ADR-0019 HTTPS data plane, and the ADR-0012 local daemon. The runtime is essentially today's local stack, relocated into the customer's environment and generalized to a node pool.
- **Assumption:** Claude LLM auth works headless in the cloud runtime — captured once and stored in the customer-VPC vault, then used by the passthrough gateway without an interactive login per job. To validate.
- **Assumption:** the customer exposes an authenticated runtime endpoint reachable by their own users; the client→runtime network path (including private-VPC/NAT cases) is the customer's to provide.
- **Assumption:** the existing `Runner` interface (`internal/sandbox/container/runtime.go`) is the correct seam for remote/pooled node orchestration — new `Runner` implementations rather than a rewrite.
- **Assumption:** Apache-2.0 permits fork and SaaS-resale of the open core; the business accepts this and relies on the proprietary control plane + hosting + trademark for defensibility.

## Outstanding Questions

**Resolve before planning the agent-plug track**
- **Which protocol backs "ACP"?** Zed's Agent Client Protocol (host↔agent, pluggable coding agents) vs an agent-to-agent spec (e.g., A2A). This shapes the agent-plug integration and where Aileron sits (host vs peer). Not blocking the other tracks.

**Deferred to planning**
- How the client discovers and authenticates to a *specific* customer runtime endpoint, including NAT / private-VPC reachability.
- The node-join / enrollment protocol and how node liveness/reachability is tracked without the control plane entering the data path.
- The exact trust-domain model for credential-aware scheduling (how a node's trust domain is declared and verified).
- Room storage model and content-locality on personal nodes (what a node may cache of room content, and for how long).
- How an enrolled runtime authenticates to the hosted control plane to push audit and pull governance without entering the job data path.
- Exact audit-sanitization rules (what job content, if any, may cross to the fleet view).
- Per-job-fresh-container vs standing-runtime isolation model on the customer substrate.
- Claude headless auth capture mechanics in the cloud runtime.
- The remote approval surface (how a human is reached for an ADR-0009 gate on a detached remote session).

## Sources / Research

- `internal/launch/launcher.go` — current local launch → sandbox path.
- `internal/sandbox/container/runtime.go` — the `Runner` interface seam that remote/pooled orchestration extends.
- `internal/server/main.go` — the single server binary that already forks into a cloud-shaped, Postgres-backed mode on `AILERON_DATABASE_URL`.
- `internal/vault/postgres.go`, `internal/vault/user_vault.go` — the multi-tenant `PostgresVault` / `UserScopedVault` (per-user KEK wrapping) already in code.
- `docs/src/content/docs/adr/0019-v4-https-data-plane.md` — credential injection at the proxy boundary (the agent-isolation mechanism reused here).
- `docs/src/content/docs/adr/0023-v4-vault-centric-encryption.md` — member-aware wrapped-key schema underpinning per-user + team/shared vaults.
- `docs/src/content/docs/adr/0027-flight-plan-sealed-installable-skill.md` — Flight Plan = sealed installable skill; the basis for shared skills-with-environments.
- `docs/src/content/docs/adr/0012-local-daemon-architecture.md` — the daemon that becomes the customer-operated runtime's core; explicitly defers cloud-topology ADRs (this milestone is where they get written).
- Issue #747 — v4 containerized runtime this builds on.

items.title: [FABRIC CONVERGENCE] Grok orchestration + VPS/website migration to canonical Agent Fabric
items.body:
Workstream: WS:EXECUTIVE-CAPACITY-FABRIC
Authority: current Chairman direction, 2026-09-24
Program owner: Sol / CEO
Protected source pin at creation: 41617f5087d14fcbc782bf419cf1a1cd16b1918f
Skillpack: mastermind.sol_skillpack.v1 1.0.1 / bootstrap-major 1

## Outcome

Converge two consumers onto the **existing** Mastermind Executive/Capacity/Worker Fabric without creating another router, queue, lifecycle, retry plane, provider selector, result store, or host-control authority:

1. **Grok Operations Bot becomes a thin orchestrator/principal** that decomposes and adjudicates while bounded execution is delegated through the canonical Fabric.
2. **Mastermind VPS / website reasoning stops directly executing through the legacy Codex -> Claude OAuth waterfall** and instead submits role-correct bounded work to the same Fabric, with Capacity selecting the least-scarce capable eligible worker/provider/host.

The accepted end state is one control plane:

```text
caller (Grok principal | website service principal | future clients)
  -> authenticated role-specific Executive ingress
  -> canonical Runtime Job / Attempt / effect truth
  -> existing COO/planning + Model Router + Capacity
  -> exact selected Worker / host / realm
  -> local or remote Worker Broker / provider-neutral adapter
  -> canonical result + review/repair evidence
  -> exact parent/service result consumption
```

Studio is an execution host, not the public orchestration authority. The existing remote Worker Gateway remains post-placement transport bound to an already-selected Job/Attempt/Worker identity; callers do not directly choose Studio, provider credentials, accounts, hosts, or worker ids.

## Current source facts

- Existing remote substrate: `control_plane/remote_worker_transport.py`, `control_plane/remote_worker_broker_client.py`, `ops/executive_os/remote_worker_gateway.py`, `control_plane/executive_capacity_join.py`.
- Existing Grok Wake substrate: `integrations/executive_wake/grok_bot_http.py` and `grok_bot_routine.py`; accepted/start is distinct from target consumption/result.
- Existing Fabric visibility: `control_plane/fabric_job_view.py`.
- Existing website legacy direct balancer: `brain/provider_waterfall.py` -> `brain/client.py`, currently used by Strategist/Committee/Macro Risk/CIO and other seats.
- Existing Astra external-Fabric freeze already establishes the key client law: model-facing callers author bounded intent; trusted code authors authority and physical placement; no public `fabric.delegate` / provider-spawn API.
- #804 is the incumbent non-CEO service-principal mutation-sink carrier.
- #957/#960/#961 are the incumbent broad COO-principal mandate/request lineage.
- #624 is the Grok autonomy architecture lineage; its older consultation-only assumptions must be reconciled with current protected Grok Wake/Company Consultation source rather than duplicated.
- #386 remains the active dispatch-consumption / watcher-wake convergence P0; do not claim end-to-end autonomy before its relevant real-path gates close.
- #633 remains the attended Astra -> Fabric client carrier and has an unrelated Auth0 DCR `EFFECT_UNKNOWN`; do not retry, replace, or reuse that exact enrollment effect.

## Architecture rulings

### A. Grok

Grok is a **principal/orchestrator**, not a worker pool and not a second scheduler.

Grok should:
- recover intent and decompose work;
- keep architecture / hard judgment / cross-return synthesis;
- issue role-correct Fabric child/root requests through an authenticated Executive profile;
- read bounded canonical job/result views;
- receive exact RuntimeBinding/Wake nudges for returns;
- request repair / continuation / stop through the incumbent lifecycle owner.

Grok should **not**:
- use its VPs to log into Studio and drive workers directly;
- choose provider/model/account/host credentials;
- maintain its own durable queue, worker registry, retry ledger or result store;
- replay worker transcripts into its main context;
- retry or fail over a modifying operation after START / effect uncertainty.

Provider-native Grok VPs/helpers may exist only as shrink-only, same-Attempt helpers under an admitted capability ceiling. Any independently recoverable responsibility, separate review, distinct custody, or durable fan-out becomes an Executive child Job.

Company Consultation remains useful for bounded principal-to-principal questions. It is not the execution Fabric.

### B. Remote Fabric

Do **not** expose the raw Worker Broker as a generic public subagent API.

The remote-callable Fabric boundary is the authenticated Executive ingress + read/status surface. After canonical placement, the existing remote broker transport reaches the selected host. This preserves one lifecycle and makes Studio/Mac minis/VPS workers interchangeable physical capacity behind Capacity.

### C. Website / VPS

Replace the legacy execution role of `brain/provider_waterfall.py` with a Fabric-backed compatibility adapter while initially preserving the `brain.client.call_model(...)` consumer contract.

Website processes are **service principals**, not CEO/Fable impersonators. They must enter through the role-correct non-CEO sink (#804 lineage or its accepted successor), with tightly derived task kind / authorities and stable operation identity.

Migration policy:
- feature-gated `fabric` backend first;
- no caller-supplied provider/model/account/host;
- pre-effect unavailability degrades according to the seat's existing deterministic fallback policy;
- once a Fabric attempt STARTS or becomes EFFECT_UNKNOWN, never replay through the old waterfall;
- preserve seat/book/usage attribution in canonical telemetry;
- old waterfall becomes diagnostic-only after accepted parity canaries, then is retired as an execution router.

First website canary should be a low-authority additive narration/research seat (e.g. CIO narration) before strategist/risk/committee paths.

## Dependency / wave plan

### G0 — ingress convergence
Reconcile the role-correct non-CEO/COO ingress owner (#804 + #957/#960/#961) into one accepted mutation sink with distinct role policies. No new listener or Job creator.

### G1 — Grok Fabric client
Add a Grok principal profile/client over the accepted Executive ingress:
- stable operation/request identity;
- bounded objective/acceptance packet;
- canonical status/fabric view;
- exact effect reconciliation;
- no placement fields;
- exact RuntimeBinding/Wake return.

### G2 — Grok token-relief canary
Run one substantive bounded project:
Grok decomposes -> Fabric child executes -> independent review/repair if required -> bounded result returns -> Grok adjudicates.
Measure Grok context/token usage, delegated share, return bytes, latency, duplicate/effect-unknown incidents, and Chairman interventions. No transcript replay.

### V0 — website Fabric compatibility adapter
Introduce a Fabric backend behind `brain.client.call_model` without changing downstream seat semantics. Map role/seat to reviewed service-principal task profiles and preserve deterministic degradation.

### V1 — one website canary
Move one additive/read-only seat to Fabric and prove output shape, attribution, timeout/result handling, restart/idempotency, and no direct OAuth-provider choice.

### V2 — staged website migration
Move remaining eligible seats in risk order. Interactive streaming/chat paths are assessed separately where their latency/streaming contract differs from batch/background reasoning.

### V3 — retire legacy balancer
After parity, failure-injection and production-path proof, remove the old Codex/Claude OAuth waterfall from normal website execution. Provider/account cooling remains a Capacity/provider-readiness responsibility, not a website router.

### R0 — remote-host proof
Prove one canonical Job placed by Capacity onto a remote eligible host, executed through the existing mTLS gateway/broker, result returned to Runtime, no duplicate effect under response loss, and exact cleanup/readback.

### R1 — resilience / scale
Fault matrix: pre-submit refusal, lost response after modifying write, host offline, provider exhausted, stale Capacity, worker crash, parent restart, duplicate submit, review rejection/repair, return-path failure. Prove no blind failover and no second control plane.

## Acceptance

Program is complete only when:
- Grok routinely delegates bounded work without direct Studio/provider orchestration;
- one remote host round trip is production-proven through canonical placement;
- website batch reasoning uses Fabric rather than the legacy direct OAuth waterfall;
- Capacity owns provider/account/host selection;
- result/review/repair returns are canonical and bounded;
- START/EFFECT_UNKNOWN never trigger blind replay;
- failures degrade truthfully;
- one real Grok token-relief comparison demonstrates a material reduction in principal-context/worker-token burn without reducing accepted output quality;
- one website staged migration passes real production-path canaries;
- Chairman performs zero routine account selection, tab shuttling, or worker-message relay.

## Immediate next action

Do not arm another dispatcher. First reconcile G0 against current #804/#957/#960/#961 and #386 source/ownership, then implement the first **client-side, role-correct** vertical on a path-disjoint carrier. The website and Grok clients can advance independently once the accepted ingress contract is stable; remote host execution remains behind current Capacity/Worker Broker ownership.

items.body:
![Find your focus and passion across seven vLLM Semantic Router Workgroups](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vllm-project/semantic-router/main/website/static/img/blog/vllm/2026-08-24-workgroups-invitation/workgroups-invitation-hero.png)

## Find Your Focus and Passion

vLLM Semantic Router organizes its durable open-source technical directions
into seven Workgroups. A Workgroup gives contributors a clear place to find
people with the same interests, shape accepted Epics, build together, and grow
with the community.

> A Workgroup is a technical home, not a repository permission level.

- [Explore the Workgroups](https://vllm-sr.ai/community/work-groups)
- [Read the community invitation](https://vllm-sr.ai/blog/join-vllm-sr-workgroups)

## Seven Workgroups

| Direction | What it owns |
| --- | --- |
| [MoM & Routing](https://github.com/vllm-project/semantic-router/issues/2965) | Model pools, versioned routing recipes, multi-model collaboration, and the recipe lifecycle |
| [Router Models & Inference Runtime](https://github.com/vllm-project/semantic-router/issues/2966) | Router Model improvement and new model families, typed signals, and an extensible inference runtime |
| [Data Plane & Networking](https://github.com/vllm-project/semantic-router/issues/2967) | Standalone and gateway-integrated request paths, streaming, reliability, and performance |
| [Enterprise & Environment](https://github.com/vllm-project/semantic-router/issues/2968) | Management security and audit, configuration lifecycle, observability, capacity planning, reference deployments, and supported environments and hardware |
| [Agentic & Context](https://github.com/vllm-project/semantic-router/issues/2987) | Context optimization, memory and session boundaries, and safe model or workflow switching for long-running agents |
| [Developer Experience & Ecosystem](https://github.com/vllm-project/semantic-router/issues/2970) | CLI, Dashboard, documentation, agent skills, integrations, tutorials, and contributor experience |
| [Evaluation & Quality](https://github.com/vllm-project/semantic-router/issues/2969) | Shared evaluation contracts, benchmarks, published results, and regression gates |

The planning hierarchy is:

`Mission → Direction → Workgroup → bounded Epic → accepted issue`

## How Workgroup participation works

Joining a Workgroup as a Member follows four steps:

1. **Apply** — choose a Workgroup above, open its charter, and leave a first-person application comment with your background and interests.
2. **Claim** — choose an available issue from your Workgroup's comment on the [current Workgroup Issues ledger](https://github.com/vllm-project/semantic-router/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3Acommunity+label%3Aaccepted+label%3Aowner%2Fmaintainers+%22Workgroup+Issues%22+in%3Atitle), open the target issue, and comment `/assign`. The claim counts only after your name appears in the target issue Assignees field.
3. **Deliver** — open a focused PR linked to the claimed issue and get a substantive contribution merged.
4. **Join** — eligible contributors are added through one reviewed roster PR. Membership becomes canonical after that PR merges.

### If you have not applied

Choose a Workgroup, open its charter from the table, and submit a Member application. You can then claim an available issue from your Workgroup's comment on the [current Workgroup Issues ledger](https://github.com/vllm-project/semantic-router/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3Acommunity+label%3Aaccepted+label%3Aowner%2Fmaintainers+%22Workgroup+Issues%22+in%3Atitle).

### If you have applied but do not know how to start

Choose an available issue from your Workgroup's weekly comment and use `/assign` on the target issue. If none fits, comment `Need task: wg/<slug>` on the [current Workgroup Issues ledger](https://github.com/vllm-project/semantic-router/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3Acommunity+label%3Aaccepted+label%3Aowner%2Fmaintainers+%22Workgroup+Issues%22+in%3Atitle) so the next review can prepare options; this does not assign a task automatically.

### If you already joined

Choose an available issue from your Workgroup's weekly comment. Use `/assign` on the target issue, or leave `Need task: wg/<slug>` on the [current Workgroup Issues ledger](https://github.com/vllm-project/semantic-router/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3Acommunity+label%3Aaccepted+label%3Aowner%2Fmaintainers+%22Workgroup+Issues%22+in%3Atitle) when the current list has no suitable work.

A contribution qualifies a contributor for the Workgroup that owns that work. A requested Lead role follows the same contribution path but requires a separate human role decision.

For the complete role guidance and card examples, read [How to join and work together](https://vllm-sr.ai/blog/join-vllm-sr-workgroups).

Find your focus and passion. Build with the community. Grow together.

items.body:
## Live commercialization / governance baseline — 2026-09-09

This issue tracks protected integration order and exact-head evidence for Accounting Information Platform. It records evidence only; it is never permission to bypass branch protection, self-approve, weaken a gate, force-push, destructively rebase, synthesize status, or transfer predecessor evidence.

### Protected integration / live rulesets

Protected/default integration remains `develop@239008c4edc7d305c97704c5102b593c6622b36f`. Applicable queued, pending, skipped, cancelled, absent, predecessor-head, merge-ref-only, prose-only, model-only or synthetic evidence is non-passing. Active rulesets remain organization `21783807` (AIP main release workflow gate), organization `18156473` (CWL Central required workflows), and repository `21768773` (AIP main release gate). The repository ruleset requires one approving review, stale-review dismissal and thread resolution and forbids non-fast-forward/deletion. GitHub release inventory must remain empty until an exact protected integrated head is release-ready.

### Canonical reconciliation stack

Lifecycle #43 is merged history through ordinary root composition and is no longer an open dependency lane.

- **#29 root**: exact `12e1a4bb9d8de5e4b6c72e2893107b07c515416b`, open/Draft/mergeable on protected `develop@239008c4...`. items.title: Night build 13 Oct: backend lane and app lane, shared board
items.body:
One place where the two builder sessions working tonight (the backend session on this repository, the app session on waldo-app from Ansh's Mac) post what they are touching, ask each other questions, and review each other's PRs. Ansh is asleep; an orchestrating session reads this issue on an hourly cadence and answers from the Waldo Build Bible.

## Lanes

- **Backend lane** (cloud session, repository waldo-backend only, branches `claude/<item>` off `beta-mvp`, one PR per item): A0 take over PR 1100 and split the rename into its own PR; A1 scheduled jobs under the owner principal; A2 browser admission on the owner binding, Browserbase default, custody by principal with dual read; A3 Telegram copy of proactive work behind a switch, and the app connect route with its migration; B the 30-day rotating session, the "did not finish" transcript row, `created_at` on transcript rows; C the Brief silent on the body unless the shared-health section is present; D guards (five block, the rest warn) and the cost ledger in the trace book; E push backend (device routes, Expo Push sender behind a fake, template text only, quiet hours, three a day); F cancel route, memory edit route, profile and facts blocks, spend ceiling with the contract sync script, the nightly eval runner as a CI job; G port PR 1088's mid-turn rebind test onto 1100.
- **App lane** (Mac session, repository waldo-app only): the design review's two plain-fix PRs (words and labels; layout and colour), the three-tab shell and greeting header, plain chat chrome, retired names out, dead composer controls hidden; the Phase 1 app items from the bible (delete the 83 unreachable files, the Brief rows on Home, Body labels as candidate); builds for both phones; the Samsung Health range reader when its turn comes.

## Protocol

1. **Disjoint files.** Each lane changes only its own repository. The backend lane never edits waldo-app; the app lane never edits waldo-backend. Docs that both cite are read-only tonight.
2. **Public contract changes are additive only**, and are announced here before the PR opens: the route or field, its zod shape, and the PR number. Tonight's expected additions, all additive: `created_at` on transcript rows; device routes (list, register, revoke); the cancel route; the memory route (claims with evidence, forget); an app connect action; a spend field on the account view. The app lane consumes only what is merged into `beta-mvp`, pinning the committed schema by hash as today; a path that waits on a backend PR is marked "awaiting backend PR #N" in the app PR, never built against an unmerged shape.
3. **Questions** are posted as comments here, prefixed `Q (backend)` or `Q (app)`, with the file and the decision needed. The orchestrator answers within about an hour from the bible's recommendations; a question only Ansh can answer is parked with `NEEDS ANSH` and the lane moves on.
4. **Cross review.** Each lane may review the other's open PRs (`gh pr view`, `gh pr diff`) and leave findings as PR review comments; findings are claims to verify, not orders. Neither lane merges anything.
5. **Progress.** Each lane posts one comment per finished PR: number, head SHA, what passed, what did not, and anything parked.
6. **Conflicts.** If both lanes need the same file (a shared doc, a generated fixture), the backend lane yields and posts the change it wanted here.

items.title: [Padiem AI] Padiem Plus / Pro / Max model-pool, free-tier rotation and fallback strategy (platform-wide: B14 routing / B54 Claw / B62 Chat)
items.body:
<!-- B14_CURRENT_OWNER_HISTORY_NOTICE_20261008 -->
> **2026-10-08 HISTORY NOTICE: NOT CURRENT MODEL APPROVAL.** Old bare Plus/Pro/Max label concept was superseded by per-model 파디엠플러스 labeling.
> Current OWNER: four Google AI Studio IDs (gemini-3.1-flash-lite, gemini-3.5-flash-lite, gemma-4-26b-a4b-it, gemma-4-31b-it); five excluded (Kilo Poolside Laguna, B.AI Qwen, Motif 3, GPT-5.6 Luna, NVIDIA Nemotron); customer label 파디엠플러스 + individual model name. See [#3554](https://github.com/skerishKang/ai-revenue-lab/issues/3554) and [reconciliation PR #3784](https://github.com/skerishKang/ai-revenue-lab/pull/3784). Google registration is LOCAL UNMERGED; source/catalog/Production readiness is a separate fact.

---

## Purpose

Capture the current product/architecture discussion before implementation hardens around one Provider or one temporary free model.

This is a **design/benchmark issue**, not a Production activation issue.

Refs #1102 #1103 #1382 #1385.

## Current product naming decision

User-facing model experience should not expose `LOW / MEDIUM / HIGH` as product labels.

Current preferred presentation:

```text
Padiem Plus
Padiem Pro
Padiem Max
```

Future expansion may add additional product tiers (for example Basic or other branded tiers) without changing Provider/model identities.

Internal compatibility identifiers such as LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH may remain temporarily, but product naming and model/provider identity must be decoupled.

## Current candidate mapping — NOT FINAL

```text
Padiem Plus -> NVIDIA Nemotron family candidate
Padiem Pro  -> Poolside Laguna family candidate
Padiem Max  -> future premium/frontier pool
```

Nemotron is not to be treated as an intrinsically low-quality model merely because it may occupy the lowest current commercial tier.

## Model-pool direction to evaluate

Rather than permanently binding one model to each tier, evaluate a bounded approved pool:

```text
Padiem Plus -> approved model pool A
Padiem Pro  -> approved model pool B
Padiem Max  -> approved paid/frontier pool C
```

At initial launch, UI may show only ~3 choices/tier experiences while B14 keeps additional approved fallback candidates behind the routing boundary.

When a free promotion/model disappears or becomes unavailable, B14 should be able to replace the underlying route without renaming the Padiem product tier.

## Kilo discovery / free-model volatility

Kilo exposes a no-auth `GET /models` endpoint containing current model IDs, pricing, context, and supported features. Free availability can change over time.

Do **not** treat `FREE_TODAY` as a permanent product contract.

Candidate architecture:

```text
Kilo /models
  -> zero-cost/free candidates discovered
  -> Padiem allow-list / policy intersection
  -> capability + privacy + quality + health gates
  -> Plus / Pro candidate pools
  -> B14 bounded selection/fallback
```

Discovery must never auto-promote an unknown model to Production solely because its price is zero.

## Rate-limit / credential principle

Do not design around multiple Kilo accounts/API keys to evade a free-model limit.

Current Kilo documentation states free-model requests, authenticated or anonymous, are gateway-limited per IP (currently documented as 200 requests/hour/IP). Therefore multiple Kilo API keys on the same serving egress are not a sound scaling strategy and must not be treated as quota multiplication.

Legitimate credential portfolio may still include:

- distinct providers with their own approved credentials/terms;
- Kilo managed routes;
- Kilo BYOK for approved direct Provider keys;
- direct Provider adapters where B14 already owns the boundary.

Credential rotation must be for normal availability/key lifecycle, **not** circumvention of Provider/account/rate-limit policy.

## Initial-launch usage policy

Owner direction for the current launch phase:

```text
Padiem app-level usage limit = effectively unlimited for initial testing/launch
commercial billing enforcement = later
```

This does not override upstream Provider/Kilo rate limits or terms.

Future Control Plane work (#1103) will add anonymous vs signed-in vs paid entitlements/quotas. Usage numbers must remain configurable policy, not hard-coded product constants.

## Fallback questions to benchmark

Evaluate separately:

1. **Model-unavailable fallback** — 429/5xx/provider outage.
2. **Free-promotion disappearance** — model no longer free/listed.
3. **Capability mismatch** — tools/vision/context requirement not supported.
4. **Quality routing** — task class better served by another approved model.
5. **Privacy/data-handling gate** — free route unsuitable for sensitive customer data.

Manual/pinned user model selections must not silently change unless the UI/product contract explicitly permits fallback.

## Benchmark / decision output

Before final tier mapping, compare a manageable shortlist from the current Kilo free pool and other legitimate Provider routes using synthetic/non-sensitive prompts.

Measure at minimum:

```text
Korean conversational quality
reasoning quality
coding quality
instruction following
long-answer quality
streaming behavior / TTFT
latency p50/p95
context window
multimodal/tool support
429/5xx behavior
privacy/data-use suitability
free availability / volatility
```

End with:

```text
PADIEM_PLUS_PRIMARY = <model or HOLD>
PADIEM_PLUS_FALLBACKS = <bounded ordered list>
PADIEM_PRO_PRIMARY = <model or HOLD>
PADIEM_PRO_FALLBACKS = <bounded ordered list>
PADIEM_MAX_POLICY = <paid/frontier policy or HOLD>
FREE_POOL_REFRESH_POLICY = <manual/periodic guarded policy>
USER_VISIBLE_MODEL_COUNT = <target, likely small>
```

## Non-actions

```text
PRODUCTION_MODEL_DEFAULT_CHANGE = NO
PRODUCTION_SECRET_INSTALL = NO
MULTI_ACCOUNT_RATE_LIMIT_EVASION = NO
AUTO_PROMOTE_ANY_FREE_MODEL = NO
BILLING_ACTIVATION = NO
REAL_USER_DATA_BENCHMARK = NO
```

Keep this issue open while the owner and CENTRAL refine the model portfolio and product-tier policy.

items.title: [Connector 2/7] Auditoria de isolamento multi-tenant (escopo por userId)
items.body:
Sub-issue da épica #38 — frente **2. Multi-tenant isolation audit**.

> Objetivo: garantir que 100% das queries são escopadas por `userId`, sem exceções nem atalhos de admin, e que isso é protegido por testes.

## Estado atual (auditoria do código)

- ✅ `@CurrentUser()` decorator usado nos controllers — `apps/api/src/common/decorators/current-user.decorator.ts`
- ✅ `JwtAuthGuard` global (`APP_GUARD`) popula `req.user` antes dos services — `apps/api/src/auth/auth.module.ts`
- ✅ Services filtram por `userId` (ex.: `meal.service.ts` com `assertOwner()`, `food.service.ts` cobre custom vs. TACO)
- ✅ Tools MCP recebem `userId` por contexto, não por input — `apps/api/src/mcp/mcp-tool.registry.ts`
- ✅ Índices compostos `[userId, X]` e `onDelete: Cascade` no `schema.prisma`
- ✅ Há testes de isolamento cross-user (ex.: `apps/api/src/progress/__tests__/weight-log.service.spec.ts`)
- ❌ **Sem Postgres Row-Level Security** (isolamento é 100% na camada de aplicação)
- 🟡 Cobertura de testes de isolamento é **parcial** — existe em progress, mas não comprovadamente em todos os domínios

## O que falta para fechar a frente

- [ ] **Varredura exaustiva**: revisar todo service/controller/repository/tool e confirmar que nenhuma query escapa do `userId`. Produzir uma matriz (domínio × tool) marcando o ponto onde o escopo é aplicado.
- [ ] **Teste sistemático que falha alto** se uma tool retorna dado sem escopo de usuário: um teste parametrizado que, para cada tool de leitura, cria dados de user-A e tenta acessá-los como user-B esperando `NOT_FOUND`/vazio. (Hoje só alguns specs cobrem isso.)
- [ ] **Avaliar Postgres RLS** como defesa em profundidade (não substituto). Spike: viabilidade com Prisma (ex.: `SET app.current_user_id` por transação) — ADR com decisão go/no-go.
- [ ] **Documentar o threat model** em `docs/` (vetores: token de outro user, IDOR via ID, admin shortcut, SQL injection → o que protege cada camada).

## Critério de pronto

- Matriz de cobertura mostra que toda query é escopada por `userId`.
- Suíte de testes falha se qualquer tool vazar dados entre usuários.
- ADR sobre RLS + doc de threat model publicados.

items.title: Roadmap 3: evidence-backed competitor gap assessment and delivery acceptance
items.body:
# OWG competitor gap assessment — 24 October 2026

## Decision

OWG has broad first implementations across task mining, process mining, process
knowledge and agent handoff. It does **not** yet demonstrate complete functional
parity with the combined capabilities of Mimica, UiPath, Celonis, Soroco,
Microsoft, SAP Signavio, ABBYY, IBM, Apromore and Disco. The largest remaining
work is connecting those implementations into a reliable company product and
proving their accuracy and business outcomes.

This assessment supersedes the old *gap descriptions*, not shipped functionality,
in [#264](https://github.com/KAVentures/openworkgraph/issues/264). Keep
[#326](https://github.com/KAVentures/openworkgraph/issues/326) as the delivery
history. Checked first-slice tasks are not evidence of complete parity.

## Method and limits

Repository baseline: `4bb6ee349d1c` (main, including PRs #366–#369). Evidence below
is from source, tests, documentation and public primary vendor pages retrieved
on 2026-10-24. Repository paths are relative to this checkout. Vendor sources
are numbered at the end. Product pages establish **advertised functionality**;
user guides establish **documented functionality**. Neither establishes runtime
quality, contractual availability, editions, deployment fit or performance.
No paid competitor environment or private customer dataset was accessed.

The vendor capabilities form a union, not a claim that every competitor offers
every feature. Do not turn vendor marketing percentages into OWG acceptance
thresholds. We inspected REA's role: public documentation was sufficient here;
no proprietary code, protected application, binary or asset needed inspection.

Notable corrections to the earlier comparison:

- UiPath's current Task Mining guide explicitly scopes it to **known tasks** and
  excludes automatic discovery of unknown tasks and ranked recommendations [S2].
  Mimica's broader discovery claims [S1] are a separate benchmark.
- Cartographer now describes a governed **Map of Work** in Open Knowledge Format,
  guided discovery, fact provenance, exceptions, named approvals and generated
  PDD/SDD [S3]. A diagram plus exported document is only part of that experience.
- Mimica Maker advertises agent code tested against actual work examples [S1].
  OWG's runnable synthetic SDK/MCP proof is valuable but does not prove that claim.
- Microsoft documents scheduled and incremental refresh, shared analytics, and
  transformations [S7–S9]; those go beyond uploading CSVs or sharing a graph.
- Celonis advertises a connected context model and querying billions of records
  [S10]. OWG's local 10M-event acceptance is a different, narrower scale claim.

## What already exists

Do not rebuild these: local desktop/browser evidence and consent; discovery
studies; versioned process catalog and independent organization design review;
CSV/XES/OCEL 2.0 import/export; columnar saved logs and incremental append;
variants and evidence drill-down; paired/nested parallel structural models;
conformance/alignment/token replay; KPIs, typed analyses, compliance rules,
root-cause **associations**, predictions/backtesting, map abstraction, dotted
charts, cohort comparison and concept drift; simulation; opportunity scenarios
and a local idea pipeline; masked screenshot PDDs; selected communications-export
mining; generated starters and executable customer-controlled SDK projects;
shadow evaluations, pinned source checks and minimized execution monitoring.

Relevant inventories: [process roadmap](PROCESS_PRODUCT_ROADMAP.md),
[event-log workspace](EVENT_LOG_WORKSPACE.md), [catalog](PROCESS_CATALOG.md),
[shared design collaboration](PROCESS_COLLABORATION.md),
[monitoring](AUTOMATION_MONITORING.md), [pipeline](AUTOMATION_PIPELINE.md).

## Capability gap matrix

“Partial” means implementation exists with a material limitation. “Missing”
means no complete product path was found in the inspected baseline, not proof
that no related helper exists. “Unproven” means acceptance evidence is missing.

| ID / priority | Competitor reference | OWG evidence and remaining work | Completion evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| R1 / P0 | Automatic discovery, variants, cross-team maps: Mimica [S1], Soroco [S11] | **Partial/unproven.** `evals/reconstruction`, `server/work_resumption.py`, multi-signal record links and team motifs exist. Family-holdout assignment quality remains below the preregistered ≥0.90 F1 / ≤0.05 contamination gates. Motifs do not prove end-to-end cross-employee cases. | Frozen development/family holdout, independent real annotations, ambiguity/abandonment/multiplexed tabs, interruption rejection, consent/revocation and exact confidence/evidence provenance. Publish failed as well as passed metrics. |
| R2 / P0 | Shared understanding of actual work: Mimica/Soroco [S1,S11] | **Partial.** Aggregated consenting team motifs and caller-reviewed source joins exist. Need source-authoritative case identity, scoped handoffs, per-case contributor provenance and unresolved boundaries. | Two employees/two apps/overlapping cases reconstructed from authorized object IDs; unmatched and conflicting identities remain unresolved; opt-out excludes future sharing and respects deletion. |
| R3 / P0 | Repeatable data ingestion: UiPath/Microsoft/Signavio [S5,S8,S16] | **Partial.** Manual CSV/XES/OCEL and selected Jira/GitHub/Zendesk/Stripe audits; append dedupes supplied exports. Missing complete connector lifecycle for Salesforce/ServiceNow/SAP/M365, checkpoints, schema versions, retries, freshness and revocation. | Real provider sandboxes, least scopes, paginated incremental extraction, late events, deleted records, rate limits, expired grants and retry without loss/duplication; no extraction by default. Coordinate existing #326 connector workstream. |
| R4 / P0 | Governed company analytics: Microsoft/UiPath [S7,S4] | **Missing connected path.** `server/event_log_routes.py` is local; Gateway shares approved process **designs**, not a tenant event-log analysis workspace. Local signals, saved analyses, pipeline and monitoring are separate stores. | Explicitly publish minimized datasets/views; dataset-level roles, field/case minimization, retention/revoke/delete, auditable exports, tenant isolation; two real identities inspect same authorized case and analysis. Preserve local-only mode. |

## Architecture and non-negotiable boundaries

Use the existing catalog as the persistent versioned process knowledge model.
Connect imported events/objects, canonical evidence and record identities through
references with explicit scope and origin. Use immutable versioned derived
artifacts; keep process review, observation consent, data sharing, tool grants,
current business intent and verified outcomes separate. Derived artifacts must
not outlive permissions invisibly. Unknown data stays unknown; missing events do
not prove conformance, productivity, savings or a correct business result.

Functional parity includes useful competitor capabilities. It does not require
copying proprietary source, names, images, layouts or broadening ordinary capture
to typed content. Support customer runtimes with explicit grants rather than
replaying historical clicks or building a second RPA engine by default. Any future
consequential action remains behind the existing current-intent, authorization,
precondition, independent-readback and replay-prevention checks.

## Validation and evidence required for each package

- Appropriate unit/property tests for semantics and real browser acceptance for
  changed user flows; keyboard, mobile, WCAG and minimized safe rendering.
- Native supported-OS CI and packaged install/start/export compatibility.
- SQLite/PostgreSQL tenant isolation and revocation where shared stores change.
- Representative declared scale and work-budget tests; unknown and refused
  computations explicitly counted. Do not benchmark only uniform happy paths.
- Exact commit/tree/artifact digests in evidence; failures remain visible.
- Separate synthetic, provider-sandbox and real pilot evidence. No mocked provider
  test closes an actual provider acceptance gate.

The weights are normalized so the stated rate stays the long-run average; the pattern is shared by both runs, and `scenario_arrival_pattern` changes only the scenario.
  - Weights can be entered, or the hour-of-week pattern measured from the selected cases' start times (at least 14 days, with its basis reported).
  - Arrivals form an exact non-homogeneous Poisson process, with one random number per case so paired runs stay paired. Daylight saving follows the zone.
  - A calendar and a pattern in one run share one clock origin.
  - Out-of-range start dates and runs past year 9999 are refused with a 422 instead of a 500; this also fixes the #382 calendar. Local times are computed by arithmetic, so Windows behaves like other platforms.
  
  Peer review found the different-origin case, fixed before merge and independently rechecked. Windows CI found the platform clock difference, fixed with a test that reproduces it on any platform. Full regression **3,007 passed, 25 skipped**; Chromium and all native CI workflows green.
- M5 / R19 censoring-aware predictions: **merged in #388**, main `8e4b6072d32db02b2b2be513316d60d86087eb8d`. An opt-in `"estimator": "survival"` learns from completed and still-open cases; the default estimator is unchanged.
  - Open cases are right-censored observations in a Kaplan–Meier curve per comparable state, with the same fallbacks.
  - Each open case's estimate is conditioned on how long it has already been idle, and is measured from the end of the log.
  - Estimates the history cannot support are withheld, with the lower bound it does support.
  - The backtest replays the log as of a cutoff. It scores the cases in progress then against the completed-cases estimator on the same cases, and counts the cases still open instead of dropping them.
  - Outcome risk still uses completed cases only.
  
  The curves match a textbook product-limit calculation. In a log of exponential case durations with long cases still open at export, survival medians are within 15% of the true remaining time; completed cases alone give under 40% of it. The as-of backtest shows at least 15% lower error and coverage near the nominal 80%. Full regression **3,015 passed, 25 skipped**; Chromium and all native CI workflows green. Production-label ingestion, drift/calibration monitoring and intervention testing remain open.
- M5 / R24 object-centric flattening diagnostics: **merged in #389**, main `e98ffb9aba3a873fee8d549ce05300a658c8b398`. `GET /v1/event-logs/{id}/object-flattening` reports, per object type, what a case analysis on it does:
  - which events it leaves out (deficiency);
  - which it copies into several cases (convergence: extra rows and duplication factor);
  - which activity repetitions are really one per object of another type (divergence, with the differing types);
  - qualifier use, and objects whose qualifier changes.
  
  The object map states the consequences for the selected type in plain language. Explaining repetitions stops at a disclosed 5M-link work budget while still counting them. Order-to-cash counts are checked against values computed by hand. 160k OCEL events take about 1 s. Full regression **3,019 passed, 25 skipped**; Chromium with WCAG and all native CI workflows green. Object-centric conformance and temporal object attributes remain open.
- M5 / R14 held-out simulation validation: **merged in #390**, main `c85048025738ac2b9b34d1cd313502dd095a52a5`. `POST /v1/event-logs/{id}/simulation/validation` calibrates only from cases finished before a cutoff, simulates them, and compares the result with the cases that started after the cutoff.
  - The comparison covers cycle-time quantiles with relative errors, arrival rates, and a two-sample Kolmogorov–Smirnov distance with its 5% critical value.
  - Cases spanning the cutoff are left out and counted.
  - A pattern measured from the log is refused, because it would see the held-out period.
  
  A stable process reproduces its later period exactly, and a process that changed after the cutoff is flagged (KS = 1). Exponential activity times expose the calibration's median-as-mean simplification: simulated times come out about 31% short. That is disclosed; calibration semantics are unchanged. Full regression **3,031 passed, 25 skipped**; Chromium and all native CI workflows green.
- M5 / R14 mean time basis: **merged in #391**, main `e9c2b911c6edd28669781009c3333b14b2ba24c4`. Calibration now reports each activity's mean gap (`mean_minutes`) next to the median. An opt-in `"activity_time_basis": "mean"` uses it for every measured activity, in both runs and in held-out validation; entered minutes still win.
  - The default stays `median`, so existing what-if results are unchanged.
  - With exponential activity times, held-out error falls below 12% across three seeds, against about 31% with the median.
  
  An unknown basis is refused with a 422. Full regression **3,036 passed, 25 skipped**; 185 JS tests, Chromium and all native CI workflows green. Whether `mean` should become the default is left open.
- M5 / R24 temporal object attributes: **merged in #392**, main `c4e343238aebd5b2e908a85cfa4b8589ced7ece8`. OCEL import keeps every timed object attribute value next to the unchanged stored value that analyses use.
  - **Limits:** each attribute's stored-value entry is kept, plus at most 1,000 other values and 32 names per object.
  - **Append:** adds later values for new and existing objects within those limits and counts what it leaves out.
  - **Export:** OCEL JSON and XML write real times. A stored value without its own time goes out at the 1970 unknown-time origin. Every kept value survives export and re-import, and an unrepresentable object is refused before any file is written.
  - **Report:** `GET /v1/event-logs/{id}/object-attributes` gives, per type and attribute, value changes, the most frequent changes, and how many event links happened while another value than the stored one held (5M-link budget). The object map summarizes it.
  
  Peer review found three round-trip losses: a stored value without a time, the newest value at the 1,000-value limit, and a stored attribute at the 32-name limit. All were reproduced, fixed and independently re-checked before merge. Full regression **3,062 passed, 25 skipped**; 188 JS tests, Chromium and all native CI workflows green; the merged tree equals the tested head.
- M5 / R24 object-centric conformance rules: **merged in #394**, main `64f8fa7b60ee744a7fed2ecd5a9622fa48a5b828`. `POST /v1/event-logs/{id}/object-constraints` checks up to 20 rules across object types without flattening the log:
  - `event_cardinality`: objects of a type per event of an activity;
  - `object_cardinality`: related objects of another type per object, optionally only through one activity;
  - `synchronization`: an activity of an object only after a required activity of every related object.
  
  Objects are related when they share an event; order is time, then event ID. Vacuous rules are counted separately, and absent activities and types are disclosed. Each rule gives a violation rate with a 95% Wilson interval and up to 50 examples. Relating objects stops at a disclosed 5M-pair budget instead of returning partial counts. The object map adds an Object rules form. Every count on the order-to-cash fixture is checked by hand. 100k OCEL events with three rules take 0.72 s. Full regression **3,099 passed, 26 skipped**; 191 JS tests, Chromium and all native CI workflows green; the merged tree equals the tested head. Conformance against an object-centric process model (for example object-centric Petri nets) remains open.
- M5 / R14 routing and arrival uncertainty: **merged in #395**, main `e980573c91c06309a4769421154a05542e0fcce0`. An opt-in `"uncertainty": {"replications": 2–50}` repeats the paired what-if run with parameters drawn from what the log supports:
  - routing shares from a Dirichlet distribution over observed path counts;
  - the arrival rate from a Gamma distribution over observed arrivals.
  
  Entered paths and arrivals stay as entered; this is disclosed. Each replication has its own random numbers, shared by baseline and scenario. The response gives 95% ranges for p50/p90 cycle times and their change, each measured path's drawn share and the drawn arrival rate. Point results are byte-identical with or without the setting. Replications × cases × 2 runs ≤ 400,000.
  
  The drawn shares match their Beta distribution. The 95% routing range covers the true share in 90–99% of 300 simulated logs, and 40 cases give more than 3× the range of 2,000. An unchanged scenario shows zero change in every replication. Full regression **3,111 passed, 26 skipped**; 193 JS tests, Chromium and all native CI workflows green; the merged tree equals the tested head.
- M5 / R14 activity-time uncertainty: **merged in #396**, main `4ab288dcfd017e204ed508ea8da98c0e0823a57f`. Calibration reports each activity's `observed_gaps`. The uncertainty replications scale each measured activity time by Gamma(n, 1/n), with n = observed gaps, which is exact for the mean of exponential times; entered minutes stay as entered. The response lists each activity's drawn minutes.
  - **Coverage:** the 95% range covers the true mean of 30 exponential gaps in 90–99% of 300 simulated samples.
  - **Results:** entered minutes stay fixed, and point results are unchanged.
  
  Full regression **3,114 passed, 26 skipped**; 193 JS tests, Chromium and all native CI workflows green; the merged tree equals the tested head. Resources and process structure are not varied.
- M5 / R14 step-by-step routing: **merged in #399**, main `110dd68bf615e66411930131b19e5c69a6681c1e`. An opt-in `routing: "transitions"` replaces replaying the most frequent complete paths with a first-order walk over the directly-follows graph of every eligible case.
  - **Calibration:** start shares and, per activity, the shares of the next activity or the case end.
  - **Scenarios:** a scenario can replace any activity's next steps.
  - **Per-case results:** each case walks with its own random numbers, so an unchanged scenario is identical and changed times never change routes. Results report `visits_per_case`.
  - **Path limit:** a case that reaches the 100-step limit is stopped and counted. Held-out validation reports these stopped routes (`simulated_routes`), states that they are compared as if finished, and the view states that routing is first-order.
  - **Uncertainty:** replications draw each row from a Dirichlet distribution.
  
  Path routing is unchanged and stays the default. On a rework loop, visits match the geometric expectation. On six optional checks (64 variants), path routing runs about 28% short on the held-out mean (KS 0.42). Transitions match the median exactly, with about +11% mean error and KS 0.15. Codex's peer review found that validation hid stopped routes (374 of 1,000 in its probe); this was fixed and re-verified before merge. Full regression on the tree combined with #398: **3,180 passed, 26 skipped**; 198 JS tests, Chromium and all native CI workflows green; the merged tree equals the tested head. Higher-order or case-attribute-dependent routing remains open.
- Parallel claims: none from Claude. Connectors remain unclaimed here. The local process → opportunity segment of M0 shipped in #376; the remaining lineage/journey segments are open.


- M0/R5 local process → opportunity linkage: **merged in #376**, main `6760c8916e7cf872de4ddf41e36ecef25fc926bf`. Exact server-resolved local revision/hash, immutable idea reference, read-only drift checks, historical navigation and decision-time refusal on changed/deleted/replaced/uncheckable sources. No copied case/evidence/model data or execution grant. This is a bounded first segment of the full lineage journey. 52 focused tests, 176 JavaScript tests and the actual Chromium catalog → idea → exact revision navigation/drift/deletion flow pass. Full regression passes with the actual SDK enabled: **2,855 passed, 15 skipped**; 847 packaged source modules/assets are byte-identical. All six native CI workflows passed, including Windows/macOS/Linux regression, the Ubuntu repeat-suite, shared database/browser checks, packaging, launch, starters, accessibility and scale. The merged file tree is identical to the tested tree.

- M0/R5 opportunity → project: **merged #379**, main `b80ac631d4c7f02eda9e18b1404401a4ea375966`. Exact approved local idea/process revision export, unchanged runtime files/spec, extra provenance manifest, content-addressed spec/archive records, repeat-export dedupe, source/revision guards and bounded local metadata. ZIPs and receipt bodies are not stored. Combined regression with Claude #378: **2,877 passed, 15 skipped**; 853 packaged source entries exact; all six CI workflows and both pipeline/quarantine browser journeys passed.
- M0/R5 project → reported monitoring spec: **merged #381**, main `0951761cded5e1c635d7d8329a344fde5bdaab0e`. Explicit dual-hash association and bounded refs, read-time invalidation, historical linking and unlink/delete isolation. A matching specification does not identify the binary that produced a run. Per-run attribution, independent execution and business outcomes remain unverified/false. Combined regression: **2,884 passed, 15 skipped**; 176 JS tests; 855 packaged source entries exact; all six native CI workflows and pipeline/monitoring browser journeys passed. Both merged trees equal their tested trees.
- Codex/Claude peer review: three reproduced #380 bugs (bare metric references, non-finite JSON, pre-filter coverage) were reported without editing Claude's branch. Claude fixed them at `af1909c`; the same independent reprobes now pass. Native CI remains a separate gate. Current claims/progress are append-only comments to avoid overwriting parallel work.
