items.title: [INTEGRATION] GitHub-triggered independent Fabric review with Slack result return
items.body:
## Outcome / proof criterion
Install and prove event-driven *independent* review of Mastermind GitHub PRs: an authorized GitHub review request must lead to a separately admitted, source-bound Subagent Fabric reviewer, one verified formal GitHub review at the exact PR head, and a matching status thread in the existing Slack channel. Dots/ChatGPT Work are optional supplementary reviewers; GitHub/Executive/Fabric must not rely on an unproven Dot wake.

This issue is **GitHub implementation/release evidence**, not a new Executive queue, Agent OS workstream, worker lease, approval or automation daemon.

## Original authorized operation; DO NOT REDISPATCH
- Chairman assignment: 2026-10-22.
- Original Fabric root: `mmx-gh-review-20261022`.
- Existing builder child: `mmx-gh-review-20261022-build01`, controller PID `44551` on its original enrolled channel. Its original `fabric_request` returned CONTROLLER_CREATED, then local controller output showed Ubuntu2/minimax LEASE_OK, SCP and LAUNCH_ATTEMPT. Last observed status: ACTIVE_OR_WAITING / worker_state UNKNOWN / result unavailable / acceptance UNVERIFIED. **Not proof of START or completion.** Do not create a replacement child/branch/retry or clear an uncertain effect.
- Protected Mastermind procedure pin: `dce821e0d9d67b67b3053290e42fb2ac0bbcdcc1` (Skillpack 1.0.1, bootstrap-major 1). Refresh only materially affected facts before release.
- Existing Slack destination: `#github-independent-reviews` channel `C0CAUK8P8S3`; inception thread https://mastermindxgroup.slack.com/archives/C0CAUK8P8S3/p1792668898495279 ; Mastermind Executive Relay bot user `U0BT71H4FQE` has been invited and membership verified. **Bot membership does not mean automatic posting is wired.**

## Scope / implementation acceptance
1. Verify `X-Hub-Signature-256` over exact raw bytes with constant-time comparison, body bound, event/action allowlist, and GitHub current source check. Signed payload *alone* cannot authorize execution; fresh-read sender's collaborator permission, repo ID, PR state and exact head.
2. Accept bounded explicit review-intent triggers (prefer `pull_request.labeled` with `independent-review` and/or authorized `review_requested`; optional explicit comment command) and reject actor-bot loops, unauthorized requesters, spoofed PR refs, ambiguous forks.
3. Use existing Executive/Fabric runtime/admission/ledger to dedupe on original PR-head/review-intent; no new queue, scheduler, account selection, worker lease or artificial START. Interruptions reconcile original effect, never silently replay.
4. Reviewer must be distinct from author/pool. No untrusted PR code executed with Github/Slack/Fabric credentials; worker gets read-only exact immutable source refs. Bounded review method and result are verified before publishing.
5. GitHub formal review uses `commit_id` of exact frozen PR head. Re-fetch current head before one publish; changed head fails stale. Default `COMMENT` or justified `REQUEST_CHANGES`, **never automatic APPROVE, merge or deployment**. Readback exact review ID/effect; duplicate delivery cannot create duplicate reviews.
6. Slack relay mirrors sanitized lifecycle/result into the same PR+head thread; public Slack channel must not disclose private repo identities/content without a separate authorized channel.
7. Full tests: invalid signature, oversized body, replay/duplicate, bad actor, fork injection, head-changed, result absent, reviewing same author/pool, lost GitHub POST result and current-head review readback. Prove one real GitHub delivery → admitted worker START → accepted result → formal PR review + Slack, or explicitly report installation gate.

## Release dependencies discovered
- No existing `integrations/mastermind_github_app` directory at pinned master.
- Current `ops/executive_os/os_public_edge.caddy.template` only permits `POST /os/executive/context`, `/os/executive/submit`, `/os/executive/status`; a new webhook requires reviewed exact Caddy/service route, not an invented reachable endpoint.
- Fabric MCP is an attended facade; `fabric_capabilities` reported `background_execution=false`, `native_parent_wake=false`, start/admission UNPROBED. Controller creation is not autonomous production webhook dispatch.
- GitHub App creation/installation, webhook secret provisioning and least-privilege subscription/permissions will require exact actual admin tool access or user-admin ceremony; do not invent app, endpoint, secret or production proof.
- GitHub official review endpoint needs Pull requests:write and supports explicit `commit_id`: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/reviews
- GitHub webhook HMAC and fast ACK requirements: https://docs.github.com/en/webhooks/using-webhooks/best-practices-for-using-webhooks

## Exact next actions
Consume **same** Fabric child result/status and any source candidate; verify changed paths and tests, commission distinct independent review only after a candidate exists, repair source defects in existing custody, open/review draft PR, and qualify host/admin release separately. Preserve all previous effects and use explicit protected delivery/CI; green tests are not live acceptance.

items.title: ADR 0006: RPMS deployment topology — direct adapter vs customer-side connector
items.body:
## Why

Today corvid's implicit deployment model is **SaaS reaches inbound into each customer's RPMS** (VPN / proxy / private CA). That works for one customer; it scales poorly to 5–50 tribal sites with heterogeneous IHS-OIT firewall postures. The May 27 IHS correspondence (Daniel McMurtrey, Portland Area) confirms that customer-side firewall is OIT-Group-Policy-controlled, with the authoritative security spec held at the Area Office — not at the tribal site.

Before we harden pooling, retry, circuit-breaker, or model decoupling, we need a decision on the production deployment shape.

## Three modes to evaluate

- **Mode 1 — Single-tenant direct.** One corvid host, one pinned adapter. Useful today.
- **Mode 2 — Multi-tenant direct (inbound to each customer RPMS).** SaaS reaches into customer networks via VPN/proxy/private CA. Per-tenant routing. Painful at scale.
- **Mode 3 — Customer-side connector (recommended north star).** Small Lakeraven-provided binary runs inside the customer network; opens an *outbound* persistent connection (mTLS WebSocket or queue) to corvid SaaS; proxies RPMS reads/writes locally. Customer firewall only needs outbound egress.

## Decisions this ADR must settle

- Recommended deployment topology (Modes 1/2/3) and the rationale.
- For Mode 3 connector: transport (mTLS WebSocket vs queue), reconnect/backoff, message envelope.
- Where RPMS credentials live (customer-side in Mode 3; secret-manager-referenced in Mode 1/2).
- Adapter router shape — factory/config resolver, not static registry. Resolves to either a direct adapter or a connector-shaped adapter.
- Audit ownership: which side records the RPC-level audit trail vs the workflow-level decision.
- **RPMS broker session user-context** — service account vs per-end-user DUZ. This answer gates the rpms-rpc pool key shape (one global slot vs keyed on user/facility).

## Blocks

This ADR gates the following:
- AdapterRouter implementation
- rpms-rpc connection pool design (pool key needs the user-context answer)
- Operational runbook (Mode 2 vs Mode 3 docs are very different)
- Customer-side connector binary design

## Out of scope

- Implementation of any mode — this is a decision artifact only.

items.title: P0 global: autonomous independent trust-root adoption and QA/Release recovery
items.body:
## Global P0 — one independent-authoring path for every protected repair

**Owner directive:** Fix recurring QA/Release, CODEOWNER, and owner-authored trust-root deadlocks globally. Preserve source provenance, security and V17 terminal integrity; do not add a new reporting/approval controller.

### Reproduced system defects
- All-CI-green owner-authored Class B workflow/skill patches stall at `TRUST_ROOT_OWNER_AUTHORED`; author cannot independently approve itself. Representative source PRs: [#2127](../pull/2127) global QA identity/event admission/adoption recovery; [#1635](../pull/1635) bounded release-governance wait and typed denials; [#2125](../pull/2125) five AMRT agents.
- Current existing Engineering App source-copy job `wow-v17-engineering-auto-repair.yml` is **not independent source review**; it still requires exact-head owner CODEOWNER, independent QA/Release. Its prior `discover` newest-first MAX_SCAN=50 starved older eligible owner PRs. #2127 owner-source patch now includes bounded hourly fair rotation, cross-page App WIP cap, inventory-limit and negative tests.
- QA workflow's dynamic display name caused false Release source mismatch. #2127 uses immutable workflow ID/path/app/run attempt/PR/SHA and nonstorming Release App event filter. #1635 preserves terminal failure while waiting for in-progress governance.

### Required independent Engineering/Copilot execution
1. Under a **genuine nonowner** GitHub coding-agent or Engineering principal and the verified canonical single-writer lease, independently implement/adopt the minimal current-main source contract from #2127 plus #1635; avoid blind owner-source copying being mistaken for independent review.
2. Verify all protected trust-root patches have real CODEOWNER approval on exact nonowner-authored PR head. QA App 5245832 and Release App 5245853 genuinely pass exact head, with authentic receipt/provenance; preserve active required regression workflows. Do not weaken ruleset or allow self-approval.
3. Confirm fair owner-source discovery over >50 PRs and cross-page 3-PR WIP, deterministic typed holds rather than permanent starvation, non-bot owner PR triage, early/late QA/Release event admission and bounded wait with truthful completed failure.
4. Merge through authorized protected path only after checks and review; verify exact deployed Render SHA and health, rerun QA/Release canaries, and use AMRT #2125 and release wait #1635 as system-wide acceptance tests. Record source, PR, commit and independent release receipts.
5. If Copilot provider fails, use existing Claude/Gemini/Cursor authenticated fallback on the **same incident and lease**, not another owner-authored duplicate PR.

No secrets or terminal-authority changes, no fabricated approvals or probability. `V17_TERMINAL_REDUCER`, `can_execute=false`. **Closure only on real independently reviewed/deployed outcome.**

## Triple D learning: App review queue liveness
The existing three-slot Engineering App replay queue is a valid safety bound, but closure/re-entry must be event-driven and independently verifiable. At 3/3, do not create a fourth PR, force-close valid work, or burn another writer attempt. Record the three exact PR/head identities, the genuine next review/merge action for each, and a fair P0/oldest eligible backlog; when one PR reaches an authenticated terminal state, admit **one** next source under the existing writer fence. A green check on an OPEN PR does not release its slot. Rerunning an old GitHub Actions event does not update stale `github.event.pull_request.body`; read current trusted PR metadata and guard HEAD races. Maintain true independent semantic review, CODEOWNER, QA/Release and receipt provenance. Train every agent on the regression matrix and observed 3/3→2/3→3/3 automatic advancement in the [canonical Triple D teaching appendix](https://github.com/gregoryharper84-ship-it/WOW-Dashboard/issues/2136#issuecomment-6460872352). Status is NOT_FIXED_VERIFIED until protected production canary receipts prove it. No new controller, no bypass, no live bets (`can_execute=false`).

items.title: [FEATURE] Graceful MCP server startup failures - fail open

labels.name: python
labels.description: Pull requests that update python code

type.name: Feature
type.description: New feature request or improvement to existing functionality. User-facing capability that didn't exist before.

items.body:
### Problem Statement

When loading multiple MCP servers (especially from a config file), if any single MCP server fails to start, the entire agent initialization fails. This creates a poor developer experience where one misconfigured or unavailable MCP server prevents the agent from using any other tools.

Currently, if you have 5 MCP servers configured and 3rd MCP server fails to connect (wrong path, server down, auth issue), you get only 2 MCP server connections instead of the 4 that would have worked.


### Proposed Solution

Implement a "fail open" strategy for MCP client initialization:

1. When starting multiple MCP clients, catch startup failures per-client
2. Log a warning for failed clients but continue loading others
3. Return successfully loaded tools from healthy clients
4. Optionally provide a callback or return value indicating which servers failed

Example behavior:
```python
# Current behavior (fail_fast=True, the default) - unchanged
clients = [mcp1, mcp2_broken, mcp3]  # Throws exception, agent unusable

# New opt-in behavior (fail_fast=False) - graceful degradation
clients = load_mcp_clients(config, fail_fast=False)
# Logs: "WARNING: Failed to start MCP server 'mcp2_broken', skipping: Connection refused"
# Agent works with tools from mcp1 and mcp3
```

To maintain backwards compatibility, add a `fail_fast=True` parameter that defaults to the current strict behavior. Users can opt-in to graceful degradation with `fail_fast=False`.


### Use Case

- **Config-driven agents**: Loading MCP servers from `mcp.json` where some servers may be optional or environment-specific
- **Development workflows**: Testing with partial MCP availability without needing all servers running
- **Production resilience**: Agent continues functioning even if one MCP server has temporary issues
- **Multi-tenant setups**: Different users may have access to different MCP servers

### Alternatives Solutions

1. Wrap each MCPClient in try/except manually - works but verbose and error-prone
2. Pre-validate MCP configs before loading - doesn't help with runtime failures
3. Lazy loading of MCP clients - more complex, changes tool discovery timing

### Additional Context


I implemented this pattern in a wrapper project and it significantly improved DX:

```python
# Fail open approach
for name, server_config in servers.items():
    try:
        client.start()
        tools = client.list_tools_sync()
        successful_servers.extend(client)
        logger.info(f"Loaded {len(tools)} tools from MCP server: {name}")
    except Exception as e:
        logger.warning(f"Failed to start MCP server {name}, skipping: {e}")
        try:
            client.stop()
        except Exception:
            pass
```

This becomes especially important with #482 (config file loading) since users will likely have multiple servers defined.

items.title: feat: Add Advanced Pre-generated Voucher Pool reference application

labels.name: area:data-access
labels.description: Exposed, JDBC, R2DBC, PostgreSQL, data modeling

labels.name: area:spring-boot
labels.description: Spring Boot application and operational examples

milestone.description: Workshop examples for the bluetape4k-dependencies 1.3.1 release train.

items.body:
## Goal

Build an advanced browser-backed reference application for pre-generated voucher pools whose codes are imported or generated in bounded batches, allocated under contention, redeemed exactly once at the application boundary, and reconciled by operators.

This is a follow-up to #534. The baseline Promotion and Voucher Campaign example creates an opaque voucher at allocation time; this issue owns the operationally heavier pre-generated pool model.

## Scope

- Model voucher batches and pool entries through `available`, `reserved`, `allocated`, `redeemed`, `released`, `expired`, and `revoked` states.
- Support deterministic batch generation/import with provenance, policy version, activation window, and tenant/campaign ownership.
- Allocate one eligible pool entry under high contention without double assignment or capacity drift.
- Enforce per-user limits, reservation expiry, redemption idempotency, batch/campaign pause, and revoke races in PostgreSQL.
- Provide an operator UI for pool depth, batch provenance, allocation/redemption timeline, stuck reservations, revocation progress, and reconciliation outcomes.
- Exercise retry storms, pool exhaustion, partial batch failure, delayed replay, and concurrent batch revocation with deterministic fixtures.

## Acceptance criteria

- Concurrent allocators cannot reserve or allocate the same voucher code to different users.
- A user retry cannot consume multiple pool entries for one idempotent allocation command.
- Redemption and revocation races converge to one recorded PostgreSQL outcome with an auditable policy version.
- Expired reservations return capacity without making a previously exposed code reusable.
- Batch import/generation is replay-safe and partial failures remain diagnosable and resumable.
- Raw voucher codes, device signals, IP addresses, and user identifiers are absent from logs, metrics labels, and operator list views.
- The browser UI distinguishes admission, reservation, allocation, redemption, and reconciliation states.

## Delivery constraints

- PostgreSQL is the authority for pool ownership, allocation, redemption, and revocation. Redis/Bucket4j/Bloom filters may reduce load but cannot decide a terminal outcome.
- Store only a keyed digest for voucher lookup after the one-time code reveal; do not make released or expired exposed codes allocatable again.
- No reusable coupon engine or voucher-pool library is created until application evidence demonstrates a stable shared boundary.
- Fraud scoring, identity verification, WAF/CAPTCHA, and notification providers remain deterministic fakes.
- Start only after the baseline #534 contract and lifecycle are stable enough to serve as the compatibility reference.

## Platform implementation requirements

- Target Java 25 with Spring Boot and virtual threads for blocking HTTP, PostgreSQL, Redis, and background-worker boundaries whose lifecycle and failure behavior are covered by tests.
- Use the `bluetape4k-dependencies` BOM as the version authority.
- Prefer Bluetape capabilities before ad-hoc code: `bluetape4k-exposed-jdbc` repositories, `bluetape4k-exposed-jdbc-tests`, `PostgreSQLServer`, `bluetape4k-bucket4j`, `bluetape4k-lettuce`, `bluetape4k-virtualthread-api`, `bluetape4k-virtualthread-jdk25`, `bluetape4k-logging`, Testcontainers, and existing audit/leader utilities where applicable.
- Use Lettuce when Redis is required. Redis loss and Bloom false positives must degrade to PostgreSQL-backed decisions.
- Tests use live HTTP clients such as `WebTestClient` with the JDK connector rather than MockMvc.
- README documentation includes executable scenarios, an architecture diagram, and contention/reconciliation sequence diagrams.

## Relationship

- Baseline lifecycle and compatibility reference: #534
- Epic context: #531
- HTTP idempotency contract: bluetape4k/bluetape4k-projects#1055
- PostgreSQL idempotency contention evidence: bluetape4k/bluetape4k-exposed#391

items.body:
# AI CLI Tools Community Digest 2026-11-10 > Generated: 2026-11-10 03:25 UTC | Tools covered: 7 - [Claude Code](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code) - [OpenAI Codex](https://github​.com/openai/codex) - [Gemini CLI](https://github​.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli) - [GitHub Copilot CLI](https://github​.com/github/copilot-cli) - [OpenCode](https://github​.com/anomalyco/opencode) - [Pi](https://github​.com/earendil-works/pi) - [Qwen Code](https://github​.com/QwenLM/qwen-code) - [Claude Code Skills](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills) --- ## Cross-Tool Comparison # Cross-Tool Comparison Report: AI CLI Developer Tools Ecosystem **Snapshot date: 2026-11-10 · Sources: Anthropic Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Google Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, OpenCode, Pi, Qwen Code** --- ## 1. Ecosystem Overview The AI CLI tooling space has consolidated into a **seven-player field with clear tiering**: established platform incumbents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Copilot CLI) shipping weekly against challenger/independent tools (OpenCode, Pi, Qwen Code) iterating faster on narrower surfaces. Release cadence is high across the board — Claude Code, Codex, and Copilot CLI all shipped within 24 hours, while Qwen Code cut a coordinated CLI/Desktop/SDK release and Pi shipped a credential-UX milestone. **Reliability, not capability, is the story of the day**: the hottest issues across every tracker are about permissions that don't apply (3 tools), agents that stop early or misreport success (5 tools), compaction corrupting context (3 tools), and quota accounting users can't trust (3 tools). Meanwhile, **MCP and subagent/worktree orchestration** have become shared infrastructure concerns rather than differentiators. The competitive frontier is shifting from "what the model can do" to **"whether the harness, permissions, and state layer survive real multi-hour, multi-agent workflows."** --- ## 2. Activity Comparison (24h window) | Tool | Issues (updated) | PRs (updated) | Discussions | Releases | |---|---|---|---|---| | **Claude Code** | 10+ hot items; ~12 closed today | **1** (substantive; Anthropic-authored) | N/A (no data) | **2** — v2.1.322, v2.1.321 (Fable 5.2 default) | | **OpenAI Codex** | 10+ hot items | **20** (all `copyberry[bot]`, all closed) | **10+ active** (Show & Tell heavy) | **3** alpha bumps (0.169.0-α7/α6, 0.167.0-α4.1) | | **Gemini CLI** | **50** updated | **38** updated | N/A (no data) | None | | **GitHub Copilot CLI** | **29** updated | **0** | N/A (no data) | **2** — v1.0.109-0, v1.0.108 | | **OpenCode** | 10+ hot items (incl. #59387 @ 339 comments) | 10 listed (mix open/closed) | N/A (no data) | None | | **Pi** | 10+ hot items (#7547 @ 96 comments) | **10+** community-authored (petrroll cluster) | **1** (Ideas) | **1** — v1.5.1 (`pi auth`) | | **Qwen Code** | 10+ hot items; multi-month CI failures | **10** listed (mix open/closed) | N/A (no data) | **3** — v0.27.1 CLI/Desktop, SDK 0.1.31 | *Notes:* "N/A" for Discussions indicates the channel was not included in the digest data, not that the community is inactive. Issue/PR counts reflect items updated in the last 24h, not totals. Codex PR activity is dominated by an automated bot; true human PR throughput was effectively zero today. --- ## 3. Shared Feature Directions **a) Permission & sandbox correctness** — *Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Copilot CLI, Qwen Code, Pi* The single most cross-cutting theme. Claude Code's Bypass mode still prompts (#103832); Gemini CLI's shell redirect extractor misses `N>`, `>|` forms (#16140) and non-UTF-8 byte paths (#16757); Copilot CLI's macOS sandbox denies localhost despite `allowLocalNetwork: true` (#5390); Codex is mid-migration from `SandboxPolicy` → `PermissionProfile`; Qwen adds a literal backstop for `git commit --amend` (#16075); Pi hardens Windows Git-diff permission bypass (#30095). **The need is uniform: user-configured permissions must be predictable and non-bypassable.** **b) Compaction/context correctness** — *Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex, Gemini CLI* Claude Code's compaction erodes standing instructions (#108601); OpenCode has two reproducible compaction bugs (tool output dropped, #62481; tool calls stringified, #50814); Codex updated retry/compaction policy (#60473). **Compaction is now a reliability-critical subsystem, not a token-saving convenience.** **c) Subagent/worktree orchestration** — *Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Qwen Code* Claude Code's `cwd`-for-Task request (#12748, year-old); Gemini CLI's subagent turn-limit misreporting (#22323) and generalist-agent hangs (#21409); Codex discussion threads on running alongside other agents in isolated worktrees (#58834, #60282); Qwen's subagent context bloat to 105k (#15660). **Worktree isolation and subagent observability are the emergent workflow.** **d) Quota/usage opacity** — *Codex, OpenCode, Copilot CLI, Qwen Code* Codex #41220 (85 comments) is the canonical quota tracker; OpenCode #59387 (339 comments!) is the community's complaint desk and #60311 documents shared-vs-per-model limit drift; Copilot CLI #5392 reports doubled prompt accounting spiking billing; Qwen optimizes GitHub channel API budget (#16690–#16692). **Users increasingly demand a trustworthy local ledger and conditional-request polling.** **e) MCP friction** — *Codex, OpenCode, Copilot CLI, Pi, Gemini CLI* Codex stdio MCP >16 MiB silent drops (#60383); OpenCode MCP OAuth refresh fragility (#63008/#63012); Copilot CLI Entra `/common` authority mismatch forcing per-session reauth (#5402); Pi's `tool_search` failing to surface direct MCP tools (#11921); Gemini CLI's >128 tools ⇒ HTTP 400 (#24246). **MCP moved from novelty to infrastructure, and its rough edges are now user-visible.** **f) Remote/approval workflow automation** — *Codex, Copilot CLI, Pi* Multiple independent Codex discussions (#60441 Tapproval/Apple Watch, #60116 Pushary/phone, #59121 agent-harness hooks) target structured remote approval; Copilot CLI's trusted-access linkage (#4322); Pi's `pi auth` standalone credential flow. **Approval is being decoupled from the terminal.** --- ## 4. Differentiation Analysis | Tool | Focus | Target User | Technical Approach | |---|---|---|---| | **Claude Code** | Enterprise-grade harness with broadest surface (CLI, Desktop, mobile Remote Control, Cowork VM, browser) | Professional/enterprise devs | Anthropic-hosted models (Fable 5.2, 1M context); heavy Cowork/VM footprint; per-surface permission model | | **Codex** | Windows Desktop + Computer Use flagship; Rust core with alpha-release discipline | Desktop-first devs, MCP integrators | Rust (`rust-v*` tags); `PermissionProfile` migration; heavy automated PR pipeline (copyberry bot) | | **Gemini CLI** | Agent reliability & code intelligence; harness depth | Agent-runtime engineers, power users | AST-aware tooling roadmap (#22745); OS-sandbox proposals (#19873); aggressive `priority/p1` rollup triage | | **Copilot CLI** | Enterprise/security posture on GitHub's platform | GitHub-centric enterprise teams | tgrep shared indexing, enumerate-only Windows FS grants, per-subdomain approvals, GHE data-residency features | | **OpenCode** | Free-tier accessibility + open extensibility | Cost-sensitive individual devs, plugin authors | Free tier as loss-leader; GUI plugin architecture; embeddings stack being built (`@​opencode/ai`) | | **Pi** | TUI polish + durable execution + provider breadth | Terminal purists, local-model users | `pi-durable` execution layer, `pi-windows-*` zips, thin-provider-abstraction design | | **Qwen Code** | Multi-surface (CLI/Desktop/SDK) + messenger/channel platform | APAC ecosystem, QQ/WeChat/DingTalk integrators | Channel-first architecture (WebShell), Tauri desktop, GitHub/Java CI lanes | **Sharpest contrasts:** - **Platform breadth vs. depth**: Claude Code owns the most surfaces but leaks the most bugs (Windows memory governor #92059, macOS permission prompts); Gemini CLI owns the narrowest surface but invests deepest in agent-internals correctness (silent success misreporting, hook crashes). - **Enterprise vs. individual**: Copilot CLI and Claude Code optimize for compliance/security (token masking, role semantics); OpenCode and Qwen Code optimize for reach (free tier, chat-channel integrations). - **TUI/durable vs. Desktop/Computer-Use**: Pi and OpenCode treat the terminal as the product; Codex and Copilot treat the desktop as the product. --- ## 5. Community Momentum & Maturity **Tier 1 — High-velocity, mature platforms** - **Gemini CLI**: highest raw activity today (50 issues + 38 PRs), disciplined `p1` rollups, but plagued by CI noise and long-lived silently-mis-succeeding subagent bugs. - **Codex**: three alpha releases + 20 closed PRs in 24h; but **all PRs bot-authored and zero human PRs**, and the hottest issue is a month-old quota tracker — high throughput, lower community self-service signal. - **Qwen Code**: coordinated CLI/Desktop/SDK release, strongest CI problem (6 top issues are CI failures), maintainer responsiveness to API-budget requests suggests a briefly-overextended but well-run operation. **Tier 2 — Established with concentrated community pain** - **Claude Code**: only one PR in 24h (though substantive), but four distinct Windows/macOS bug clusters and the highest-reaction security request in the dataset (passkey #84862, 171 👍). Community is loud; maintainer PR velocity is thin. - **Copilot CLI**: 29 issues, zero PRs updated — healthy issue backlog, quiet merge cadence; strongest enterprise-specific feature stream (data-residency token masking, subdomain approval). - **OpenCode**: #59387 alone has 339 comments — **the single largest community thread across all seven tools** — which is simultaneously a momentum signal and a reputational risk (free-tier crisis). **Tier 3 — Niche but rapidly iterating** - **Pi**: strongest human-authored PR throughput of the day (petrroll's Windows-fix wave), a 96-comment meta-thread signaling genuine investment in a platform (Windows) the maintainers are still deciding whether to own, and the fastest credential-UX fix (#11977 closed same-day). **Highest signal-to-noise of any tool today.** **Maturity scoring (qualitative):** Gemini CLI and Codex have the most mature engineering pipelines; Claude Code has the most mature enterprise surface; Pi and OpenCode are the most responsive to individual contributors; Qwen Code has the most visible organizational strain (CI). --- ## 6. Trend Signals **1. The connector/integration reliability gap is now the #1 shipping risk.** Claude Code's Docs connector returns 403/404 (#108161); Codex Computer Use fails across localized Chrome (#54474, #59380); Copilot CLI's MCP Entra flow forces per-session reauth. **Shipping a connector that half-works now costs more trust than not shipping it.** For decision-makers: treat integration reliability SLAs (not feature lists) as the procurement differentiator. **2. "Silent success" is the most dangerous agent failure mode.** Gemini CLI's `Termination Reason: "GOAL"` on failure (#22323, #21983), Codex's premature task termination (#50771, #36596), and OpenCode's compaction dropping tool outputs (#62481) all confirm: **when the harness reports success but the work failed, automation becomes unusable.** Expect "verification hooks" and evidence-backed review skills (#58849) to become standard harness primitives. **3. Quota trust is eroding faster than quota efficiency is improving.** Copilot CLI's doubled prompt counting (#5392), OpenCode's shared-vs-per-model docs drift (#60311), and Codex's #41220 all point to the same conclusion: **users no longer trust provider accounting and are building their own ledgers** (cct #58359 in Codex discussions). Vendors that publish a verifiable local ledger will have a real moat. **4. Windows remains the industry's neglected platform.** Every single tool in this dataset has Windows-specific pain points — Claude Code's memory governor and Remote Control persistence, Codex's project loss and hidden taskbar, Copilot CLI's PowerShell hangs, OpenCode's renderer crashes and console spawning, Pi's 96-comment meta-thread and GitHub-detection regressions. **Windows users are systematically underserved across the field** — a real opening for whichever vendor commits first. **5. Agent orchestration is formalizing.** Pi's Redux/Saga proposal (#11984), Codex's worktree orchestrators (#58834, #60282), and Gemini CLI's unified-agent-loop request (#15327) all argue the same thing: **the community is outgrowing ad-hoc agent supervision and wants structured orchestration patterns** (sagas, handoff verification, receipts). Developers building adjacent tooling should target this gap now. **6. Enterprise security reviews are becoming gating items.** Copilot CLI's token masking under GHE data residency (#5388), trusted-access linkage (#4322), and browser-use plugin documentation for enterprise review (#5389) show that **enterprise procurement now requires the same audit trail that individual devs want for debugging.** Fields like "trusted access for cyber" and "audit-logged destructive actions" (OpenCode #63018) will become table-stakes. **7. Bot-generated backlog is a growing ecosystem tax.** Qwen Code's "provisional / no test identified" CI issues (#14724, #13078), Codex's all-bot PR stream, and Gemini CLI's maintainer-only rollups all indicate that **automated tooling is beginning to drown human signal**. The tools that invest in smart triage/budget-aware polling (Qwen's ETag PRs #16741) will keep contributor velocity where others lose it. --- ### Bottom Line for Technical Decision-Makers - **Choose on reliability surfaces, not feature lists.** Every tool can now call tools, use MCP, and run subagents. What separates them is whether permissions are honored, compaction preserves semantics, and failures are reported honestly. - **Gemini CLI and Codex** offer the most mature engineering cadence today; **Claude Code** offers the most enterprise surface; **Pi** is the best barometer for where the power-user community is heading (Windows, durable storage, TUI polish). - **Watch two threads closely:** OpenCode #59387 (whether free-tier economics are sustainable) and the cross-vendor quota-accounting debates — the first vendor to ship a **verifiable, local usage ledger** will likely win durable developer trust in 2027. --- ## Per-Tool Reports
Claude Code — anthropics/claude-code ## Claude Code Skills Highlights > Source: [anthropics/skills](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills) # Claude Code Skills — Community Highlights Report *Data as of 2026-11-10 | Source: github.com/anthropics/skills* --- ## 1. Top Skills Ranking (by PR attention) > Note: The dataset does not expose per-PR comment counts (all `Comments: undefined`), so ranking below reflects overall community attention inferred from issue linkage, revision activity, ecosystem discussion, and topical salience. **1. mcp-builder — MCP v2 compatibility fix** - **Function:** Generates MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers; the failing script is the connection helper. - **Highlights:** Fixes #1668. Adapts to the `mcp>=2.0.0` rename of `streamablehttp_client` → `streamable_http_client` and the new `create_mcp_http_client` header pattern. Touches the most plumbing-sensitive part of the Skills stack (MCP transport), so it has broad downstream impact. - **Status:** OPEN (created 2026-09-08, last updated 2026-10-08) - **Link:** https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/pull/1742 **2. skill-creator — Trigger-eval isolation & cross-platform fixes** - **Function:** The meta-skill that teaches Claude to author and evaluate other skills. - **Highlights:** Addresses false-miss/negative-pass scoring in trigger evals from per-worker probe competition, Windows `select()` on subprocess pipes, and unrelated tool interference. Directly tied to the contested Issue #556 (0% trigger rate) and #1352 (UUID cross-matching). - **Status:** OPEN (2026-06-10 → 2026-09-16) - **Link:** https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/pull/1298 **3. notion-spec-to-implementation + quantitative-resume-auditor (dual-skill PR)** - **Function:** Transforms Notion specs into implementable task breakdowns; plus a resume-auditing skill. - **Highlights:** One of the few PRs bundling two new community skills. The Notion spec-to-task flow is a rare "PM-to-agent" bridge, which is a high-demand workflow direction. - **Status:** OPEN (2026-06-02 → 2026-10-15) - **Link:** https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/pull/1245 **4. docx — Timeout & revision-mark verification fix** - **Function:** Word document generation/editing. - **Highlights:** Fixes a false-success bug where `soffice` timeouts were reported as successful; adds verification that `w:ins`/`w:del`/`w:moveFrom`/`w:moveTo` revision marks were actually cleared. Relevant to the broader docx correctness cluster (see Issue #2018 on invalid merged-run XML). - **Status:** OPEN (2026-09-19 → 2026-11-01) - **Link:** https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/pull/1792 **5. webapp-testing — Security hardening (`shell=True` removal)** - **Function:** End-to-end testing of web apps via scripted browser/server flows. - **Highlights:** Removes `subprocess.Popen(..., shell=True)` in `with_server.py`, closing a CWE-78 command-injection vector when agent/user command strings flow into a system shell. Signals that the community is starting to audit shipped skills for security, not just features. - **Status:** OPEN (2026-10-06 → 2026-11-01) - **Link:** https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/pull/1980 **6. pyxel — Retro game development** - **Function:** Building/debugging/verifying Pyxel retro games in Python, with headless input-driven runs and frame inspection. - **Highlights:** One of the longest-lived open PRs (since March 2026). Stands in for the "creative/indie dev" category that otherwise has little representation in the official set. - **Status:** OPEN (2026-03-05 → 2026-11-01) - **Link:** https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/pull/525 **7. xlsx — External link resolution in `recalc.py`** - **Function:** Excel spreadsheet recalculation and external-reference risk detection. - **Highlights:** Fixes #2013 — `external_links_at_risk` only inspected workbook-level defined names, missing worksheet-scoped aliases and indirect references, producing false negatives on formulas pointing at external workbooks. - **Status:** OPEN (2026-10-14 → 2026-11-03) - **Link:** https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/pull/2019 **8. md2video-audio / proofcore-contract-auditor (emerging long-tail)** - **Function:** Markdown → MP4 with TTS voiceover via Marp; and Solidity/Rust static analysis with TON blockchain audit anchoring. - **Highlights:** Illustrate the two fastest-growing long-tail categories: media generation and Web3/smart-contract auditing. Both are self-contained, single-purpose skills — exactly the pattern the community is now favoring. - **Status:** OPEN - **Links:** https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/pull/1703 · https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/pull/1771 --- ## 2. Community Demand Trends (from Issues) Ranked by comment volume and 👍 signal: | Trend | Signal Issue | What the community wants | |---|---|---| | **Namespace trust & provenance** | [#492](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/issues/492) (46💬, 3👍) | Stop community skills from shipping under `anthropic/`; users may grant elevated permissions to non-official skills. Comments are highest in the entire tracker — this is the #1 concern. | | **Org-wide skill distribution** | [#228](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/issues/228) (17💬, 8👍) | Shared skill libraries inside a Claude.ai org instead of manually emailing `.skill` files. High 👍 ratio = strong product intent. | | **Skill-trigger truthfulness** | [#556](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/issues/556) (13💬, 7👍) | `run_eval.py` reports 0% trigger rate with `claude -p`; the eval harness itself is unreliable. Corroborated by [#1352](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/issues/1352) (multi-worker UUID cross-match). | | **Context budget** | [#1487](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/issues/1487) (5💬) | `claude-api` eagerly injects ~156k tokens, blowing the context window in one tool call. Demand for lazy/progressive SKILL.md loading. | | **Tooling/governance skills** | [#412](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/issues/412), [#1385](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/issues/1385), [#1329](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/issues/1329) | Agent-governance patterns, a three-gate "reasoning quality" pipeline, and a symbolic compact-memory notation. All are meta-workflow / agent-reliability proposals. | | **Skill-authoring best practice** | [#202](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/issues/202) (CLOSED, 8💬) | `skill-creator` reads like developer docs; wants concise, operational, token-efficient instructions. | | **Descriptions that say *when*, not just *what*** | [#2064](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/issues/2064) | Frontmatter descriptions must be trigger-oriented, not feature-oriented. | **Distilled new-Skill directions the community most wants:** 1. Security & provenance tooling (namespace verification, permission auditing) 2. Quality-gate / reasoning-verification pipelines 3. Memory & context compression 4. Spec → implementation workflow automation 5. Reliability fixes to *existing* bundled skills (docx, xlsx, webapp-testing, skill-creator) --- ## 3. High-Potential Pending Skills (Open PRs, active within last ~30 days) These are unmerged but have strong momentum and low merge risk (small, verifiable fixes): 1. **PPTX — `--cols` input validation** ([#1975](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/pull/1975)) — Fail-fast argparse instead of a ValueError after LibreOffice render. 2. **webapp-testing — element discovery fix** ([#1976](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/pull/1976)) — `textarea`/`select` were misreported as `text`. 3. **algorithmic-art — `wrapAround()` correctness** ([#1977](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/pull/1977)) — Modulo wraps negatives into `[0, max)`; fixes #1897. 4. **skill-creator — YAML frontmatter parsing** ([#1997](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/pull/1997)) — Preserve quoted scalars and escaped characters through eval/optimization. 5. **pdf — case-sensitive file references** ([#538](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/pull/538)) — `REFERENCE.md`/`FORMS.md` → lowercase; breaks on Linux/macOS. 6. **claude-api — dead documentation URLs** ([#1730](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/pull/1730)) — 3 hard-404s verified by `curl -sI -L`. 7. **docs — clarify document-skills snapshot status** ([#2108](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/pull/2108)) — Explains the sync relationship to `~/.claude/skills/synced/`; resolves confusion behind Issue #189 (duplicate skills). 8. **scnet-hpc — HPC cluster operations** ([#1615](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/pull/1615)) — Slurm + SSH profiles; a niche but well-scoped new skill. **Best merge bets:** #1975, #1976, #1977 (each a one-line-logic fix tied to a filed issue, by an author with a clean PR cluster) and #1730 (documentation-only). --- ## 4. Skills Ecosystem Insight > **The community's most concentrated demand is trust and correctness of the skill harness itself — not more skills:** users are loudly asking for namespace/provenance integrity, reliable trigger evaluation, and bounded context injection, which together determine whether any skill can be safely discovered and executed at all. --- # Claude Code Community Digest — 2026-11-10 ## 1. Today's Highlights Two releases landed: **v2.1.322** adds Vertex fast mode across global/US/EU regions, while **v2.1.321** introduces **Claude Fable 5.2** as the new default Fable model (1M context, $8/$40 per Mtok) and a `--settings ` flag for `claude remote-control`. On the issue tracker, the highest-engagement item remains the passkey/WebAuthn sign-in request (#84862, 171 👍), and a cluster of permission-handling bugs on macOS and Windows continues to dominate activity. ## 2. Releases **v2.1.322** - Added fast mode on Vertex in global, US, and EU regions, with automatic fallback to standard speed if Vertex refuses the request. **v2.1.321** - Added **Claude Fable 5.2** (`claude-fable-5-2`) — now the default Fable model. 1M context window, $8/$40 per Mtok, $0.20/Mtok cache reads. - Added `--settings ` to `claude remote-control`, applying a settings file to every session it launches (note: mid-run file changes do not apply to new sessions, per the truncated changelog). ## 3. Hot Issues 1. **[#84862](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/84862)** — *Passkey (WebAuthn) sign-in across every surface* (33 comments, 171 👍). Long-running top-voted enhancement; consensus is that password-based auth is the weakest link in Claude's account security story. 2. **[#93201](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/93201)** — *Built-in browser ignores Allowed sites for internal hostnames* (24 comments, 37 👍). macOS Cowork browser prompts on every action for `*.habifino.local` with "site-level permissions disabled" — a serious blocker for private-network workflows. 3. **[#12748](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/12748)** — *Add `cwd` parameter to Task tool for Git worktrees* (19 comments, 30 👍). A year-old request still drawing attention; subagent worktree isolation remains awkward without it. 4. **[#56089](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/56089)** — *Configurable VM bundle (vhdx) storage location on Windows* (17 comments, 62 👍). High-reaction request driven by disk-space pain from Cowork's VM image placement. 5. **[#103832](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/103832)** — *Bypass mode still prompts on `start_session`* (12 comments, 19 👍). Regression: `mcp__ccd_session__start_session` now needs two approvals even in Bypass — direct violation of the mode's contract. 6. **[#100114](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/100114)** — *Windows: Remote Control not restored after relaunch* (10 comments). Sessions silently archive on mobile after desktop restarts; Remote Control state persistence is unreliable. 7. **[#108161](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/108161)** — *Docs connector output unreachable to the session* (4 comments). Delete implementation-only or unjustified cases instead of recreating private construction. Genuine non-API library contracts may move to their owning package with explicit boundary rationale.

Historical scope and receipts: [#33778](https://github.com/okou-ai/okou/issues/33778). No implementation, workflow configuration, active PR or release was changed by this issue consolidation.

### Decide the scenario before preserving the test

1. Establish the meaningful user/product behavior, and whether the case instead overtests internal state or a contrived race a user would hardly encounter.
2. Delete unjustified cases and their now-unused db helpers/test APIs, or rewrite valuable cases through **existing normal production APIs accessible to external users or genuine webhooks/Runner callbacks**, with externally observable outcomes.
3. If normal APIs cannot construct the case, reconsider its value. Do not preserve it by replacing a test API with an in-process db helper, private worker driver, renamed wrapper or new test-only product endpoint.

The full construction and execution chain matters; a public final assertion does not legitimize private setup. Prior exception labels do not automatically override this rule. Preserve valuable publicly constructible behavior; explain every deleted case/group and lost boundary.

Only batch019 was executed; the existing watcher owns continuation, with the late cleanup failure explicitly retained and Crates terminal status now verified.

[PR #37918 corrective manifest](https://github.com/okou-ai/okou/blob/3412a46cc7e22a2295b10fe0a2419cd980bb420c/docs/implementation/issue-37440-correction/README.md) and [merged receipt](https://github.com/okou-ai/okou/issues/37440#issuecomment-6049442273).

<details>
<summary>Superseded issue text — historical evidence only, not current instructions</summary>

## Current milestone: retire all test-only API endpoints

**Scope reset by Ethan on 2026-10-06:** start by retiring every test-only API endpoint. The comprehensive classification of the entire API test suite is deferred; it is not a prerequisite for this milestone.

### Acceptance

- Zero remaining test-only HTTP operations (method + path) across the refreshed repository inventory, including `/api/test/*`, test-only CLI/provisioning paths, guarded preview/QA routes and locally declared test-support contracts.
- Their actual API/E2E/QA consumers are migrated or retired; obsolete HTTP handlers, registrations, contracts, actions and wrappers are removed. Renaming or moving a test-only endpoint does not satisfy retirement.
- Ordinary business setup and observation use production APIs, webhooks/Runner flows and external effects. Do not simply move arbitrary private row reads/writes into new helpers.
- Necessary existing approved financial/security/historical/clock fixtures, scoped real-worker invocation and owned cleanup retain their exact guarantees through appropriate scoped non-HTTP test harnesses or real production entry points. Their former HTTP transport is also retired. A concrete unresolved replacement/coverage issue stays an explicit blocker, not an exception to the zero-endpoint goal.
- Current-HEAD independent review, required CI and the protected merge queue pass. Keep this issue open for Ethan to assess phase completion and the next priority; partial PRs use `Refs #37440`.

### Execution and progress

Work by endpoint family and its actual callers. **The previous minimum of 30 test cases per PR no longer applies to this phase.** A small complete retirement is eligible; a necessary preparatory change must identify the endpoint dependency it closes. Do not add unrelated tests merely to reach a quota, or inventory all tests before starting.

Track baseline/new discoveries, retired operations/paths/actions, remaining operations, exact callers, active PR and blockers. A starting source audit at `874eccdba54c094f8f181cc57a4c8b0ae1bd9d98` found **73 known test/preview HTTP operations, 68 unique paths and 191 actions**; refresh this against current main, including nonstandard paths. Temporary mocked external-provider routes and synthetic HTTP-framework probes are a separate test mechanism, not shipped test-support endpoints.

[Source/caller audit and historical case reconciliation](https://app.okou.ai/artifacts/rxg9t7ut52.zip). The 5,389-case census and confirmed 122-case lower bound remain supporting historical evidence, not the current milestone denominator. Historical completion credit and all 34 exact user decisions remain preserved; this scope reset grants no blanket loss of business/financial/security coverage.

Keep the existing implementation thread, workflow and completion watcher. Preserve any owned active PR and finish its normal protected lifecycle; select subsequent work by endpoints. No local Vitest/dev server, longer timeouts, added retries, relaxed assertions, protection bypass or production/release changes.

<details>
<summary>Original broader goal and context — preserved for the later whole-suite phase</summary>

## Context

While implementing #37421 (PR #37430), we decided that API tests should assert only externally observable behavior: HTTP responses, chat events, whether a run is created, public read endpoints, and replies delivered to integrations. They should not read database rows to make assertions.

#37430 only cleans up the tests on the pick / enqueue / claim / run-preparation path. Outside that path, roughly 110 API test files (counted at #37430 head `ae1ca18`) still read tables directly, via `.select(...)` / `.from(...)` or DB fixtures, to assert state.

## Goal

Across the rest of the API test suite, replace database-row assertions with assertions on externally observable results, module by module.

## Rules

- Assert only what a user or client can observe: HTTP responses, public read APIs, chat events, run creation or rejection, and integration replies.
- Build scenarios only through public APIs, run callbacks, the controllable app clock (`mockNow`), and test-environment configuration. Do not write rows directly to construct internal states.
- If a scenario cannot be built through public APIs, or it only checks an extreme race or an internal property, delete the test rather than keep a DB-level construction.
- Do not wait on wall-clock time (`expect.poll` / `vi.waitFor`). Drain background work with `flushWaitUntilForTest()`.
- Do not widen timeouts or add retries.

## Suggested approach

- Inventory the files by module (billing, storage/artifacts, connectors, integrations, workflows, auth, and so on). Then take them in batches, one PR per module group.
- In each PR, list the removed assertions and the observable assertion that replaces each one.

## Acceptance

- No API test asserts on database rows read directly from tables.
- No API test constructs internal state by writing rows directly, unless an explicitly documented exception exists.

items.title: PRD: Recruitment application-review agent (Gmail + Streak)

labels.name: ready-for-agent
