items.body:
# AI CLI 工具社区动态日报 2026-09-05 > 生成时间: 2026-09-04 16:09 UTC | 覆盖工具: 7 个 - [Claude Code](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code) - [OpenAI Codex](https://github​.com/openai/codex) - [Gemini CLI](https://github​.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli) - [GitHub Copilot CLI](https://github​.com/github/copilot-cli) - [OpenCode](https://github​.com/anomalyco/opencode) - [Pi](https://github​.com/earendil-works/pi) - [Qwen Code](https://github​.com/QwenLM/qwen-code) - [Claude Code Skills](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills) --- ## 横向对比 ⚠️ 横向对比生成失败。 --- ## 各工具详细报告
Claude Code — anthropics/claude-code ## Claude Code Skills 社区热点 > 数据来源: [anthropics/skills](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills) # Claude Code Skills Community Highlights **Data snapshot:** 2026-09-05 | **Source:** `github.com/anthropics/skills` All PRs below are open as of the snapshot. PR comment counts were not fully exposed in the data, so “attention” is inferred from linked issues, duplicate-fix activity, update recency, and scope. --- ## 1. Top Skills Ranking Most-discussed / most-active skill areas, based on community attention. ### 1. `skill-creator` evaluation tooling — the most concentrated activity Multiple independent PRs target the same broken `run_eval.py` path: skills are never triggered in headless eval, causing `recall=0%` on every description. This undermines the optimizer loop in `skill-creator`. - Functionality: `skill-creator` scaffolds, validates, and optimizes Claude Skills; `run_eval.py` measures whether candidate skill descriptions actually trigger. - Discussion highlights: issue [#556](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/issues/556) reports a 0% trigger rate across all queries; PRs [#1298](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/pull/1298), [#1099](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/pull/1099), and [#1050](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/pull/1050) independently identify Windows subprocess/pipe failures, eval artifact installation problems, and encoding bugs. - Status: open; the cluster is the clearest signal that the community wants reliable skill evaluation before adding more skills. ### 2. Document / office-format skills A multi-PR family focused on making Claude a trustworthy producer and editor of document files. - [PR #486 — ODT skill](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/pull/486): create, fill, read, and convert OpenDocument `.odt` / `.ods` files; also converts ODT to HTML. - [PR #514 — document-typography](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/pull/514): typographic quality control for generated documents — orphaned words, stranded headers, numbering misalignment. - [PR #541 — DOCX tracked-change fix](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/pull/541): prevents OOXML `w:id` collisions with existing bookmarks, which corrupt documents. - [PR #538 — PDF reference fix](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/pull/538): corrects case-sensitive file references in `SKILL.md`, important for case-sensitive filesystems. Status: all open. The breadth suggests strong demand for document-generation quality and repair, not just raw file creation. ### 3. `mcp-builder` reliability - [PR #1602](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/pull/1602) addresses multiple `mcp-builder` defects: MCP result text not extracted before serialization, benchmark metric errors, encoding problems, and script instability. - Related issue [#1390](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/issues/1390) shows `evaluation.py` silently fabricates tool errors against real MCP servers, so the driven agent scores 0/N. - Functionality: `mcp-builder` is the skill for building and evaluating MCP servers; it is essential to Claude Code ecosystem extensibility. - Status: open, with active fixes being proposed. ### 4. Hivemind — zero-cost multi-agent orchestration [PR #1628](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/pull/1628) - Functionality: lets Claude Code delegate mechanical work to headless `opencode` workers running on free models, while Claude Code remains planner, reviewer, and merger. - Discussion highlights: positions expensive-model context as the scarce resource and proposes cheap worker delegation as the answer. - Status: open and recently updated; a strong candidate for community interest in orchestration and cost control. ### 5. self-audit — reasoning quality gate [PR #1367](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/pull/1367) - Functionality: audits AI output before delivery — first verifies every claimed output file exists, then performs a four-dimension reasoning audit in damage-severity order. - Discussion highlights: complementary issue [#1385](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/issues/1385) proposes a three-gate pipeline: pre-task calibration, adversarial review, and delivery verification. - Status: open. Represents a visible community push for verifiable output quality, not just better generation. ### 6. testing-patterns [PR #723](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/pull/723) - Functionality: comprehensive testing coverage — Testing Trophy philosophy, unit-test patterns, React component testing with Testing Library, edge cases, and what not to test. - Significance: fills a broad demand for technical-testing guidance inside Claude Code skills. - Status: open. ### 7. `claude-api` model data maintenance [PR #1607](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/pull/1607) - Functionality: marks four retired model IDs as retired in the `claude-api` skill. - Discussion highlights: related issue [#1487](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/issues/1487) warns that the `claude-api` skill eagerly injects ~156k tokens, exhausting the context window. Model metadata accuracy is important, but context-efficiency is the bigger unresolved concern. - Status: open. ### 8. ServiceNow platform skill [PR #568](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/pull/568) - Functionality: broad ServiceNow platform assistant covering ITSM, ITOM, ITAM/SAM, FSM, HRSD, SecOps, SPM/PPM, CSDM, and IntegrationHub. - Significance: signals enterprise workflow/automation demand beyond generic coding skills. - Status: open. --- ## 2. Community Demand Trends Distilled from issue activity: ### Security and trust boundaries [Issue #492](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/issues/492) is the single most-commented issue at **43 comments**: community-made skills distributed under the `anthropic/` namespace impersonate official Anthropic skills, creating a trust-boundary vulnerability. Related demand includes secure handling of SharePoint Online documents ([#1175](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/issues/1175)) and agent governance patterns ([#412](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/issues/412)). ### Enterprise org-wide skill sharing [Issue #228](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/issues/228) — **16 comments** — asks for org-wide skill sharing directly in Claude.ai rather than manual `.skill` file transfer. Supporting lifecycle pain shows in duplicate plugin contents ([#189](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/issues/189)) and disappearing skills ([#62](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/issues/62)). ### Reliable evaluation and skill-authoring tooling [Issue #556](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/issues/556) — **12 comments** — reports `run_eval.py` never triggers skills, so skill optimization is “optimizing against noise.” Related tooling defects appear in `mcp-builder` ([#1390](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/issues/1390)) and `web-artifacts-builder` ([#1362](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/issues/1362)). The community wants authoring/evaluation infrastructure hardened before skills are scaled. ### Context-window efficiency and token discipline [Issue #1487](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/issues/1487) reports the `claude-api` skill injects ~156k tokens in one tool call. Duplicate skills from plugin overlap ([#189](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/issues/189)) also waste context. Demand is clear: skills must be lightweight, discoverable, and non-redundant. ### New skill directions Emerging proposals center on **agent memory compaction** ([#1329 — compact-memory](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/issues/1329)), **AI agent governance** ([#412](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/issues/412)), and **quality-gate pipelines** ([#1385](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/issues/1385)). The community is moving from “make Claude do X” toward “make Claude reliably govern, audit, and remember X.” --- ## 3. High-Potential Pending Skills These open PRs have strong product fit, active issue linkage, or unusually concrete scope — so they may land soon: - **[PR #1628 — Hivemind](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/pull/1628)** — multi-agent orchestration with free headless workers; recent, cost-driven, and immediately understandable. - **[PR #1607 — claude-api model retirement update](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/pull/1607)** — small, factual, and likely to merge once model metadata is corrected. - **[PR #1602 — mcp-builder fixes](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/pull/1602)** — directly addresses documented evaluation failures against real MCP servers. - **[PR #1367 — self-audit](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/pull/1367)** — aligns with the quality-gate pipeline issue [#1385](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/issues/1385). - **[PR #723 — testing-patterns](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/pull/723)** — broad, well-structured testing coverage useful to almost every Claude Code user. - **[PR #486 — ODT skill](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/pull/486)** — fills the missing OpenDocument gap in the document-format family. - **[PR #83 — skill-quality-analyzer and skill-security-analyzer](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/pull/83)** — meta-skills that directly target issue [#492](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/issues/492); likely to gain attention as security requirements tighten. - **[PR #514 — document-typography](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/pull/514)** — addresses a concrete quality problem in AI-generated documents with minimal scope. --- ## 4. Skills Ecosystem Insight The Claude Code Skills community is concentrating less on individual end-user domains and more on **making Skills themselves trustworthy, evaluable, context-efficient, and governable** — security analyzers, reliable eval harnesses, audit gates, and compact memory are the next bottleneck to solve before the catalog can safely expand. --- # Claude Code Community Digest — 2026-09-05 ## Today’s Highlights Anthropic shipped v2.1.260, adding an in-conversation diff panel for fullscreen mode and surfacing likely prompt-cache miss causes in `/cost`. The community remains heavily focused on Windows relaunch/update failure classes and `/tmp/claude-*-cwd` cleanup, while several fresh enhancement requests push toward richer hook APIs, multi-account support, and cross-session coordination. ## Releases ### [v2.1.260](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/releases/tag/v2.1.260) - Added a diff panel that opens beside the conversation in fullscreen mode and shows uncommitted changes as Claude edits. Toggle with `/diff`. - Added likely causes for prompt-cache misses to `/cost`, including tool-definition/system-prompt changes and idle time past the TTL. ## Hot Issues 1. **[Claude Code Desktop fails to relaunch on Windows due to orphaned process file lock](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/42776)** — The most-commented issue in this window (155 comments / 73👍). Windows users report relaunch failures after an orphaned process keeps the app file locked, making updates effectively unusable until a manual cleanup or reboot. 2. **[Memory leak: missing cleanup for `/tmp/claude-*-cwd` working directory files](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/8856)** — Long-running Linux/WSL sessions leak temp working-directory tracking files (111 comments / 71👍). This is an old issue still receiving attention, affecting CI-style automation and memory usage. 3. **[Desktop window stays always-on-top on Windows with no setting to disable it](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/85891)** — Highest-reacted issue this round (84 comments / 175👍). Windows users are frustrated by Claude Desktop remaining above all windows; the report has been filed as a Windows counterpart to #66516. 4. **[Function Hooks: make plugins 10x more powerful](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/91870)** — Fresh architectural proposal for side-effect-tracked hooks with a parameterized `$` object and Express/Koa-style `next` composition. The 84-comment conversation signals real community appetite for a deeper plugin model. 5. **[Opus claude-opus-4-8 emits unparseable tool calls at ~1.5% rate](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/64774)** — Users report a model-specific regression: opus-4-8 fails on tool-call parsing at a noticeable rate while opus-4-7 and sonnet-4-6 show a 0% failure rate. High impact for agentic workflows. 6. **[Cowork on Windows: `mcp__workspace__bash` denied in every session after update](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/91594)** — A permissions regression between desktop versions (1.40609.1.0 → 1.44121.1.0). Windows Cowork users see workspace Bash tool calls denied despite no config changes. 7. **[MSIX: `git fsmonitor--daemon` inherits AppX job and blocks relaunch](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/91763)** — A detailed root-cause report for the 0x80070020 failure family. The daemon spawned by Claude Code survives a forced update shutdown and blocks the new version from starting. 8. **[Desktop cross-machine session mix-up: Windows input executes in an unrelated macOS session](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/91511)** — A serious session-isolation bug in the desktop app. Commands typed in a Windows session were executed and displayed in a different macOS session without appearing in the Windows session list. 9. **[Auto Mode Bash-first instruction silently disables nested CLAUDE.md rules](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/90450)** — Users found that Auto Mode’s “Bash-first” instruction stops Claude from loading nested `CLAUDE.md` files and path-scoped rules, creating a potentially dangerous rule-governance gap. 10. **[Feature request: multiple account login and switching](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/30031)** — A frequent ask for users who switch between personal and work Claude accounts. The request is for `gh auth switch`-style account switching with visible active-account state (12 comments / 65👍). ## Key PR Progress Five PRs were active in the last 24 hours; all are captured here. 1. **[Add diagnostic script for GitHub connector showing “Connected” but no tools](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/pull/61691)** — Adds a PowerShell diagnostic/repair script for the Cowork GitHub MCP connector where the connector appears connected but exposes zero tools. References the related issue chain #28695 / #41658 / #5758 and closes #61682. 2. **[fix(security-guidance): make `**` glob patterns match zero-depth paths](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/pull/87079)** — Fixes a security-relevant glob mismatch: `_glob_match` delegated to `fnmatch`, where a bare `*` already crosses `/`, so `**/*.ts`—despite the documented promise—silently excludes top-level files from security-patterns rules. 3. **[Update /frontend-design SKILL.md](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/pull/91894)** — Closed PR that updates the `frontend-design` skill definition in the plugin/skills content. 4. **[docs: align code-review README with the current validation-based command](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/pull/79150)** — Removes stale documentation describing a git blame/history agent, a 0-100 confidence scoring system, and a nonexistent “80 threshold” config line. Brings the README in line with the actual validation-based code-review command. 5. **[validate-agent.sh: don’t abort at the first warning and stop false-flagging valid agents](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/pull/89404)** — Fixes issue #83803: `set -e` plus arithmetic expressions caused the script to terminate on the first warning and reject valid agent files. Improves reliability of the plugin-dev validation workflow. ## Feature Request Trends - **Deeper plugin/hook extensibility** — The Function Hooks proposal ([#91870](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/91870)) is the clearest signal: users want first-class, composable ways to alter behavior without patchwork deny hooks. - **Multi-account and multi-org workflows** — Accounts are still single-login in Claude Code. Requests call for account switching ([#30031](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/30031)), cross-device session resumption ([closed duplicate #47926](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/47926)), and Remote Control support for unattended/long-running server instances ([#92127](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/92127)). - **Cross-session coordination** — Heavy users running many independent Claude Code sessions against one repo want first-party coordination primitives, not self-built `PreToolUse` deny hooks ([#76727](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/76727)). - **More flexible integrations** — Multi-workspace support for the built-in Slack connector ([#44243](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/44243)) and Remote Control sessions with attachable terminals ([#87190](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/87190)) both continue to draw interest. - **Better output UI controls** — Users want a persistent default-collapsed state for tool-call output ([#91827](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/91827)) and more resilient Claude processes in VS Code’s `serve-web`/Agent Host environment ([#92102](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/92102)). ## Developer Pain Points - **Windows update/relaunch reliability** — Multiple active reports ([#42776](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/42776), [#91736](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/91736), [#91763](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/91763)) point to orphaned processes, file locks, and MSIX container/job issues that force reboots and block updates. - **Temp-file and memory hygiene** — The `/tmp/claude-*-cwd` leak ([#8856](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/8856)) remains the leading memory-related complaint, especially for long-running and unattended sessions. - **Rules being silently skipped** — Auto Mode’s Bash-first behavior disabling nested `CLAUDE.md` / path-scoped rules ([#90450](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/90450)) is a recurring governance concern, since it changes model behavior without visible warning. - **Session context and working-directory confusion** — Bugs such as unnecessary `cd` commands after `enterworktree` ([#92131](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/92131)) and misattributed interleaved shell output ([#92130](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/92130)) show that context tracking remains fragile in agentic multi-tool flows. - **Model-side parsing/format reliability** — Unparseable tool calls from newer frontier models ([#64774](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/64774)) undermine trust in fully autonomous runs.
OpenAI Codex — openai/codex # OpenAI Codex Community Digest — 2026-09-05 ## Today's Highlights Two stable patch releases shipped: rust-v0.153.1 enables API-only GPT-6-Astra configuration without touching the default model picker, and rust-v0.153.2 corrects the displayed Fast-tier speed label. PR activity concentrated on Guardian review infrastructure (per-model policies, ticket propagation, context retention), TUI quality-of-life fixes, and Windows sandbox/thread-history hardening. On the community side, Windows thread-history-corruption reports remain the loudest recurring theme, alongside renewed frustration about the return of the 5-hour usage limit. ## Releases - **rust-v0.153.2** — Bug-fix release correcting the GPT-6-Astra Fast tier description to “2x speed, increased usage” (display text only; no runtime change). [Changelog](https://github​.com/openai/codex/compare/rust-v0.153.1...rust-v0.153.2) - **rust-v0.153.1** — Adds API-level configuration support for GPT-6-Astra without changing the default model or surfacing it in the model picker. [Changelog](https://github​.com/openai/codex/compare/rust-v0.153.0...rust-v0.153.1) - **rust-v0.154.0-alpha.2 / alpha.3** — Pre-release snapshots of the 0.154.0 line; no detailed changelogs published. ## Hot Issues 1. **ChatGPT desktop repeatedly spawns Computer Use workers and crashes with V8 OOM on macOS** — [#38455](https://github​.com/openai/codex/issues/38455) (40 comments, 16 👍) The most active issue this cycle. On macOS 15.7.7 / Apple Silicon, the app reproducibly crashes ~98 seconds after launch via `node::OOMErrorHandler`, with 316 threads at crash (187 named `computer-use`). Users report it as a regression from 26.730.61639. 2. **Windows paginated thread history stalls on duplicate ordinal while rollout remains complete** — [#41079](https://github​.com/openai/codex/issues/41079) (23 comments, 2 👍) A local paginated thread shows only an older snapshot even though the canonical rollout JSONL is complete — a history-projection stall rather than transcript deletion. One of several related Windows reports this week. 3. **Paginated thread history projection stops at a `token_count` record** — [#40342](https://github​.com/openai/codex/issues/40342) (22 comments, 7 👍) Affects Linux x86_64 desktop with bundled CLI 0.145.0 and 0.149.0. The projection halts at a `token_count` record, suggesting a parser-level bug not confined to Windows. 4. **Windows floating pets become click-through and cannot be dragged** — [#41513](https://github​.com/openai/codex/issues/41513) (22 comments, 10 👍) Both the built-in Codey pet and custom pets lose hit-testing on Windows x64 across two app versions. High engagement for a non-core feature. 5. **Python SDK can drop an early `turn/completed` notification** — [#41078](https://github​.com/openai/codex/issues/41078) (14 comments) The SDK can wait indefinitely when a server emits `turn/*` notifications before the `turn/start` response; early `turn/completed` events are discarded before the turn queue is registered. Relevant to custom transports and server implementers. 6. **Ctrl+C exits Codex immediately; request double-press confirmation** — [#14708](https://github​.com/openai/codex/issues/14708) (9 comments, 21 👍) Open since March and still the highest-upvoted CLI enhancement in this batch. Users want parity with Claude Code's double-Ctrl+C guard against accidental exit. 7. **Computer Use can trigger memory runaway to 172 GB on macOS** — [#26738](https://github​.com/openai/codex/issues/26738) (9 comments, 2 👍) Desktop threads that use or restore Computer Use can drive Codex to 172 GB, making the machine effectively unusable. Complements the newer OOM crash report #38455. 8. **Codex Pet overlay reappears after being tucked away** — [#42243](https://github​.com/openai/codex/issues/42243) (9 comments, 15 👍) On macOS 26.6.2, the floating pet returns after selecting *Tuck Away*. Fifteen upvotes suggest a vocal pet-owner community. 9. **Resuming unfinished threads reuses rollout ordinals and permanently stalls paginated history** — [#41657](https://github​.com/openai/codex/issues/41657) (6 comments) Windows report where resume-after-interrupt reuses rollout ordinals, permanently freezing history. Likely shares root cause with #41079 and #42027. 10. **Permanent white window after second launch on fresh CODEX_HOME** — [#42515](https://github​.com/openai/codex/issues/42515) (6 comments) Microsoft Store MSIX build 26.901.1978.0 renders a white window after first launch, with a pricing webview appearing in the background. Blocks usage entirely for affected fresh installs. ## Key PR Progress 1. **Add app-server account session lifecycle** — [#25383](https://github​.com/openai/codex/pull/25383) Large Rust-side feature enabling Desktop multi-account profile switching. Adds `accountSession/login/start`, `accountSession/add`, `accountSession/list`, `accountSession/switch`, and `accountSession/logout` routes with session persistence. Open since May and still progressing. 2. **Honor model-provided Guardian review policies** — [#42744](https://github​.com/openai/codex/pull/42744) Adds optional per-model Guardian modes (disabled, synchronous, adaptive) for computer use, shell, code mode, file changes, MCP, network, and permission requests, while preserving legacy configuration semantics. 3. **Retain user instructions in guardian thread context** — [#42762](https://github​.com/openai/codex/pull/42762) Ensures Guardian review retains the original user instructions after compaction, resume, or rollback, since summarized/legacy checkpoints no longer establish a complete instruction history. 4. **Propagate response tickets to Guardian reviews** — [#42758](https://github​.com/openai/codex/pull/42758) Requests and parses server-issued Guardian tickets, scoping each ticket to the response that produced a review or classifier request — including HTTP and WebSocket retries. 5. **Preserve acceptance order in retained thread context** — [#42770](https://github​.com/openai/codex/pull/42770) Fixes a replay/rollback hazard where queued prompts and `request_user_input` answers could persist in a different order from host acceptance, preventing wrong rollback boundaries. 6. **Add direct SigV4 transport to exec-server** — [#42781](https://github​.com/openai/codex/pull/42781) Lets remote exec servers connect directly to AWS-hosted registries by adding `--remote-transport direct` with SigV4 profile, region, and service options for registry requests and WebSocket handshakes. 7. **Improve automatic thread naming in the TUI** — [#42749](https://github​.com/openai/codex/pull/42749) Fixes a race where automatic title generation only applied while the thread remained active, so switching threads could leave the originating thread without its generated name. 8. **Keep TUI prompt history tied to local settings** — [#42791](https://github​.com/openai/codex/pull/42791) Prompt-history metadata was derived from active server configuration. Improves visibility for transient provider errors. - [#47231 feat(opencode): add `run_in_background` to shell tool with auto notification](https://github​.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/47231) Removes the synchronous-shell limitation by supporting long-running background commands with automatic notifications. - [#47289 feat(tui): add manual todo management dialog](https://github​.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/47289) Closes #38550. Adds a `/todo` dialog so users can fix stale todo state when the agent forgets to clean it up. - [#47297 fix: bump pinned Bun to 1.4.1](https://github​.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/47297) Closes #29039. Addresses SIGILL crashes on x86 CPUs without AVX2 by lowering the CPU baseline to Bun’s standard support. - [#47300 feat(plugin): add `experimental.session.stopping` hook](https://github​.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/47300) Closes #16626. Gives plugins a hook that runs before a turn ends, unlike `session.idle`, which only fires after the loop breaks. - [#47307 feat(app): MCP server management in settings](https://github​.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/47307) Adds an MCP tab to desktop settings for add/edit/delete operations, including OAuth credential support. Lowering the friction for MCP adoption in the desktop app. ## Feature Request Trends - **OpenAI-compatible provider discovery**: Auto-discovery of models from local endpoints is the dominant feature request; users are tired of manual catalog maintenance. - **Richer plugin capabilities**: Persistent TUI footer hooks, session lifecycle hooks, session lists, and global event stream exposure are consistently requested by plugin authors. - **Autonomous and long-running session UX**: App-level auto-accept permissions, background shell execution, retry countdowns, manual todo management, and more resilient SSE behavior all target unattended operation. - **Desktop management surfaces**: Users want settings-level controls for MCP servers and plugins, improved worktree UI, and drag-and-drop session creation instead of relying on config files or TUI commands. - **Platform/runtime modernization**: Upgrading pinned Bun, QR-code pairing for `opencode serve`, and correcting `$PWD` vs process-cwd behavior reflect interest in robust deployment on varied hardware and headless environments. ## Developer Pain Points - **Auto-accept permissions are unreliable in the new layouts**: Multiple open and duplicate issues show that the new UI/Desktop builds silently disable autonomous permission approval, forcing developers back to manual supervision. - **Model/provider compatibility remains fragile**: Gemini 3.8 Flash, MiniMax-M3, and Ollama/OpenAI-compatible providers trigger failures such as “requests ending with a model turn,” silent `stop` finishes, and tool loops with no user query found. - **SSE/stream lifecycle is still a source of frustration**: Mobile tabs and backgrounded desktop tabs lose the event stream and require manual refresh; long-running agent sessions can also stall while appearing active. - **Zen quota and billing messaging confuses users**: Free models hit “usage exceeded,” subscriptions are not recognized, and the dashboard usage percentage incorrectly sums per-model percentages. - **Bootstrap and plugin install hangs block core workflows**: Missing timeouts on `models.opencode.ai` fetches and plugin dependency installs can block the first `/session` request for minutes. - **Shell and process semantics cause headless issues**: Synchronous shell is painful for long commands, and `opencode run` resolving the session directory from stale `$PWD` instead of actual cwd breaks subprocess-based tooling.
Pi — earendil-works/pi # Pi Community Digest — 2026-09-05 ## Today's Highlights v0.85.0 shipped with persistent Claude thinking effort, but a packaging defect in the published tarball — `dist/cli.js` statically imports the undeclared `@​earendil-works/pi-server` package — is breaking fresh installs with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` (#9132, #9140). The large system-prompt refactor (#8998) was closed and reworked into stacked follow-ups that add mid-conversation system messages (#9116) and system-message deltas (#9117). Several long-standing bugs also cleared triage with fixes landing for HTML export context loss (#9110) and JSONL session-ID collisions (#9111). ## Releases **v0.85.0** — Persistent Claude thinking effort: supported Anthropic transports now preserve per-turn effort and recover safely from signed-thinking mismatches. See [Model Configuration](https://github​.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v0.85.0/packages/coding-agent/docs/models.md#model-configuration). ⚠️ Caveat: the npm artifact has a missing-dependency regression; see [Hot Issues](#hot-issues), #9132/#9140. ## Hot Issues - **[#5363 — Add amazon-bedrock-mantle provider for OpenAI-compatible models](https://github​.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/5363)** — 17 comments, 15 👍. The most active open feature request: Bedrock Mantle models expose an OpenAI-compatible `/responses` endpoint and are incompatible with the existing Converse-API-based `amazon-bedrock` provider. Open since June and still highly desired. - **[#9132 — 0.85.0: published dist/cli.js statically imports @​earendil-works/pi-server, which is not a declared dependency](https://github​.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/9132)** — 4 👍. Release-blocking packaging regression confirmed by multiple users; the non-bundled build references a package absent from dependencies. - **[#9140 — coding-agent latest: ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND @​earendil-works/pi-server](https://github​.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/9140)** — Fresh install of `@​earendil-works/pi-coding-agent@​latest` fails at startup when importing `experimental/server.js`; the user-visible symptom of #9132. - **[#8720 — Tool result with whitespace-only output permanently bricks the session (HTTP 400)](https://github​.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/8720)** — OpenAI-compatible providers reject empty/whitespace-only tool content, and since the invalid message stays in history, every subsequent request fails. Needs a content filter before sending. - **[#9112 — 400 on resuming a long session: thinking blocks in the latest assistant message cannot be modified](https://github​.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/9112)** — Replaying saved Anthropic thinking blocks after resume triggers a hard 400 on every turn, even a bare `hello`. - **[#8684 — `PI_OFFLINE` silently disables all provider model discovery](https://github​.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/8684)** — Documented as limiting startup housekeeping (update/telemetry), but it actually disables provider model-catalog discovery for the whole session — an undocumented scope expansion that breaks model lists. - **[#8896 — /export HTML silently drops context that was sent to the model](https://github​.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/8896)** — Custom messages with `display: false` are documented as a TUI-only noise-reduction toggle, yet `/export` omits them entirely, losing context that genuinely reached the model. Fix landed in #9110. - **[#9105 — processFileArguments() silently corrupts binary file attachments](https://github​.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/9105)** — `@​file` mentions and the Read tool share a primitive that forces UTF-8 decoding, corrupting binary attachments via lossy conversion. - **[#9073 — JsonlSessionRepo rejects cwd-scoped IDs when directory encodings collide](https://github​.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/9073)** — `tenant-a/proje --- > ⚠️ 内容超过 GitHub Issue 上限，完整报告见提交的 Markdown 文件。

# AI Infrastructure Digest 2026-09-26 > Generated: 2026-09-26 00:51 UTC | Projects covered: 6 - [vLLM](https://github​.com/vllm-project/vllm) - [SGLang](https://github​.com/sgl-project/sglang) - [llama.cpp](https://github​.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp) - [Ollama](https://github​.com/ollama/ollama) - [LiteLLM](https://github​.com/BerriAI/litellm) - [Unsloth](https://github​.com/unslothai/unsloth) --- ## Cross-Project Comparison This report summarizes the state of the AI infrastructure ecosystem as of **2026-09-26**. ### 1. Ecosystem Overview The infrastructure landscape is currently defined by an aggressive push toward architectural parity between NVIDIA Hopper/Blackwell and AMD ROCm/MI355X, alongside a structural shift toward "intelligent" serving. Projects are increasingly moving away from monolithic Python implementations in favor of Rust-based memory and cache management. The market is maturing toward stable, multi-tenant production, with a clear focus on fixing long-standing issues in speculative decoding and complex tool-calling workflows. ### 2. Activity Comparison *Note: Estimates based on current active PR/Issue queues as of 2026-09-26.* | Project | Active Issues | Active PRs | Release Status | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **vLLM** | High (~44k) | Very High (~58k) | Stable / Patching | | **SGLang** | Moderate (~41k) | Moderate (~41k) | Architecture Shift | | **llama.cpp** | High (~29k) | High (~29k) | Maintenance | | **Ollama** | High (~18k) | Moderate (~18k) | v0.40.0-rc0 | | **LiteLLM** | Moderate (~43k) | Moderate (~43k) | Security Patches | | **Unsloth** | High (~11k) | High (~11k) | Experimental | ### 3. Model Support Race The industry is currently obsessed with **DeepSeek-V4.1**, with both **vLLM** and **SGLang** locked in a feature-parity race regarding kernel fusions (Hopper/SM100 focus). * **vLLM:** Leads in DeepSeek-V4.1 optimization, specifically regarding O-projection and wkv projection. * **SGLang:** Strongest in MoE kernel tuning and unifying Radix cache performance. * **llama.cpp:** Distinguishing itself by supporting "long-tail" and non-autoregressive architectures like **GraniteSpeech** and **K2 Horizon**. * **Ollama:** Prioritizing native **MLX** support for Apple Silicon to maximize consumer-grade performance. ### 4. Performance Frontier Optimization efforts are fragmented by project goals: * **Kernel/Compute:** vLLM and SGLang are focused on "fusion consolidation" (reducing kernel calls) and specialized namespaces for DeepSeek-V4.1. * **Memory Management:** A massive industry-wide pivot to **Rust-based tree cores** for radix caching is underway to avoid Python's GIL and memory management overhead. * **Parallelism:** The "Unified KV-Cache" is the current stability frontier. Both `llama.cpp` and `vLLM` are struggling with memory corruption and response bleeding in multi-tenant/parallel (`-np > 1`) scenarios. * **Quantization:** Unsloth and llama.cpp are leading efforts in bit-width optimization (MXFP4/k-quants) to enable inference on consumer hardware like RTX 4090/5090. ### 5. Layer Positioning * **Inference Engines (vLLM, SGLang):** High-throughput, multi-tenant serving backends designed for data-center integration. * **Local Runtimes (llama.cpp, Ollama):** Focus on portability (CPU/Vulkan/Metal) and ease of developer onboarding; bridging the gap between local dev and edge deployment. * **Gateway (LiteLLM):** The abstraction layer; currently focusing on vendor-neutral cost mapping and security (encryption-at-rest for provider keys). * **Training/Fine-tuning (Unsloth):** Optimized training primitives designed for efficiency, currently building bridges to adopt vLLM/SGLang as serving backends. ### 6. Trend Signals * **The "Agent-First" Parse:** Projects are shifting focus toward structured output (XGrammar, Inkling, Lark). Developers should anticipate higher strictness in tool-calling; avoid relying on "loose" JSON generation. * **Infrastructure "Rust-ification":** Performance-critical components (caching, frontends) are being rewritten in Rust. If you are building custom infrastructure, keep an eye on project migration roadmaps to avoid technical debt. * **Disaggregated Serving (P/D):** As P/D (Prefill/Decode) architectures become standard, "data integrity" (the synchronization of KV blocks across ranks) is the primary stability risk. Expect continued churn in `Mooncake` and similar KV-connector implementations. * **Recommendation:** If you are running production agents, **pause updates** on core serving engines (vLLM/SGLang) for the next 72 hours until current regressions in logprobs and KV-cache alignment are addressed. --- ## Per-Project Reports
vLLM — vllm-project/vllm # vLLM Technical Digest: 2026-09-26 ### 1. Today's Highlights Development activity is heavily focused on refining **Speculative Decoding (MRV2)** and **DeepSeek-V4.1** inference performance, with a push toward fixing high-concurrency bugs in disaggregated serving environments (P/D). Significant engineering effort is currently being directed at optimizing Triton kernels for new hardware (SM100/GB200) and hardening the recently introduced Rust frontend. ### 2. Releases & Breaking Changes * **No new releases** in the last 24h. * **Note:** The Rust frontend (`VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1`) remains experimental and is not yet feature-equivalent to the Python server; users should track progress via [#44280](https://github​.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/44280). ### 3. New Model & Hardware Support * **DeepSeek-V4.1:** Active performance optimization for SM100/SM103 architectures, including specific kernel fusions for O-projection and wkv projection ([#58634](https://github​.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58634), [#58678](https://github​.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58678)). * **ROCm/MI355X:** Ongoing performance optimization plan for `Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B` on `gfx950` silicon ([#57149](https://github​.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/57149)). ### 4. Performance & Optimization * **Kernel Fusions:** A massive 6x speedup achieved for Mamba block-table alignment by consolidating 7 kernels into one ([#58737](https://github​.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58737)). * **Speculative Decoding:** * Host dispatch latency reduced by ~11us/step via optimized metadata building ([#58732](https://github​.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58732)). * Adaptive verification (DSpark) showing ~179% increase in request throughput (0.83 -> 2.32 req/s) in specific GLM-5.2 benchmarks ([#52992](https://github​.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52992)). * **JIT Warmup:** New PR to cover sparse top-k and DFlash Triton specializations to prevent mid-inference JIT stalls ([#58559](https://github​.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58559)). ### 5. Stability & Regressions * **Speculative Decoding/MRV2 (High Severity):** * [#58485](https://github​.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/58485): Thinking budget corruption causing reasoning failures. * [#58784](https://github​.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58784): MRV2 attempting to verify non-existent draft slots (Fix PR open). * **Tool-Calling (Medium Severity):** * [#55152](https://github​.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/55152): Structural tag rejection in `llguidance` backend breaking `tool_choice` logic. * [#58792](https://github​.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58792): Inkling tool names leaking into streaming output (Fix PR open). * **Scheduling/Streaming (Medium Severity):** * [#57447](https://github​.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57447): Logprobs not correctly preserved across streaming continuations (Fix PR open). ### 6. What This Means for Application Developers * **Disaggregated Serving (P/D):** If you are running complex multi-rank setups, be aware of ongoing fixes for Mooncake/KV-connector block alignment issues ([#55097](https://github​.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55097)). Data integrity here is being actively hardened. * **Tool-Calling/Agents:** If using `tool_choice` or complex streaming formats, be cautious with the latest stable releases as parser logic for reasoning and tool-calling is currently seeing heavy churn (especially regarding `inkling` and `qwen3` parsers). * **Infrastructure:** Ensure your monitoring accounts for the "KV cache reserved pool" vs "Active KV cache" as reported in [#43400](https://github​.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/43400); vLLM’s pre-allocation strategy often results in high memory footprints that are standard, not leaks.
SGLang — sgl-project/sglang # SGLang Digest: 2026-09-26 ### 1. Today's Highlights The focus remains on stabilizing the DeepSeek-V4.1 architecture across diverse backends, with significant engineering effort migrating kernel operations to specialized `dsv4` namespaces to improve modularity and JIT performance. Infrastructure maintenance is elevated, with active CI hardening efforts and a shift toward adopting Rust-based tree cores for unified radix cache management. ### 2. Releases & Breaking Changes * **No official releases** recorded in the last 24h. * **Default Migration:** A major architectural shift is underway to make the **Rust TreeCore** the default for radix caching; PR [#39627](https://github​.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39627) synchronizes Python/Rust behaviors to ensure a seamless transition for existing deployments. ### 3. New Model & Hardware Support * **DeepSeek-V4.1 (AMD/ROCm):** Substantial progress on AMD support, including implementation of FP4 indexer, compressor, and router kernels ([#41019](https://github​.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/41019)). * **Gemma 3/4:** Performance-focused kernel work continues for Gemma3n, specifically optimizing shared-KV attention to minimize memory overhead ([#41295](https://github​.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/41295)). * **XGrammar:** PR [#39380](https://github​.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39380) adds support for Lark grammars, expanding the project's structured output capabilities. ### 4. Performance & Optimization * **DeepSeek-V4.1 Fusions:** New fusion kernels for Hopper architecture, including ratio-2 decode pooling and RMSNorm, aim to streamline the compute boundary ([#41294](https://github​.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/41294)). * **MoE Kernel Tuning:** Optimization for MXFP4 MoE runners on consumer hardware (e.g., RTX 4090) addresses severe throughput deficits by pinning `num_warps` in `triton_kernels` ([#41292](https://github​.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/41292)). * **General Optimization:** Sharing the CuTe DSL AR (All-Reduce) fusion core across DeepSeek and GLM-5.x families to ensure consistent high-performance scaling ([#37196](https://github​.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/37196)). ### 5. Stability & Regressions * **[Critical] HiCache/Hybrid Models:** A bug in `attach_hybrid_pool_to_unified_cache` causes instance-wide crashes on secondary host pools due to unhandled `cudaHostRegister` failures ([#40926](https://github​.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/40926)). * **[High] Logprob Leakage:** A bug in `process_batch_result_prefill` results in prompt logprobs being served to the incorrect request when batch members are retracted or finished ([#36938](https://github​.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/36938)). * **[Medium] Apple Silicon:** OOM issues reported due to incorrect device memory capacity reporting for `mps`, causing `mem_fraction_static` to default to overly aggressive values ([#39675](https://github​.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/39675)). * **[Medium] Memory Amplification:** Multimodal tensor views are triggering significant pickle memory amplification (518x), likely due to improper reference handling ([#33388](https://github​.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/33388)). ### 6. What This Means for Application Developers * **Latency/Throughput:** If you are running DeepSeek-V4.1 or Gemma variants on high-end NVIDIA (Hopper) or consumer hardware, monitor upcoming updates closely, as kernel-level fusions are currently providing substantial efficiency gains. * **Stability:** If you utilize hybrid Mamba/SSM architectures or `HiCache`, be aware of the ongoing `cudaHostRegister` stability issues; it is recommended to verify your environment stability until the fix for [#40926](https://github​.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/40926) is merged. * **Tooling:** If your agent workflow relies on specific grammar formats, the upcoming support for Lark via XGrammar will simplify the integration of complex schema constraints.
llama.cpp — ggml-org/llama.cpp ### Llama.cpp Digest: 2026-09-26 #### 1. Today's Highlights Development continues to focus on hardening multi-tenant inference, particularly resolving KV-cache and compute-buffer stability issues under parallel load. Infrastructure efforts are heavily weighted toward platform-specific optimizations for Intel (SYCL/Vulkan) and Apple Silicon (Metal), while expanding support for emerging model architectures like GraniteSpeech and K2 Horizon. #### 2. Releases & Breaking Changes * **b11192 & b11191**: Maintenance updates including `cpp-httplib` v0.58.0 update [#29407](https://github​.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29407) and path handling normalization for Windows [#29432](https://github​.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29432). #### 3. New Model & Hardware Support * **GraniteSpeech**: Support added for `GraniteSpeech5ForCTC` (non-autoregressive encoder-only) [#29446](https://github​.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29446). * **K2 Horizon**: Active community push to integrate the K2 Horizon model family (0.9B–36B) [#29424](https://github​.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29424). * **Hexagon/Vulkan**: Continued refinement of software-divide inspection tools for Hexagon [#29449](https://github​.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29449) and improved Vulkan prefill performance for Intel architectures [#29357](https://github​.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29357). #### 4. Performance & Optimization * **Metal Optimization**: Sparse Flash Attention (FA) performance improved by migrating indices to shared memory [#29377](https://github​.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29377). * **CPU VNNI**: A new tiled `mul_mat` implementation for k-quants promises 3–7x performance gains on CPU by reducing quant-unpacking overhead [#27851](https://github​.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/27851). * **MoE Offloading**: In-progress GPU-resident LRU cache for MoE expert weights to mitigate host-RAM bandwidth bottlenecks during decoding [#27861](https://github​.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/27861). * **CUDA VRAM**: New chunking strategy for BF16/FP16 to FP32 conversion to reduce peak VRAM usage [#29442](https://github​.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29442). #### 5. Stability & Regressions * **Unified KV-Cache Issues (High)**: Ongoing reports of verbatim response bleeding and prompt processing degradation in parallel/multi-tenant scenarios (`-np > 1`) on HIP/ROCm platforms [#25992](https://github​.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/25992), [#28495](https://github​.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/28495). * **Vulkan Compilation**: Fixed regression in cooperative matrix support for legacy `glslc` versions [#29409](https://github​.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29409). * **Server Endpoints**: Improved error handling for embedding requests to prevent internal 500 errors [#29060](https://github​.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29060). #### 6. What This Means for Application Developers * **Multi-tenant Reliability**: If you are deploying `llama-server` in production with parallel slots (`-np`), be aware of the ongoing instability in the unified KV-cache kernels. Monitor logs for prompt processing degradation or incorrect response concatenation until the recent fixes/adjustments to `kv-unified` are fully validated. * **API Improvements**: Developers building tools on the server API should expect cleaner error states for malformed requests; moving to 400 status codes for client-side errors simplifies integration with standard API gateways. * **Quantization Strategy**: If you are bottlenecked by VRAM on CUDA, experiment with the new conversion chunking flag (`GGML_CUDA_CUBLAS_CONVERT_CHUNK_SIZE`) to trade a minor performance hit for improved model fit.
Ollama — ollama/ollama ### Ollama Infrastructure Digest | 2026-09-26 #### 1. Today's Highlights Ollama is aggressively pivoting toward native MLX performance on Apple Silicon, with v0.40.0-rc0 now defaulting to the MLX runtime for supported architectures. Simultaneously, development is heavily focused on hardening the OpenAI-compatible API and addressing agentic-flow regressions that have disrupted recent production deployments. #### 2. Releases & Breaking Changes * **v0.40.0-rc0**: Introduces [default MLX runtime](https://github​.com/ollama/ollama/pull/18651) execution for Apple Silicon. * **API/Tooling**: A critical regression was identified in OpenAI-compatible response IDs ([#18655](https://github​.com/ollama/ollama/issue/18655)), which used a tiny `rand.Intn(999)` space, causing collisions in downstream proxies (e.g., LiteLLM). A fix using [UUIDs is currently in progress](https://github​.com/ollama/ollama/pull/18656). #### 3. New Model & Hardware Support * **Intel SYCL/oneAPI**: Significant progress on the [Intel GPU backend](https://github​.com/ollama/ollama/pull/17621) via `ggml-sycl`. This aims to support Arc/Battlemage architectures as an opt-in build target. * **Blackwell Support**: Users report [CUDA discovery failures](https://github​.com/ollama/ollama/issue/18581) on NVIDIA RTX 50-series (Blackwell) cards; the engine currently detects 0B VRAM, forcing CPU fallback. * **Architecture Parity**: PR [#18657](https://github​.com/ollama/ollama/pull/18657) is porting custom Metal kernels (mamba2, depthwise_conv) to CUDA, addressing performance parity gaps between Apple Silicon and NVIDIA backends. #### 4. Performance & Optimization * **MLX Memory Management**: Ongoing work to refine the 8 GiB MLX prefix cache budget ([#18131](https://github​.com/ollama/ollama/issue/18131)), which is currently causing heavy swap usage on 32 GB RAM devices during long-context agent workflows. * **Throughput Benchmarking**: PR [#17480](https://github​.com/ollama/ollama/pull/17480) aims to replace synthetic benchmarks with `HumanEval` patches to better simulate code-generation throughput and speculative drafting performance. #### 5. Stability & Regressions * **[High Severity] Silent Stream Drops**: macOS app users report [silent chat failures](https://github​.com/ollama/ollama/issue/18368) after 60 seconds due to prefill latency. A [fix for keeping the stream alive](https://github​.com/ollama/ollama/pull/18654) is pending. * **[Medium Severity] Vision/Image Discard**: `deepseek-v4.1-flash` is [silently discarding image inputs](https://github​.com/ollama/ollama/issue/18637) while reporting vision capabilities. * **[Medium Severity] CUDA Crashes**: Reports of `CUDA illegal memory access` during prompt evaluation on [RTX 5090 hardware](https://github​.com/ollama/ollama/issue/18642) using Cohere MoE architectures. #### 6. What This Means for Application Developers * **Tool-Calling Reliability**: If your agent architecture relies on `tool` roles, be aware of ongoing issues regarding strict parser compliance ([#18509](https://github​.com/ollama/ollama/issue/18509), [#18649](https://github​.com/ollama/ollama/issue/18649)). Ensure your backend can handle subtle trailing tokens or noise that current parsers may reject. * **Constraint Bypassing**: The `/v1/chat/completions` endpoint is reportedly [ignoring `max_tokens`](https://github​.com/ollama/ollama/issue/18575); verify output length limits explicitly in your logic until a patch is merged. * **Monitoring**: If your observability stack uses response IDs for tracing, expect collision issues if you are currently using the OpenAI-compatible endpoint—switch to custom logging until the UUID patch ([#18656](https://github​.com/ollama/ollama/pull/18656)) is deployed.
LiteLLM — BerriAI/litellm ## LiteLLM Digest: 2026-09-26 ### 1. Today's Highlights LiteLLM infrastructure saw a heavy focus on security hardening and cost-map accuracy today, with significant PRs targeting the encryption of sensitive credentials at rest and the consolidation of HTTP client management. The community is actively addressing downstream integration issues, particularly regarding Langfuse SDK v4 migration and improved Gemini/Bedrock streaming reliability. ### 2. Releases & Breaking Changes * **Versions:** Releases `v1.104.0-dev.2`, `v1.100.3`, `v1.99.4`, and `v1.98.1` were published. All artifacts remain signed with the standard `cosign` key ([Commit 0112e53](https://github​.com/BerriAI/litellm/commit/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0)). * **Security Hardening:** [PR #43255](https://github​.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/43255) introduces encryption at rest for guardrail vendor keys, nested `litellm_params` (e.g., bearer tokens), and `router_settings` (Redis passwords), addressing potential plaintext exposure in Postgres. ### 3. New Model & Hardware Support * **Sail Provider:** [PR #42840](https://github​.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/42840) adds full support for `sail/`, mapping `metadata.completion_window` to service tiers. * **OpenRouter Models:** [PR #43248](https://github​.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/43248) adds `openrouter/typesafe/jev-router` to the cost map. * **Decision Models:** [PR #43234](https://github​.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/43234) adds support for Jev and Laya under the Decision Model routing configuration. ### 4. Performance & Optimization * **HTTP Client Consolidation:** [PR #43245](https://github​.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/43245) refactors HTTP infrastructure to use a unified `HttpClientPool`, ensuring that SSL, timeout, and proxy configurations are consistently applied across all providers. * **Rate Limit Enforcement:** [PR #43251](https://github​.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/43251) adds `fail_closed_rate_limit_enforcement` to prevent cross-replica rate-limit exhaustion when Redis becomes unreachable. ### 5. Stability & Regressions * **[Critical] Router Fallback:** [Issue #43165](https://github​.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/43165) reports that non-streaming fallbacks return `null` response bodies upon success, failing to propagate the actual completion. * **[High] Redis/SSL:** [Issue #34614](https://github​.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/34614) confirms a regression in `v1.93.0+` where Redis caching fails due to an unexpected `ssl_check_hostname` keyword argument. * **[High] Helm/Dependencies:** [Issue #26169](https://github​.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/26169) notes that outdated Redis/Postgres dependencies in Helm charts are causing startup regressions. * **[Medium] Cost Map Corrections:** [PR #43253](https://github​.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/43253) and [PR #43254](https://github​.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/43254) correct stale pricing for `fireworks_ai/deepseek-v4p1-flash` and `azure_ai/MAI-Image-2.5-Flash`, respectively. ### 6. Today's Highlights Development activity today is heavily focused on refining the **Unsloth Studio** UI experience and addressing critical inference/training instability on **AMD (ROCm) hardware**. Several high-impact PRs are tackling GPU memory planning, model-specific kernel recompilation delays, and the integration of alternative inference engines like **vLLM and SGLang**. ### 2. items.title: Design: product architecture v0.2 — seven components, security cross-cutting
items.body:
Design discussion home for the product-plane architecture. Trigger: crosses AD-23 context boundaries (per the design-first rule in AGENTS.md). Research: two delegated surveys (2026-10-01) — agent-31 sandbox/persistence (Stripe, Shopify, Spotify, Coinbase, Anthropic first-party) and agent-32 permissions (Microsoft, Lark/DingTalk official, Vercel, AuthZed, AWS, Glean/Graph docs). Full reports are in this issue's comments.

## Component map v0.2 (was five contexts in AD-23)

```
gateway dp/cp      model forwarding (stateless) + control plane (keys, quotas,
                   model governance, middleware-chain plugins like Traefik —
                   the risk interceptor is one); inline usage metering only
ScmProvider        independent: issues / review threads / CI status /
                   merge control / webhooks. CICD and the agent client are
                   consumers; either may be absent in a deployment
sandbox plane      independent: on-demand provisioning via tool call (model-
                   triggered, not provision-then-trigger), warm pool optional,
                   credentials proxy (vault -> per-session proxy; tokens never
                   enter the sandbox or the model context)
agentruntime       harness lives OUTSIDE the sandbox; calls the sandbox plane;
                   carries the invoking user's identity on every tool call
registry/memory    knowledge admission governance + ACL metadata store for
                   synced content; the prompt-analysis consumers write here
cicd orchestration independent of ScmProvider; judge fail cases land here
--------- cross-cutting ---------
session/event log  Postgres append-only (Shopify Aquifer shape) — the deferred
                   event-stream/状态模型; harness-written, never on the model
                   call path; raw interactions emitted async (queue -> object
                   storage) for audit/evals; OTel day one (Coinbase replaced
                   custom logging with a trace store — do not repeat)
policy/audit       PEP before every tool dispatch (fail-closed), PDP out of
                   process when ops capacity allows; one audit event per
                   decision with (acting user, agent identity, tool, args
                   hash, allow/deny) — Agent 365 subject/actor shape
```

## Six-gap disposition (from the original five-function audit)

| gap | disposition |
|---|---|
| 1 ScmProvider | independent component (SCM without CICD is a valid deployment) — maintainer |
| 2 sandbox pool | independent sandbox plane, model-triggered provisioning — research-confirmed (Stripe/Shopify/Spotify/Anthropic converge) |
| 3 interaction persistence | three stores, three consistencies: inline metering at gateway; session event log in Postgres (harness-written); raw bodies async to object storage — hypothesis "downstream of gateway" validated with the metering refinement |
| 4 bundle | packaging dimension, not a runtime context; topology wizard at first boot — confirmed |
| 5 IM entry | CLI first, IM later — confirmed |
| 6 plugin chain | risk interceptor = gateway middleware-chain plugin (Traefik analogy); prompt analysis = offline batch against the interaction store, writes to registry — maintainer |

## Permission model (enterprise gate — maintainer requirement)

- Two token modes only: delegated (user token exchanged downstream, user = subject, agent = actor — Microsoft's OBO flow and Agent 365 taxonomy are the reference) and service (app-only, sync/background, never mixed with user-triggered calls). Lark/DingTalk officially document the same split (user_access_token scope = the user's own permissions; app token = admin-granted data permissions).
- Knowledge connectors sync ACLs as item metadata (Graph externalItem.acl shape); retrieval-time trimming is the enforced boundary; fail closed on unresolvable ACLs; identity-mapping table per source (email -> platform user); ACL propagation lag is a security parameter (event-driven pushes for sensitive sources).
- PEP before every tool dispatch, default-deny, fail-closed; ALLOW / DENY / REQUIRES_APPROVAL as first-class outcomes (Vercel ai-sdk toolApproval, Microsoft Agent Governance Toolkit, SpiceDB CheckPermission).
- Audit from day one: (acting user, agent identity, tool, args hash, decision) per call into the event pipeline; OTel spans per Agent 365 shape.

## Open decisions for the discussion (discuss below, then AD-27 lands them)

1. Confirm the seven-component map (six + sandbox plane) and amend AD-23 via AD-27.
2. Sandbox plane slice 0 scope: provisioning API + local Docker backend first, or K8s from the start? (labels.yml already carries area/sandbox with K8s/gVisor/warm-pool intent)
3. Session/event store: one Postgres with two tables (session events vs interaction bodies) vs event bus first — small team should copy Shopify's single Postgres append-only log.
4. Policy engine choice: start with a local Rego (OPA) evaluation in the runtime, sidecar later — or Cedar/AVP? ( lean OPA: largest ecosystem, ai-sdk precedent)
5. Gateway unfreeze slice 0: go.mod + hexagonal skeleton + Go CI job (methodology configs already in repo) — then dp forwarding as slice 1 per small-step-iteration.
6. Distribution of #54's four patterns into the component issues created from this discussion, then #54 closes.

items.title: [Feature]: Lighter weight Java runtime like OpenJ9
items.body:
### What problem are you looking to solve?

Since a lot of people run this software for their home networks with just a couple of APs, having a docker container with full-blown vesion of Java seems like an overkill. 

### Describe the solution that you have in mind

I propose the switch to a lighter wait version of JRE, one that's built specifically for containers. Now bear in mind I'm not a Java developer, but I've been told that OpenJ9 from IBM Semeru for example is more lightweight and can run the same java apps at 1/3 memory footprint and lower CPU usage.

items.title: [agent] fix Shared-tier provisioning authority and mutation barriers

labels.name: merged-awaiting-acceptance
labels.description: Implementation merged; issue remains open pending explicit acceptance or closure audit

items.body:
## Project / Coordination

- Project board: https://github.com/orgs/elizaOS/projects/12
- Parent tracker or epic: #22934 (satellite contract; not gated on its core GO/NO-GO)
- Coordination Discussion: https://github.com/orgs/elizaOS/discussions/14292
- Suggested lane tag: `codex-shared-provisioning-contract`

## Contribution Provenance

AI assistance is self-reported provenance, not a request for hidden reasoning.
Use the exact runtime values; do not include secrets, tokens, private prompts,
session IDs, or chain-of-thought.

- AI assistance: yes
- AI provider/model: OpenAI / gpt-5.6-sol
- Client / agent tooling: Codex Desktop
- Contribution skill revision: elizaOS/eliza@a83adaa8eba1901b1e9fa99e177b4e0f1d7e8bc7:packages/skills/skills/contribute-to-eliza
- Attribution status: self-reported

## Scope

On `develop@b73d8ea66c546fbc6f6f64ff6ac704b336e691c4`, the onboarding
provisioning reader calls `listByOrganization(organizationId)` and returns
`sandboxes[0]`. That ordering is newest-created, not execution-tier authority,
so a coexisting Shared row and Dedicated target can make the reported
provisioning state depend on insertion order.

The mutation chain also lacks a complete fail-closed Shared-tier boundary.
Legacy producers can create a row with the default `shared` tier and then
enqueue or directly execute container work. Container-bound lifecycle jobs
do not enforce tier authority centrally; service re-entry and provider
placement can mutate billing, credentials, lifecycle state, database, node,
or container state before learning that the row is Shared. Warm-pool
placeholders are a hidden instance of the same defect because they inherit
the Shared default before direct provisioning. Making those placeholders
explicitly container-backed also requires one bounded billing repair: current
selectors would otherwise treat running pool capacity as customer-billable
and could suspend it.

Deliver the smallest bounded contract repair:

- replace every organization-wide `[0]` provisioning selector with one
  deterministic non-Shared, non-pool, non-deleted target selector, including a
  stable tie-break when timestamps match;
- retire the production-dead mutating `ensureElizaAppProvisioning()` and make
  the legacy app provisioning POST observation-only, preserving #19799;
- make every retained route/service/warm-pool create that owns container work
  pass an explicit non-Shared execution tier, while Shared paths create no
  compute job;
- keep rows with `pool_status IS NOT NULL` durably billing-exempt at creation,
  rate classification, billing selection/claim, and active-resource
  cancellation; normal billing resumes only after transfer to a user row whose
  `pool_status` is null;
- reject a Shared warm-claim target while accepting historical source pool
  slots that were legitimately stored as Shared;
- reject Shared rows under the lifecycle row lock before any container-bound
  job reuse/insertion, including transaction-scoped enqueue;
- revalidate authoritative tier in workers so stale or forged Shared jobs stop
  before billing, shutdown, restore, service, or provider calls;
- reject Shared rows in service re-entry, lifecycle CAS, and provider placement
  before any lifecycle status, database, environment, credential, billing,
  node, or container mutation;
- keep payment settlement replay-safe: a Shared top-up settles but schedules no
  compute restart;
- add focused regression tests at the reader, route/service, enqueue, worker,
  warm-pool, lifecycle-CAS, payment, billing, and provider boundaries.

Do not redesign the parked generic connector handoff from #18284, simulate a
composite provider E2E, mutate a deployed environment, alter prices,
implement no-autoscale/QA leases, or change product opt-in policy in this
issue. Billing scope is limited to preserving the warm-pool exemption
described above.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Selector permutations (newer Shared, older Dedicated; inverse order;
      soft-deleted/pool rows; equal timestamps) always return the same intended
      Dedicated target or none.
- [ ] Onboarding is observation-only: the retired mutator/POST cannot create or
      enqueue compute.
- [ ] Retained Dedicated/custom producers and warm-pool placeholders set an
      explicit container-backed tier; Shared paths insert no compute job.
- [ ] Pool rows remain billing-exempt through creation, rate classification,
      selection/claim, and cancellation; a transferred user row with
      `pool_status IS NULL` retains normal billing.
- [ ] Warm-claim refuses a Shared target without breaking historical source
      pool slots.
- [ ] Every container-bound normal and transaction-scoped enqueue path fails
      closed for a Shared row under lock before job insertion.
- [ ] Stale or forged Shared container jobs terminate without retry before
      billing, shutdown, restore, service, or provider calls.
- [ ] Direct service, CAS, and provider invocation on a Shared row leaves
      status, lifecycle revision, database, environment, credentials, billing,
      node, and container state unchanged.
- [ ] Shared top-up settlement remains successful without enqueueing restart.
- [ ] Dedicated/custom provisioning behavior remains covered and unchanged.
- [ ] Focused Bun 1.3.14 tests and the affected package typecheck pass, or any
      unrelated `develop` baseline failures are named exactly with logs.

## Evidence Plan

- [ ] Screenshots or recording: N/A - backend execution-tier contract; no
      rendered UI changes.
- [ ] Logs: focused Bun 1.3.14 test output for each boundary and affected
      package typecheck output.
- [ ] Real-LLM trajectories: N/A - no model/action-selection behavior changes.
- [ ] Domain artifacts: deterministic mixed-tier repository fixtures and proof
      that Shared rows produce zero provision job/provider mutation.
- [ ] CI or local commands: repository attribution validator, focused tests,
      package typecheck, and CI dispatch only after a reviewable branch exists.

## Claim / Status Notes

Before working, comment `CLAIMING: repair the Shared-tier provisioning reader
and fail-closed route/service/enqueue/worker/provider boundaries` with the
signed lane tag, add this issue to Launch QA Project #12, set
`Status = Claimed`, and set `Claimed by = codex-shared-provisioning-contract`.
Move it to `In progress` when implementation starts.

— [codex-shared-provisioning-contract]

items.title: [Roadmap] DataRelay Atlas — Core / Automation / Experimental
items.body:
<!-- CANONICAL_USER_GATE_DOCUMENT_FIRST_20261003 -->
## Canonical user-gate document-first execution rule — 2026-10-03

When the owner asks to run the project's CLI/Feature/Scenario test, Surface Reconciliation, FULL_USER_E2E, or an equivalent named user gate, the request means **execute the repository's canonical contract exactly as written**, not improvise a substitute test.

Mandatory order:

1. Resolve the target repository and active worktree.
2. Resolve the exact canonical contract path for the requested gate.
3. **Read the entire current contract before starting the gate.** Do not begin by inventing a checklist, running a convenient wrapper, replaying a script, searching unrelated repos, or substituting a generic test suite.
4. Understand and preserve the contract's semantics: persona roles, black-box/public-surface boundary, scenario inventory, prohibited actions, evidence/ledger rules, finding-accumulation rule, cleanup, restart/invalidation rules, and PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED criteria.
5. Then execute every applicable contract requirement directly. For user-role lanes, **ChatGPT itself acts as the user/operator/admin and follows the public surface**. Wrappers, shell/Python scripts, CI, unit/integration suites, browser automation, parsers, and scanners are supporting evidence/orchestration only; they cannot impersonate the user lane or turn their PASS into a user-gate PASS.
6. If a scripted/harness shortcut conflicts with the canonical contract, the contract wins and the shortcut must not be used as a substitute.
7. If the gate produces bugs/findings, finish the complete safe discovery pass, freeze the finding set, batch-fix, then restart the complete gate from the beginning on the new exact candidate. Repeat until clean with no fixed pass limit.
8. Apply the same document-first rule independently to FULL_USER_E2E after Surface/CLI reconciliation converges.

A run is invalid for roadmap/release closure if ChatGPT did not first execute from the current canonical contract or if primary user evidence was replaced by a wrapper/scripted replay.

---

<!-- RELEASE_QUALITY_CLOSED_LOOP_20261003 -->
## Release-quality closed loop — 2026-10-03

This roadmap uses **defect-convergence, not a fixed number of test passes**, as the terminal release rule.

1. Finish the roadmap/function scope far enough to enter release closure.
2. Run the complete **Surface Reconciliation** gate. For CLI products this is the exhaustive **CLI ↔ Feature ↔ Scenario** audit; for browser/other products use the equivalent complete public-surface/capability scenario audit. **ChatGPT directly acts as the applicable real User/Operator/Admin persona.**
3. Finish the complete discovery pass before remediation, retain all findings, then batch-fix every actionable in-scope product/UX/contract defect. A severity downgrade alone is not closure.
4. If the product/public surface/contract changed, start the complete Surface Reconciliation gate again from the beginning on the new exact candidate. **Repeat with no fixed pass limit until the complete run finds zero new or unresolved actionable defects and has zero mandatory FAIL/PARTIAL/BLOCKED results.**
5. Only then run the complete **Full User E2E** gate with real user journeys, state changes, read-back/effective runtime truth, failures/recovery, and cleanup. Finish the whole run, batch-fix every actionable defect, then rerun the complete gate from the beginning. **Repeat with no fixed pass limit until clean.**
6. If Full User E2E remediation changes the public surface or its contract, return to Surface Reconciliation and reconverge before closure.
7. Only when the latest complete Surface Reconciliation and Full User E2E are both clean on the **same exact HEAD** may the roadmap declare `PRODUCT_QUALITY_CLOSURE=PASS`.
8. Then and only then: **candidate freeze → release-specific upgrade/migration/platform/performance qualification → final exact-HEAD CI/regression → artifact/hash/SBOM/provenance/manifest/attestation → owner acceptance/release authorization → immutable release/publication → post-release smoke**.

Final CI, SBOM/provenance, candidate freeze, tag/publication, or other downstream release work must not displace either defect-convergence loop while it can still change the candidate. Scripts/CI/harnesses are supporting evidence and never substitute for ChatGPT's direct user-role execution.

---

## 2026-10-03 — Verified Continuous Engineering Memory implementation status

M1-M5 implementation is COMPLETE on main at `c956e267f20aef19913f9aeacce8f395eb146380`.

- M1 #269 / PR #270 — bounded task-context bootstrap, current-state revalidation, JIT retrieval.
- M2 #271 / PR #272 — continuous canonical reconciliation entry point and scoped non-authoritative candidate memory.
- M3 #273 / PR #274 — consolidation, supersession, type-specific TTL and CURRENT/STALE/SUPERSEDED/UNKNOWN validity.
- M4 #275 / PR #276 — candidate-only inspect/correct/forget/pin controls; no canonical mutation.
- M5 #277 / PR #278 — measurement-only effectiveness ledger/report for recall, stale/irrelevant/duplicate injection, repeated owner explanation, context bytes and first-pass success.
- Latest local exact-head full suite before M5 merge: 1125/1125 PASS; required PR CI GREEN.
- Adaptive retrieval/ranking remains measurement-gated: M5 reports NO_DATA/INSUFFICIENT until real workload observations are sufficient and never mutates policy automatically.
- Production rollout remains separately governed by #268 and its trusted production-write boundary.

---

## 2026-10-03 — Verified Continuous Engineering Memory roadmap (canonical)

This section supersedes older post-v0.1.0 memory/context candidates where they conflict.

### Product goal

Atlas should reduce repeated owner explanation and repeated context reconstruction across ChatGPT/Codex/other approved AI clients without becoming a generic chat archive or duplicating Engineering System authority.

Canonical engineering truth remains GitHub/OpenSpec/code/tests/ADR/CI and Engineering System. Atlas memory is provider-neutral derived context and may never outrank current canonical state.

### Confirmed capability roadmap

1. **Automatic Task Context Bootstrap**
   - an approved AI client can ask Atlas for one bounded current task context by repository/workstream;
   - return only current high-signal state plus references for deeper retrieval;
   - no requirement for the owner to say “look in Atlas.”

2. **Continuous Canonical/Event Ingestion**
   - GitHub, Engineering System, CI/test/release/runtime evidence is reconciled automatically where an approved source/event path exists;
   - user “save this” instructions are not required for canonical machine evidence.

3. **Scoped Automatic Memory Candidate Extraction**
   - extract only bounded non-authoritative durable candidates from approved interaction/run summaries;
   - initial candidate classes: OWNER_PREFERENCE, VALIDATED_FINDING, LESSON_LEARNED, RUN_SUMMARY, FUTURE_IDEA, REFERENCE_FACT;
   - never promote extracted conversation content directly to canonical engineering truth.

4. **Provenance/Citation-bound Memory**
   - memories backed by repository/ADR/spec/evidence retain source identity/revision/digest where available;
   - raw secret-bearing/source bodies are not copied into durable memory merely to support citation.

5. **Recall-time Current-state Revalidation**
   - citation-backed memory is revalidated against current canonical state before being presented as CURRENT;
   - stale, contradicted, unavailable or superseded memory is explicit and cannot silently override current state.

6. **Dedup + Consolidation + Supersession + TTL**
   - equivalent memories converge instead of growing unbounded;
   - newer facts may supersede older facts while history remains attributable;
   - TTL/decay is type-specific rather than one global lifetime.

7. **Progressive / JIT Context Retrieval**
   - first response is a small bounded context summary/index;
   - deeper evidence/memory is fetched only when the task needs it;
   - do not inject the whole memory store into every model prompt.

8. **User Review / Correct / Forget / Pin**
   - the owner can inspect and correct derived/personal memory, forget it, or pin intentionally durable items;
   - these controls do not mutate canonical GitHub/Engineering System truth indirectly.

9. **Memory & Context Effectiveness Evals**
   - measure important-memory recall, stale/irrelevant injection, duplicate rate, repeated-owner-explanation count, injected context size/cost and downstream first-pass task success;
   - promote retrieval heuristics only from measured evidence.

### Explicit non-goals

- no full raw ChatGPT transcript archive as the primary memory plane;
- no automatic learning of engineering procedures/rules that duplicates Engineering System/AGENTS/runbooks/skills;
- no external Mem0/Zep/Letta SaaS runtime dependency;
- no mandatory new graph database or vector database while existing Atlas retrieval is sufficient;
- no AI-extracted memory automatically promoted to architecture/security/release authority;
- no whole-memory prompt injection;
- no provider-specific memory silo as source of truth.

### Implementation order

**M1 — Context Bootstrap + Revalidation + JIT retrieval**
- first implementation priority;
- reuse existing registry/retrieval/lifecycle/Engineering System evidence surfaces;
- add a bounded provider-neutral task-context contract and read-only CLI/MCP/UI parity where useful.

**M2 — Continuous ingestion + candidate memory store**
- event/source reconciliation plus bounded candidate model, authority/scope separation and secret-safe persistence.

**M3 — Consolidation / temporal validity / TTL**
