## Autonomous Engineering Control Plane north star — 2026-09-25

Atlas should evolve beyond prompt-driven orchestration into an **Autonomous Engineering Control Plane**. The long-term operating model is:

```text
Human intent / product decision
        ↓
Executable GitHub Work Packet
        ↓
Atlas planner / policy
        ↓
bounded execution graph
   ├─ Cursor implementation worker
   ├─ deterministic test / CI worker
   ├─ independent AI audit provider
   ├─ browser / integration verifier when required
   └─ GitHub state writer
        ↓
Trust Plane
        ↓
PASS / REWORK / HUMAN_REQUIRED
        ↓
next ready Work Packet or owner escalation
```

The architectural destination is:

> **Atlas is the orchestrator; ChatGPT, Cursor, Codex/GPT audit providers, browser automation, and CI are bounded workers/providers. GitHub remains canonical engineering state.**

ChatGPT may remain an independent supervisory/audit surface, but routine orchestration must not depend on a human repeatedly writing prompts or manually sending `계속`.

### Capability sequence

Implement this in the following order. Do not skip directly to a large agent fleet.

1. **Executable Work Packet**
   - treat the canonical Work Packet as a machine-executable specification, not only a handoff note;
   - include bounded acceptance criteria, allowed effects, required deterministic tests/evidence, retry policy, budget/policy limits, and HUMAN_REQUIRED conditions;
   - GitHub remains canonical; transient model conversations remain non-canonical.

2. **Autonomous Planner**
   - derive a bounded execution plan/graph from the Work Packet plus Engineering System policy;
   - prefer deterministic templates and typed transitions over unrestricted free-form planning;
   - verify repository, branch, exact HEAD, clean/expected worktree, and canonical packet before dispatch.

3. **Worker Runtime**
   - treat Cursor and future providers as workers, not conversational authorities;
   - reuse bounded project-local worker/session state where safe instead of creating a new conversation for every packet;
   - preserve host/worktree isolation and never allow one project's worker to mutate another project's worktree.

4. **Trust Plane**
   - separate machine-verifiable completion from model judgment;
   - deterministic gates include exact HEAD, worktree state, tests, CI, provenance, policy, required artifacts, and stale/duplicate suppression;
   - semantic audit runs only after deterministic preconditions are satisfied;
   - a worker claiming PASS is never sufficient by itself.

5. **Automatic REWORK loop**
   - deterministic or audit failures become one bounded consolidated finding set;
   - safely redispatch the same workstream without human prompt rewriting;
   - retry only within explicit bounded policy;
   - repeated failure, ambiguity, security-sensitive decisions, credentials, destructive effects, or owner approvals escalate to `HUMAN_REQUIRED`.

6. **Dependency Graph**
   - replace simple linear queue chaining with explicit dependency/readiness relationships;
   - serialize conflicting worktree/resource mutations;
   - allow independent work to run concurrently only when dependencies, isolation, and budget permit.

7. **Multi-agent concurrency**
   - increase worker count only after a single Work Packet can reliably complete the full closed loop;
   - concurrency is a throughput optimization, not the foundation of correctness;
   - enforce global/project concurrency, budget, rate, and blast-radius limits.

### First mandatory milestone

Before scaling concurrency, Atlas must prove one real Work Packet can progress without further human prompting through:

```text
READY
  ↓
RUNNING
  ↓
VERIFYING
  ├─ PASS → COMPLETED / next ready packet
  ├─ REWORK → bounded redispatch → RUNNING
  └─ HUMAN_REQUIRED → owner
```

Exit criterion:

> One bounded Work Packet can go from READY to COMPLETED, including at least one possible REWORK cycle, using canonical GitHub state, deterministic gates, bounded independent audit, and safe worker redispatch without Rick or ChatGPT manually rewriting the next prompt.

### Relationship to current Atlas work

- **Issue #47** is the immediate bridge toward this architecture: host-local worker execution, durable project descriptors, exact-HEAD audit checkpoints, bounded audit providers, automatic REWORK redispatch, and GitHub-backed state.
- **Queued Work Packet chaining** remains the near-term linear predecessor to a true dependency graph.
- **Engineering System** remains the canonical methodology/policy source. Atlas consumes and executes those contracts; it must not fork a separate methodology.
- Existing functional-core and production-dogfood work remains valid. This control-plane direction should reduce manual orchestration across those phases rather than create a disconnected side project.

### Non-goals / safety constraints

- Do not make model conversation history canonical.
- Do not treat model self-reported PASS as completion evidence.
- Do not auto-cross owner approval, credential, destructive, release, deploy, or other HUMAN_REQUIRED gates.
- Do not create a general-purpose workflow engine unrelated to engineering control.
- Do not increase agent count before deterministic trust/idempotency/recovery behavior is proven.
- Do not duplicate Engineering System primitives when an adopted canonical primitive already exists.

### User-facing target

Routine operation should converge toward:

```text
Rick: "DRAtlas, Issue #72 진행해"

Atlas:
resolve packet → validate state → plan → execute → verify
→ rework automatically if bounded and safe
→ audit → update GitHub → continue to next ready packet

Owner notification:
✅ COMPLETED
⚠️ HUMAN_REQUIRED
❌ BLOCKED
```

The key optimization is therefore not "better prompts". It is moving repeatable intent, context, policy, verification, retry, dependency, and evidence into durable system contracts so prompts become a thin control surface rather than the workflow itself.


## Model-Aware Instruction Governance — 2026-09-25

Atlas should operationalize the Engineering System Model-Aware Prompt / Instruction Hygiene contract. Atlas does **not** define prompting methodology; it discovers managed instruction surfaces, invokes the canonical audit/eval contracts, preserves evidence, and coordinates safe adoption.

### Target lifecycle

```text
model / harness / instruction change
        ↓
Atlas resolves affected repositories + instruction surfaces
        ↓
Engineering System prompt-surface inventory
        ↓
read-only instruction audit
        ↓
bounded proposed diff
        ↓
behavior eval / deterministic policy checks
        ↓
   ┌───────────────┬────────────────┐
   │               │                │
NO_CHANGE      CANDIDATE_PASS   HUMAN_REQUIRED
   │               │                │
checkpoint      canary / PR       owner decision
                   ↓
             measured comparison
                   ↓
             managed adoption
```

### Atlas capability sequence

#### AIG-0 — Consume, do not fork, the Engineering System contract

Atlas must consume the canonical Engineering System definitions for:
- prompt/instruction surface inventory;
- finding classifications;
- behavior-eval requirements;
- provider/model profile identity;
- rollout/canary evidence.

No Atlas-specific duplicate methodology or competing prompt policy.

#### AIG-1 — Repository instruction inventory

For registered projects, Atlas should be able to identify behavior-bearing surfaces such as:
- `AGENTS.md`;
- managed Cursor/provider rules;
- skills/hooks;
- Work Packet templates;
- tool/MCP descriptions;
- repository-owned prompt/request templates;
- approved model/reasoning/tool profiles.

Store provenance and hashes/revisions, not secret-bearing raw prompt history when unnecessary.

#### AIG-2 — Trigger and scope resolution

Instruction audit should be eligible when one of these bounded triggers occurs:
- approved model/provider/harness version changes;
- Engineering System managed instruction baseline changes;
- a behavior-bearing instruction surface changes;
- repeated eval/telemetry evidence suggests instruction-induced waste or regression;
- owner explicitly requests an audit.

A trigger must resolve to a bounded repository/workstream/model profile. Do not launch organization-wide scans by default.

#### AIG-3 — Read-only audit worker

Use a dedicated bounded audit provider/worker to:
- classify load-bearing vs candidate cruft;
- identify duplicate/contradictory/model-obsolete instructions;
- return normalized findings and proposed diffs;
- cite current model/provider guidance when the audit depends on it;
- never directly modify repository policy in the initial phase.

The audit worker is advisory evidence, not authority.

#### AIG-4 — Eval + Trust Plane integration

Before a proposed instruction change can advance:
- run the Engineering System behavior-eval set appropriate to the repository/task;
- run deterministic security/policy checks;
- compare exact outcome, retries, tokens/cost, latency, and human intervention;
- bind evidence to exact repository revision + instruction candidate + model/harness profile;

For a candidate that passes offline eval:
1. apply only through the normal branch/PR/Work Packet path;
2. canary on one selected repository/profile;
3. observe measured task outcomes;
4. compare with the previous baseline;
5. either promote through Engineering System managed rollout or REWORK/rollback.

No direct default-branch rewrite. No bulk repository mutation.

After the single-packet autonomous control loop is proven, instruction hygiene can become a low-frequency maintenance node in the Atlas dependency graph:

```text
affected-surface discovery
        ↓
audit
        ↓
eval
        ↓
candidate PR / no-op / HUMAN_REQUIRED
```

This should be cheap when nothing changed and must not consume expensive model calls repeatedly for the same exact revision/profile.

Priority order remains:

## Provider Capacity Broker / Quota-aware Scheduling — 2026-09-25

Atlas should eventually orchestrate not only **which worker performs a task**, but also **which approved provider/model/runtime capacity should execute it**. The reference idea is quota/reset-aware routing such as openllms, but Atlas must implement a stricter **policy-aware Capacity Broker** rather than a subscription-limit maximizer.

### Target architecture

```text
Work Packet / execution node
        ↓
Engineering System eligibility policy
        ↓
Atlas Provider Capacity Broker
        ↓
approved candidate routes
   ├─ Cursor/native runtime
   ├─ Claude native/approved SDK/API
   ├─ OpenAI API / approved native runtime
   ├─ Codex/reviewer provider
   └─ future local/enterprise providers
        ↓
route scoring
(capability + policy + trust + cost + quota/reset + latency)
        ↓
selected worker/provider
        ↓
normalized evidence
        ↓
Trust Plane
```

### Broker responsibilities

For each eligible provider/model/runtime route, Atlas may track:
- provider + model/profile;
- usage mode;
- policy eligibility;
- health / cooldown / throttling;
- remaining quota or credit where observable;
- reset horizon where observable;
- estimated marginal cost;
- latency / queue depth;
- task capability compatibility;
- current Work Packet budget;
- host/session/worktree availability;
- recent failure state;
- whether model/provider transition would invalidate cached context or require re-validation.

### Routing strategies

Atlas should support policy-bounded strategies such as:

- **CAPABILITY_FIRST**
- **COST_FIRST**
- **RESET_SOON**
- **BALANCED**
- **FAILOVER**
- **STEWARDSHIP**

`STEWARDSHIP` should become the preferred long-term policy: choose the best approved route using capability, current cost, expiring capacity/reset horizon, latency, trust requirements, and project budget.

### Policy gate before scoring

Candidate generation must occur in this order:

```text
all configured routes
    ↓
provider-policy eligibility
    ↓
task capability compatibility
    ↓
trust / verification compatibility
    ↓
budget / blast-radius / WIP admission
    ↓
capacity scoring
```

A route with attractive quota but `UNKNOWN` or `DENIED` policy status is not eligible.

### Failover semantics

Failover must be explicit and attributable.

Example:

```text
Cursor / model A
   ↓ rate/quota failure
compatible route check
   ↓
Claude / model B
   ↓
new provider identity recorded
   ↓
fresh deterministic evidence
   ↓
independent audit as required
```

Rules:
- no silent provider/model switching;
- no reuse of stale semantic audit across materially different provider/model paths;
- no provider switch that bypasses tool, permission, or worktree constraints;
- repeated failover exhaustion becomes `BLOCK` or `HUMAN_REQUIRED`.

### Evidence contract

Every execution node should be able to retain bounded metadata such as:

```text
IMPLEMENTER_PROVIDER=
IMPLEMENTER_MODEL=
IMPLEMENTER_PROFILE=
USAGE_MODE=
ROUTING_STRATEGY=
ROUTE_REASON=
CAPACITY_SNAPSHOT_REF=
WORK_PACKET_BUDGET=
SUBJECT_HEAD=
```

Independent audit records its own provider/model identity separately.

Canonical GitHub state should contain only bounded attribution/evidence references, not raw OAuth/session tokens or provider secrets.

### Reference implementation intake

Treat projects such as `openllms` as reference implementations for:
- reset-aware scheduling;
- quota discovery;
- cooldown/health handling;
- failover;
- weighted route scoring;
- unified provider abstraction.

Do not adopt any consumer-subscription credential/session mechanism merely because a reference implementation supports it. Only approved provider-native/API/enterprise usage modes are eligible for Atlas production routing.

### Relationship to existing Atlas roadmap

This capability depends on earlier foundations:

1. **#47 bridge**
2. **single Work Packet autonomous closure**
3. **dependency/readiness graph**
4. **provider capability adapters**
5. **Provider Capacity Broker**
6. **Model-Aware Instruction/Harness maintenance**
7. **measured multi-agent concurrency**

The broker may later improve concurrency scheduling, but it must not be used to justify broad multi-agent scale-out before the Trust Plane and dependency graph are reliable.

### Initial implementation slice

When activated, start small:

1. synthetic provider descriptors only;
2. deterministic policy eligibility evaluator;
3. deterministic route scoring tests;
4. one approved real route plus one approved fallback route;
5. record selection evidence and failover behavior;
6. no consumer-subscription pooling in the first production slice.

### Example operator outcome

```text
Task: independent final audit
Eligible routes:
- GPT-5.6 Sol API: ALLOWED, high capability, paid
- Codex fallback: ALLOWED, lower marginal cost, available
- Claude subscription generic API bridge: UNKNOWN → excluded

Policy: STEWARDSHIP
Selected: GPT-5.6 Sol API
Reason: required audit capability + current budget available
```

or:

```text
Task: bounded implementation
Primary route unavailable due to quota reset window.
Compatible approved fallback selected.
Provider transition recorded.
No trust or policy gate weakened.
```

### Exit criterion

Atlas can choose among multiple approved AI execution routes based on capability, policy, trust, budget, quota/reset horizon, and health; fail over safely; and produce enough exact attribution to reproduce and audit why that route was used.

```text

                    │
        ┌───────────┴───────────┐
        │                       │
  Frontier Reasoning       Decision Plane
  GPT / Opus / Cursor      Jev / equivalent
        │                       │
architecture / code        bounded selection

        └───────────┬───────────┘
                    │

                    │

```

### Decision Plane boundary

Atlas prepares and validates the candidate options. The decision model only chooses among them.

Examples:

```text
optional context:
[SECURITY.md, OAuth ADR, RELEASE.md, backup runbook]
              ↓
             Jev
              ↓
[SECURITY.md, OAuth ADR]
              ↓
mandatory-context/policy validation
```

```text
eligible workers:
[fast-worker, standard-worker, frontier-reasoner]
              ↓
             Jev
              ↓
standard-worker
              ↓
capacity/policy/trust validation
```

```text
classified failure:
[RETRY, REFRESH_STATE, FOCUSED_DIAGNOSTIC, SWITCH_PROVIDER, HUMAN_REQUIRED]
              ↓
             Jev
              ↓
FOCUSED_DIAGNOSTIC
              ↓
deterministic safety validation
```

### First PoC scope

Start with the two lowest-risk, easiest-to-measure classes:

1. **Optional context selection**
   - mandatory `AGENTS.md` / policy context remains deterministic;
   - Jev selects only optional notes/spec/ADR/runbook candidates;
   - measure context tokens, wrong-context rate, frontier-model task success, and rereads.

2. **Focused-check selection**
   - harness generates affected cheap checks from `.engineering/tests.yaml` and changed scope;
   - Jev ranks/selects which focused checks run first;
   - required terminal CI/exact-head gates remain deterministic and cannot be skipped;
   - measure time-to-first-signal, total test cost, missed regressions, and rework.

### Follow-on decision classes

Only after the first PoC passes:
- worker/model routing among Engineering-System-approved candidates;
- recovery-path selection after tool/test failures;
- dependency-graph ready-node ranking;
- diagnostic-next-step selection;
- deciding whether a task requires frontier reasoning.

### Shadow-mode rollout

Initial implementation must not affect real execution.

For each eligible decision, record:

```text
CURRENT_DECISION=
DECISION_MODEL_CHOICE=
CONFIDENCE=
CANDIDATE_SET=
VALIDATION_RESULT=
ACTUAL_OUTCOME=
COST_DELTA=
WALL_TIME_DELTA=
```

Do not persist sensitive raw prompt/context contents when a bounded reference/hash is sufficient.

### Replay evaluation

Before activation:
- replay historical Atlas/Engineering System decisions where the eventual outcome is known;
- compare Jev choice to the current deterministic/frontier decision;
- calculate task-success impact, frontier-call reduction, cost, wall time, retries, and false-routing rate;
- define explicit go/no-go thresholds for each decision class.

### Activation policy

```text
SHADOW
  ↓
REPLAY_PASS
  ↓
CANARY
  ↓
LIMITED_ACTIVE
  ↓
MEASURED_EXPANSION
```

Any material quality regression, confidence instability, stale-state error, or policy mismatch returns the class to shadow/default routing.

### Relationship to Provider Capacity Broker

The Capacity Broker should produce the **eligible candidate set**. The Decision Plane may rank/select among those candidates.

```text
configured providers
   ↓
policy/capability/trust/budget eligibility
   ↓
approved candidate routes
   ↓
Decision Plane ranking
   ↓
deterministic post-validation
   ↓
selected route
```

Jev must never make an otherwise ineligible provider eligible.

### Relationship to Autonomous Engineering Control Plane

Roadmap order:

1. #47 bridge;
2. single Work Packet autonomous closure;
3. dependency/readiness graph;
4. provider capability adapters;
5. Capacity Broker eligibility layer;
6. **Decision Plane shadow/replay PoC**;
7. low-risk decision-class activation;
8. measured multi-agent concurrency.

A limited shadow PoC may be prepared earlier if it does not interrupt the active critical path, but production routing remains gated on the closed-loop/Trust Plane foundations.

### Success criteria

For at least one decision class, demonstrate:
- equal-or-better verified downstream task success;
- measurable reduction in frontier-model calls or context/test cost;
- lower or equal wall time;
- no deterministic/security/trust gate weakening;
- bounded fallback when confidence/validation fails;
- exact attribution of decision-model provider/version/profile;
- clean rollback to the existing deterministic/frontier path.

### Non-goals

- no replacing Opus/GPT-5.6/Cursor for architecture, code generation, novel debugging, or semantic final audit;
- no allowing Jev to decide permissions, release/deploy, secrets, exact-head PASS, or HUMAN_REQUIRED gates;
- no broad production rollout based solely on vendor benchmark claims;
- no making Jev a mandatory Atlas dependency.

### Exit criterion

Atlas can use a cheap bounded decision model for one low-risk decision class, prove in shadow/replay/canary evidence that it reduces cost/time without degrading verified outcomes, and fall back deterministically when the decision is invalid or uncertain.

items.body:
# 梳理 0.0.1.legacy 已支持能力与实现问题，形成重构范围基线

## 身份与责任

- 交付层级：delivery
- 主工作类型：investigation
- 交付修订：1
- 创建操作标识：legacy-capability-baseline-12580c03-beee-4485-ae99-b39ad0d2e4a4
- 责任范围：`apps.0.0.1.legacy/` 与 `packages.0.0.1.legacy/` 的已支持能力、真实消费者、明显性能及代码质量问题；面向后续重构调度。
- 卡负责人、主结果接受者及授权依据：PanQiWei。用户在调度中心会话明确要求创建第三张调查卡，交独立会话梳理 legacy 能力，报告直接写入本卡评论，不要求 PR。
- 受影响语义拥有者：本卡不修改产品、架构、公共契约或工程政策。调查中的冲突和范围取舍交 PanQiWei 及对应承诺拥有者判断。
- 长期依据：以提交 `02c0fc82dfc254fe598922daabf319b18e39b600` 的两个 legacy 目录为调查快照。项目约束见同提交的[项目要求](https://github.com/nemori-ai/omne-harness-lite/blob/02c0fc82dfc254fe598922daabf319b18e39b600/docs/requirements.md)、[包组织](https://github.com/nemori-ai/omne-harness-lite/blob/02c0fc82dfc254fe598922daabf319b18e39b600/docs/package-organization.md)、[交付工作类型](https://github.com/nemori-ai/omne-harness-lite/blob/02c0fc82dfc254fe598922daabf319b18e39b600/docs/engineering/work-types.md)。本次评论交付方式以用户明确要求为准。

## 问题、结果与范围

本阶段先完成 0.0.1.legacy 到新架构和包结构的重构。0.1.0 的目标能力更广，不能全部算入本阶段。调查回答三个问题：legacy 实际支持什么；重构怎样核对这些功能没有丢失；哪些明显的性能和代码质量问题需要避免重现。

成果为本卡评论中的能力基线报告。以用户或调用方能完成的功能点组织，不以目录、包、类或函数数量代替能力。覆盖应用入口，也覆盖有公开入口、可独立使用的包能力，并区分已经接入应用与仅可独立调用的能力。

不实施重构、不修复缺陷、不决定新技术栈、不扩充 0.1.0 功能、不起草新架构。本卡不要求交付 PR，也不要求新增仓库报告文件。保留功能结果不等于保留旧 API、目录、存储格式或兼容层。旧实现的不安全行为、缺陷或限制不得自动升级为新系统承诺。

## 依据与验收

| 当前依据或获准问题 | 唯一源定位与条款／场景 | 所核修订及Git提交 | 本次成功判据、方法和禁止结果 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 实际支持哪些功能 | [legacy 应用](https://github.com/nemori-ai/omne-harness-lite/tree/02c0fc82dfc254fe598922daabf319b18e39b600/apps.0.0.1.legacy)、[legacy 包](https://github.com/nemori-ai/omne-harness-lite/tree/02c0fc82dfc254fe598922daabf319b18e39b600/packages.0.0.1.legacy)及真实调用链 | 上述固定提交；执行环境和依赖版本另记 | 覆盖两个目录的对外能力与消费者。README、SPEC、源码、测试和实际运行相互核对。不得仅凭文档宣称已支持。 |
| 重构如何不丢功能且不扩大范围 | 用户本次授权；现行项目要求与包组织仅提供约束和规划参照 | 卡 revision 1；上述固定提交 | 每个确认支持的能力有可观察的保留判据和回归场景。明确与未实现的 0.1.0 目标分界。目标包归属最多是规划建议，不是采用决定。 |
| 哪些实现问题应避免重现 | 固定快照的实现、调用路径及相称验证；[#193](https://github.com/nemori-ai/omne-harness-lite/issues/193)仅作待核线索 | 每项链接到固定提交的具体源码或测试位置 | 分开记录已证实问题与静态疑点，说明影响和依据。不得用主观评价代替反例，不得编造性能数据。 |
| 报告可跨会话使用 | 本卡报告评论及其索引 | 每个报告版本注明源提交、报告日期与评论链接 | 下一调度会话可直接据此拆分重构任务、定位功能验收与风险。报告在评论中完整可读，不依赖执行者本机 tmp。 |

## 工作类型附加内容

### 调查方法与边界

1. 从两个 legacy 根入口、实际应用命令和公开包入口建立覆盖清单，再追踪实现与真实消费者。README 的遗漏或旧路径不能直接判为能力缺失。相关测试、配置、锁文件和资源按需纳入，不顺带调查整个新系统。
2. 核对文档承诺、源码路径、测试覆盖与实际可用条件。对代表性路径做低成本、可复现的验证。明确区分本次实跑、现有测试、历史记录及静态推断。
3. 已支持能力给出前提和限制。未运行、需要外部凭据或环境不足的能力保留“待核实”，注明证据与缺口。不能把未验证等同于不支持，也不能把存在函数等同于已支持。
4. 性能调查优先确认同步阻塞、重复初始化或读取、无界并发、资源生命周期、缓存或池化使用等真实路径。代码质量调查关注会增加重构风险的职责耦合、重复逻辑、失效抽象、错误吞没及测试缺口。这些是排查方向，不是预先认定的缺陷。
5. 仅在必要且环境允许时做局部测量。记录命令、负载、环境、重复方式、结果范围和正确性，遵循 `pstack:benchmark-checklist`。不能仅凭代码行数、依赖名称或一次耗时认定性能结论。
6. 按 `pstack:poteto-mode` 的 Investigation 流程及适用的 `pstack:how` 开展。按项目文档写作规则表达结论。调查到的修复建议留在本卡，不在本任务实施。

### 报告最小内容

- **摘要与覆盖范围**：固定源提交、日期、调查入口、覆盖方法、未覆盖内容和阻塞。解释能力粒度，避免同一功能按多层实现重复计数。
- **能力清单**：每项有稳定编号、用户或调用方能完成的动作、入口和消费者、必要前提、可观察结果、支持状态、证据链接、限制及重构回归场景。状态区分“已支持”“部分支持”“待核实”“仅有设计或已移除”。独立可调用但未接入应用的能力单独标明。
- **非回归基线**：汇总确认支持及部分支持能力的验收场景，按适用情况包含正常、失败、取消、持久化、重启恢复、权限或租户边界。场景绑定能力编号；未实现的目标不能列为既有能力。
- **问题与教训**：性能与代码质量问题分别编号，链接受影响能力、具体实现位置、复现或静态依据、影响及重构时的规避原则。结论标注“已证实”或“待验证假设”。规避原则不代替后续技术设计。
- **调度输入**：说明能力之间的必要依赖、可独立迁移的部分、需保留的真实消费者及高风险交界。可以建议对应新包组，但不得把完整 0.1.0 目标或新增能力混入本阶段。
- **未知与决定项**：列明尚需环境、证据或负责人判断的问题及其影响。合理未知允许保留，但不得用泛泛的“未充分测试”替代已能查清的事实。

报告可拆为多条编号评论。第一条提供摘要与后续评论索引，最终一条注明本次报告范围和未决项。源码证据使用固定提交的永久链接，尽量定位到行；运行证据保留可复现命令及必要摘要，不上传秘密或整段原始日志。

## 交付条件

| 条件ID | 类型 | 目标 | 阶段 | 所需结果与判据 | 确认责任及证据入口 | 适用目标 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| D-01 | capability | 上述固定源快照和本卡评论 | start | 执行会话能读取两个 legacy 目录，并能向本卡提交报告评论；缺外部凭据只限制相关动态验证，不阻塞可独立完成的调查 | 调度者在派发前核对；执行者在报告列环境缺口 | all |

#197 的技术栈设计和 #198 的 Cursor／手册治理均不是本卡开工前置。本卡没有 Git 集成条件，不设置到 main 或集成分支的合并目标。报告交付不代表实现已修复或功能已迁移。后续卡是否依赖本报告，由调度者按具体能力和证据另行登记。

## 实施与持续成果交接

本会话是建卡及调度中心，本次只建卡，不执行调查。后续交给单独调查会话。派发时，调度者先核对当前卡修订及有无活动执行，再登记唯一 attempt、固定输入和实际会话身份。

执行者只读源码，不修改共享工作树、提交代码、推送分支或创建 PR。需探路时使用自己的临时目录和隔离数据，不访问真实租户数据、不改外部系统。需要付费模型调用、破坏性操作或扩大调查范围时，先报告必要性，只停相关部分。根目录及相关目录的 AGENTS 仍按适用范围加载。

指定调查会话可以直接追加本卡报告评论。Issue 正文、Project Stage 及接受决定仍由调度者和具名接受者按各自权限维护。调查会话不得自行关闭本卡或宣告接受。

本次获准成果保存入口就是本卡评论。无需另写长期设计正文；若后续需要将已接受结论提升为长期规范，由调度者另行安排并明确唯一源，不在本卡默默扩大交付。报告接受后作为重构拆卡和非回归核对的输入，不自动授予技术方案采用或实现开工。

### 当前执行摘要

- 状态：调查任务已完成，交付 revision 1 已由 PanQiWei 接受；Project Stage 为 Accepted。没有活动 attempt，不再等待调查派发或接受。
- 人的责任：PanQiWei。其在2026-10-12本会话明确委派 Codex 主会话完成本次接受决定、正文摘要和 Stage 的一次集成更新；其他共享更新仍按原具名单写责任处理。
- 已完成 attempt：`issue-199-r1-codex-20261012-01`。执行身份与授权见[领取回执](https://github.com/nemori-ai/omne-harness-lite/issues/199#issuecomment-6126665246)。
- 固定输入：`02c0fc82dfc254fe598922daabf319b18e39b600`，未更换调查基线。
- 成果：[报告版本1索引及全部八条评论](https://github.com/nemori-ai/omne-harness-lite/issues/199#issuecomment-6127020852)，包含能力清单、非回归、问题与教训、运行证据、调度输入及具体未知。
- 验证：覆盖75个legacy成员，固定快照构建成功，20成员代表测试2407通过、1分层跳过、0失败；本次实跑和静态证据分别标明，未宣称完整产品验收。
- 写范围与保存：只读源码，报告保存于本卡评论，原始调查材料在任务 tmp；没有代码库正式变更、代码提交、推送或 PR。
- 执行分支、Git 集成路线及最后成果 Git 提交：不适用，本任务交付评论报告。
- 平台状态：PanQiWei于2026-10-13要求完成状态收尾，本轮关闭Issue为completed，Project Stage保持Accepted。[收尾记录](https://github.com/nemori-ai/omne-harness-lite/issues/199#issuecomment-6138865715)仅取代此前保留open的处置。

## 决定与剩余责任

PanQiWei 已接受本卡交付 revision 1 的完整调查结果，决定及授权原文见[接受记录](https://github.com/nemori-ai/omne-harness-lite/issues/199#issuecomment-6128983956)。调查完成，Project 4 的 Stage 为 Accepted；按负责人2026-10-13新指示关闭为completed，见[收尾记录](https://github.com/nemori-ai/omne-harness-lite/issues/199#issuecomment-6138865715)。原接受范围和报告结论不变。

报告作为后续重构拆卡与非回归核对的输入。报告中的具体未知、待验证假设和未实现目标已在接受范围中保留；本次不修复缺陷、不迁移功能、不采用新技术方案，也不授予后续实现开工。后续任务及相应决定由 PanQiWei 和相关承诺拥有者安排。
